`cond ? a : b` evaluates to `a` when `cond` is true (QC-19) and to `b` otherwise. The rerelease uses it, including nested (`rerelease-mg1/ai.qc`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_fx.qc`).
`a` and `b` must have the same type; that is the type of the whole expression.
Progs encoding: lowers to an `IFNOT` over the two arms storing into a shared temporary, over vanilla opcodes; no new opcode is used.

`?:` is read at FTEQCC's `TERNARY_PRIORITY`, the assignment priority, which is tighter than `&&` and `||`: without `flag_cpriority`, `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` sets `priority_class[PC_LOGICAND] = 7;`, `priority_class[PC_LOGICOR] = 7;`, `priority_class[PC_TERNARY] = 6;` and `priority_class[PC_STORE] = 6;`, and `QCC_PR_RefExpression` tries `if (priority == TERNARY_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("?"))` on the operand it read at the priority below. The right operand of `=` is read at its own priority and that of `&&` and `||` at the one below theirs, so each reaches the `?` first: `x = a ? b : c` assigns the conditional, and `a && b ? c : d` is `a && (b ? c : d)`, as is `a || b ? c : d` with `||`. A comparison, `a == b ? c : d`, is the condition. Both arms are read at `TOP_PRIORITY` (`val = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` for the middle and `QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA)` for the last), so a conditional in the last arm nests to the right, `a ? b : c ? d : e` is `a ? b : (c ? d : e)`, and the last arm takes `&&` and `=`. This differs from C, where `?:` is looser than `||`; FTEQCC takes the C order only with `flag_cpriority` (`priority_class[PC_TERNARY] = 12;`), which is not its default.
On an expression of type `vector`, `.x`, `.y` and `.z` name its first, second and third float. The rerelease uses `.z` as an lvalue (`rerelease-ctf/hook.qc` `offset.z *= -1`).
A member is a float lvalue when its base is an lvalue, so it may be assigned and used with a compound operator (FTE-6).
Progs encoding: a vector's three floats are consecutive globals (QC-21), so `v.x`, `v.y` and `v.z` are the global at the vector's offset, offset plus one and offset plus two; no new opcode is used.
`const T name = value;` declares a named compile-time constant of type `T`. The rerelease uses it heavily for float and string constants (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`).
A `const` is folded at compile time where it is used; it may initialise another `const` (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `const float LightStyles_MAX = LightStyles.length - 1`).
Assigning to a `const` is an error.
Progs encoding: a `const` that is only folded contributes no global of its own; its value is emitted as an immediate (QC-20) wherever it is used.

`var T name = value;` declares a mutable global of type `T` with an initial value, the opposite of `const`. The rerelease uses `var float` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` `var float num_players = 0;`, `rerelease-rogue/newplats.qc` `var float elvButnDir = 0;`).
It differs from a bare `T name = value;` global by overriding FTEQCC's default that an initialised global is constant, so the name may be assigned to later.
Progs encoding: a global definition (QC-21) with its initial value, writable at runtime; no new opcode is used.
`nosave T name;` declares a global that the engine's save and load of the globals skips. The rerelease uses `nosave float` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` `nosave float load_flag;`).
It is otherwise an ordinary global of type `T` (QC-21). The qualifier affects only savegames, which id's VM spec does not cover, so its only compile-time effect is to be accepted.
Progs encoding: an ordinary global definition (QC-21); the `nosave` flag lives in FTEQCC's extended def flags, which a version 6 progs does not carry, so it is a front-end-only qualifier here.

`T name[N] = { ... };` and `T name[] = { ... };` (size inferred from the initialiser) declare an array of `T`. The rerelease declares string and struct (FTE-14) arrays with an inferred size (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `const string LightStyles[] = {...}`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poseInfo poses[] = { ... }`).
`name[i]` subscripts the array with a float index `i`. The rerelease uses both a loop variable and a field as the index (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poses[i].mdl`, `poses[self.style]`).
`name.length` is the element count as a float constant (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc` `LightStyles.length`, `rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `poses.length` in a `for` bound).

Progs encoding: FTEQCC lays an array out as consecutive globals and compiles a subscript to its array-access helper over vanilla opcodes (it does not use a version 7 feature for the rerelease, FTE-1.1). The exact lowering is fixed by P2-06 and recorded in this section's vectors then.

`typedef struct { T1 f1; T2 f2; ... } Name;` defines an aggregate type `Name` with the named fields, in declaration order. The rerelease defines one (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc` `typedef struct { string mdl; float frame; } poseInfo;`).
`Name v;` declares a value of the type; `v.f` reads field `f`. The rerelease reads struct fields through an array element (`poses[self.style].mdl`, `poses[i].frame`).
A struct initialiser `{ a, b }` gives its fields in order, and an array of structs (FTE-13) is initialised with one such brace group per element.

Progs encoding: a struct value occupies the sum of its fields' sizes in consecutive globals; field access is a fixed offset. No version 7 feature is used for the rerelease (FTE-1.1); the exact layout is fixed by P2-06 and recorded then.

`enum { A, B, C };` declares named float constants starting at 0 and increasing by one, like a sequence of `const float` (FTE-10). The rerelease uses the bare form and the typed forms `enum : int { ... }` and `enum class Name : int { ... }` (`rerelease-mg1/lights.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`, `rerelease-hipnotic/defs.qc`).

An explicit value `A = n` sets the running value; the next unvalued name is `n + 1`. QuakeC floats hold these, so `: int` and `enum class` names resolve to the same float constants; the `: int` and `class` are accepted and otherwise ignored for a version 6 target.
Progs encoding: each name is a folded float constant (FTE-10.4); an `enum` contributes no global of its own.

`enum Name { ... }` also names a type, `Name`, which declares parameters and variables of the enum: `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` reads the name (`name = QCC_PR_ParseName();`) and makes it a type (`enumtype = QCC_PR_NewType(name, basetype->type, true);`). The rerelease declares `enum UpgradeType { ... }` and `float GetUpgradeAmount(UpgradeType Type)` (`rerelease-mg3/defs.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

`#pragma name args` is a compiler directive. The rerelease uses `#pragma warning disable F317` and `#pragma warning enable F317` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`), which turn one FTEQCC warning off and on around a block.

A `#pragma` this compiler does not recognise is accepted and ignored with a warning, so unknown build-time hints do not stop a compile. `#pragma warning` is recognised and adjusts whether the named diagnostic is reported.
`#pragma` produces no tokens and no progs output; it affects only diagnostics and the build.

`rettype name(params)` declares `name` with the function type `rettype(params)`: after the name `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("("))` ... `type = QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType(false, type);`. The type is the one `rettype(params) name` declares, so a C-style definition and a vanilla prototype (`void() InitLightStyles;` in `rerelease-mg3/world.qc`) are the same function (QC-11.5).

A function declarator's body may follow it without `=`: `isinitialised = QCC_PR_CheckToken ("=") || ((type->type == ev_function) && (pr_token[0] == '{' || pr_token[0] == '[' || pr_token[0] == ':'));`. This holds for both orders, `void InitLightStyles() { ... }` and `void(entity e) remove { ... }` (`rerelease-mg1/defs.qc`).

The `;` after a function declaration is optional: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` ends with `if (type->type == ev_function) QCC_PR_CheckTokenComment (";", ...)`, which takes a `;` if there is one. A `;` before a definition is skipped (`while (QCC_PR_CheckToken(";")) ;` at the start of `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`), so `};` after a body is also accepted.

A builtin initialiser is `#number` or `#number:name`, and the number may be 0: `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType` takes any integral immediate (`pr_immediate._float == (int)pr_immediate._float`), then `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":")) QC_strlcpy(fname, QCC_PR_ParseName(), ...)`; the name is the engine's name for the builtin. The rerelease binds its `ex_` extensions this way.

A function's builtin initialiser may also start with `:` in place of `#`, and the engine name may stand in place of the number: a string literal after `#` or `:`, or a name after `:`, is the name, and the number is then 0. `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`), when `if (type->type == ev_function && pr_token_type == tt_punct)`, reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("#") || QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))`, with `int binum = 0;`, then the number of FTE-17.4, `else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_string) QC_strlcpy(fname, pr_immediate_string, sizeof(fname)); else if (pr_token_type == tt_name) QC_strlcpy(fname, pr_token, sizeof(fname));`, and a `:name` after it only `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))`, so `#"a":b` and `:a:b` are errors. A name directly after `#` never reaches it: `QCC_PR_Lex` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reads `#` and a letter as a macro use, and with no such macro reports "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined %s"; this profile reports it as `E0209`. By FTE-17.2's `pr_token[0] == ':'` the `:` form may follow a function declarator with no `=`, and only a function takes it. The pinned FTEQCC, built by `cargo xtask oracles build`, compiles `void(string s, ...) bp = #"ex_bprint";`, `= :ex_bprint3;`, `= :5;`, `= :"ex_bprint4";`, `= :0:ex_bprint5;` and `void(string s, ...) bx :ex_bprint6;` with 0 warnings, and rejects `= #"ex_a":ex_b;`, `= :ex_a:ex_b;`, `= #ex_bprint2;` and `float fx = :ex_bprint7;`. The vanilla profile reads none of these forms (QC-13.3).

The number of a builtin initialiser is FTEQCC's `binum`, which depends on the literal's type (FTEF-3.1): a `float` literal is bound as in QC-13.10, `(int)` of its value once that value is whole and from -2^31 to 2^31 - 1, so `#123456789` is 123456792; an integer literal with the `i` suffix is its `int`, the whole number kept to 32 bits, so `#16777217i` is 16777217 and `#4294967313i` is 17; and a literal with a `u` or `l` suffix is "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`). `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`) reads `if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_float && pr_immediate._float == (int)pr_immediate._float) binum = (int)pr_immediate._float; else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_integer) binum = pr_immediate._int;`, then the string and name of FTE-17.5, `else QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_BADBUILTINIMMEDIATE, "Bad builtin immediate");`; `QCC_PR_LexNumber` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) gives a number with no suffix and no fraction the type `float` (`pr_immediate._float = (float)(num*sign);`), an `i` suffix `type_integer` with `pr_immediate._int = num;`, and a `u` or `l` suffix `type_uint`, `type_int64` or `type_uint64`, which no branch takes. The pinned FTEQCC binds `#16777217i` as 16777217, `#0x1000001i` as 16777217 and `#4294967313i` as 17, and rejects `#16u`, `#16l` and `#16ll`; built for arm64 it binds `#2147483648` as 2147483647, where the x86 result of VM-9.2 is the rule.

`...` may end a list after named parameters: each parameter begins with `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("..."))`, which, with no type after it, sets `ftype->vargs = true` and ends the list. The rerelease declares `void(string s, ...) bprint = #0:ex_bprint;`.

A parameter may have a default value, `type name = value`: `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("=")) paramlist[numparms].defltvalue = QCC_PR_ParseDefaultInitialiser(paramlist[numparms].type);`. The rerelease writes `float(entity e) predicate = (float(entity e))SUB_True` (`rerelease-mg1/subs.qc`).

A parameter's type is read by `QCC_PR_ParseType`, so it may be a type name the program defined, such as the named enum (FTE-15.4) of `float GetUpgradeAmount(UpgradeType Type)` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

FTEQCC's punctuation adds, among others, `->`, `~`, `^`, `<<`, `>>`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `&~=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `(+)` and `(-)`, tried before shorter punctuation as its table says: "longer symbols must be before a shorter partial match". `^` is exclusive or, `<<` and `>>` shift, and each `op=` stores `a op b` back to `a`; `&~=` clears the bits of its right side.
`pr_punctuationremap[]` reads three of them as others: "(+) -> |=", "-> -> ." and "(-) -> &~=". So `a (+) b` is `a |= b`, `a (-) b` is `a &~= b`, and `e->f` is `e.f`.

Without `flag_cpriority` (the default for the rerelease's `-Tid` build), `QCC_PrioritiseOpcodes` gives shifts, `&`, `^` and `|` the priority of `*` and `/` (`priority_class[PC_MULDIV] = 3; ... priority_class[PC_SHIFT] = 3; ... priority_class[PC_BITAND] = 3; priority_class[PC_BITXOR] = 3; priority_class[PC_BITOR] = 3;`), one tighter than `+` and `-` as in vanilla (QC-15.1). The compound assignments are in `PC_STORE`, with `=`: right-associative, at the assignment priority.

A term may start with `-`, `+` or `~`: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken ("-")) { ... e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` and the same for `+`, with `#define UNARY_PRIORITY 1`, so the operand is a term with its postfix forms; `~` takes `QCC_PR_Expression (NOT_PRIORITY, ...)`, the operand of `!` (QC-15.6). `-e` negates, `+e` is `e`, and `~e` is the bitwise not.

A negative number where a binary operator belongs is a subtraction: `QCC_PR_RefExpression` "work[s] around (4-3) being parsed as 4 -3 with no operator between" by reading the token as `+` and the negative number after it, at the priority of `+`. The lexer still reads `-1` after a value as one number (QC-4.1). The rerelease writes `self.count -1` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_sacrifice_triggers.qc`).

`(type) e` is a cast: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `(`, then `newtype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`; if it is a type, `)` and `e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA); e = QCC_EvaluateCast(e, newtype, false);`. A parenthesis that does not open a type is a parenthesised expression, as in vanilla. This profile parses before names are known, so it takes a cast at a `(` followed by a type keyword or `.`; the rerelease casts to no type a program defines.

A `.` followed by a digit starts a number: `QCC_PR_Lex` dispatches `(c == '.'&&pr_file_p[1]!='.'&&pr_file_p[1] >='0' && pr_file_p[1] <= '9')` to `QCC_PR_LexNumber`. The rerelease writes `float DRAW_AI_SINGLE_FRAME = .1;` (`rerelease/defs.qc`).

A number may end in the float suffix `f` or `F`, which is not part of its value: after the fraction `QCC_PR_LexNumber` has `else if (c == 'f' || c == 'F') { pr_immediate_type = type_float; pr_file_p++; break; }`. The rerelease writes `1.0f` (`rerelease/client.qc`).

**Withdrawn** (P2-26, #82): it kept FTEQCC's escapes beyond one byte "Unknown escape char" under the FTEQCC profile, which now also reads the full dialect. Replaced by FTE-20.4 for the one-byte escapes and `dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-13.4 for the rest.

Besides `\n` and `\"`, the escapes that stand for one ASCII byte are `\r`, `\t`, `\a`, `\v`, `\f`, `\#`, `\\`, `\?` and `\'`, as `QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint` maps them (`else if (c == 't') c = '\t'; //tab` and the rest). The rerelease uses `\t` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`). FTEQCC's other escapes are the full dialect's (`dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-13.11).

A statement that starts with a type declares locals with no `local`: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` passes a name for which `QCC_TypeForName(pr_token)` finds a type, or one of the words `float`, `vector`, `string`, `entity`, `var`, `const` and the other type and storage keywords, to `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`, and also a statement starting with `.` ("for local .entity without var/local"). Such a declaration may stand anywhere among the statements. The rerelease writes `float playerFlags = CheckPlayerEXFlags(playerEnt);` mid-body (`rerelease/weapons.qc`) and `poseInfo pose = poses[self.style];` (`rerelease-mg1/misc_corpses.qc`). This profile parses before names are known, so it takes a statement that starts with a name and then another name, `Type name`, for a declaration of a type the program defined; no expression statement starts that way.

A local may be a field or a function variable: FTEQCC's check is commented out, `// QCC_PR_ParseError ("Fields must be global");`. The rerelease declares `void() tutsh;` and `local void() pain_event;` in bodies (`rerelease-mg1/map_specific/mge2m2.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/monsters/boss_final.qc`).

A definition that is not a function may lack its `;`: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reports `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_UNDESIRABLECONVENTION, "Missing semicolon at end of definition");` and goes on. The rerelease's `local float color = bottom + top * 16` has none (`rerelease-ctf/teamplay.qc`). This profile reports `W0203` (QCD-7.18).
A block may be empty: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` reads `while (!QCC_PR_CheckToken("}")) QCC_PR_ParseStatement ();`. The rerelease has `else { }` holding only a comment (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_upgrades.qc`).

A `;` alone is an empty statement: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` takes it with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT, "Hanging ';'");`, unless a macro expansion produced it. A macro written `if (CheckContentsDamage()) return;` and used with a `;` after it makes one (`rerelease-mg1/ai.qc`, `rerelease-mg1/monsters/tarbaby.qc`). This profile reports `W0204` (QCD-7.19) for every one, since the parser does not see expansions.

A parameter or local is a new definition that shadows a global of the same name, whatever its type: when `QCC_PR_GetDef` allocates in a function's scope it skips global definitions, `if ( (def->scope || (scope && allocate)) && def->scope != scope) { ... continue; // in a different function }`. A use in the body finds the function's own definition first. The rerelease names a parameter `light` beside the spawn function `void() light` (`rerelease-mg3/mg3_weapons.qc`, `rerelease-mg3/lights.qc`). A second declaration of a name in the same function is still that definition again, or a type mismatch (QC-11.5).

**Withdrawn** (P2-26, #82): it made a second initialiser that is not a literal always "NAME redeclared", which the full dialect's corpus contradicts. Replaced by FTE-22.5 for literals and `dialect-fteqcc.md` FTEF-17.5 for the rest.

A name initialised twice with the same value is accepted: for a "dupe initialisation" `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` compares the two word by word and reports `"incompatible redeclaration"` only when they differ. The rerelease initialises `float SIGIL_E1 = 1;` in both `rerelease-mg1/defs.qc` and `rerelease-mg1/items_runes.qc`. This profile compares two literal initialisers by value and accepts them when equal, and a differing literal is still "NAME redeclared" (QCD-3.6); other initialisers compare as FTEF-17.10 says.

With `-Fautoproto` every top-level declaration of the program is visible in every function body: `qccmain.c` describes the flag as "Causes compilation to take two passes instead of one. The first pass, only the definitions are read. The second pass actually compiles your code." `rerelease-mg3` needs it (FTE-1.2). Between the passes `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` makes a new table of `#define`s (`Hash_InitTable(&compconstantstable, ...)`), so the second pass defines its macros again.

Frame macros (QC-8) carry from one file to the next: at the start of a file `QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros (true)`, which with `newfile` set only restarts the numbering (`if (!newfile) pr_nummacros = 0; pr_macrovalue = 0;`). A `$frame` name another file defined takes the new value ("old file, override it"); one this file already defined keeps its first (QC-8.7). With `-Fautoproto` the frame macros of the first pass are still defined in the second, so a file may use a frame name a later file defines (`rerelease-mg3/misc_corpses.qc` uses `$CORPSEFRAME_PLAYER_6` from `rerelease-mg3/player.qc`).

Under FTEQCC a `#` opens a builtin only when the byte right after it is `"`, `-`, a digit, `)` or `,`. `QCC_PR_Lex` reads any other as a macro use: `if (c == '#' && !(pr_file_p[1]==')' || pr_file_p[1]==',' || pr_file_p[1]=='\"' || pr_file_p[1]=='-' || (pr_file_p[1]>='0' && pr_file_p[1] <='9'))) //hash and not number`, then `if (!QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()) { ... QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_CONSTANTNOTDEFINED, "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined %s", pr_token); }`. So `= # 5;`, `= # "x";`, `= #'a';`, `= #.5;`, `= #+5;`, `= #(5);`, `= #/**/5;`, `= #\t5;` and `= #;` are errors, which this profile reports as `E0209`, and `= #5;`, `= #-5;` and `= #"x";` are builtins. `:` is plain punctuation, so `= : 5;`, `= :'a';` (97) and `= : "nmr";` (`nmr`) are builtins. The vanilla `#` is plain punctuation too (`pr_punctuation[]` in id's `qcc/pr_lex.c` lists `"#"`), and id's `qcc` binds `= # 5;` as 5, as the vanilla profile does.

An FTEQCC hex number with a fraction is C's `atof` of its text, which reads `0x` as a hexadecimal float: `QCC_PR_LexNumber` keeps the `0x` in `pr_token`, takes only decimal digits after the `.` (`if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') { pr_token[tokenlen++] = c; }`), and sets `pr_immediate._float = (float)atof(pr_token);`. The digits before the `.` are read in full, so `0x10000000000000005.0` is about 1.8e19 and binds no number. So `0x10.0` is 16, `-0x10.0` -16, `0x1.8` 1.5 and `0x1.08` 1.03125; `0x1.a` is `0x1.` (1) and then a name.

A `d` literal is a `double`, and FTEQCC binds no builtin number for it: the initialiser takes only `type_float`, `type_integer` and `type_string` immediates, and `QCC_PR_LexNumber` gives `type_double` to a `d` or `D` after a fraction (`else if (c == 'd' || c == 'D') { pr_immediate_type = type_double;`) and after the digits of base 8 or 10 (`else if (c == 'd' || c == 'D') { //note: conflicts with hex.`). So `= #16d;`, `= #16.0d;`, `= #0d;`, `= #010d;`, `= #0x1.5d;` and `= :16d;` are "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`), and `qc_syntax::builtin_binum` gives them no number. In base 16 `d` and `f` are digits (`c < 'a'+base-10`), so `#0x1d` is 29 and `#0x10f` 271; in base 8 or 10 `f` makes a `float`, so `#16f` and `#16.0f` are 16.

A `-` is part of a number only right before a digit (`QCC_PR_Lex`: `( c=='-' && pr_file_p[1]>='0' && pr_file_p[1] <='9')`), and FTEQCC binds a negative builtin number like any other (FTE-17.4): `#-5` and `:-5i` are -5, `#-0x10` -16. `= #- 5;`, `= #-.5;`, `= :- 5;` and `= :-.5;` read the `-` alone and are "Bad builtin immediate" (`E0209`).

Adjacent string literals are one string (FTEF-16.8): `QCC_PR_LexString` loops, skipping whitespace and comments with `QCC_PR_LexComment(&pr_token_precomment);` before each part, until `else if (first) { ... } else break;`. So `= #"ab" "cd";` binds the engine name `abcd`, `= :"x" "y";` `xy`, and the parts may stand on separate lines or around a comment. An empty string sets no name: `fname` stays empty, so the builtin is named after the definition (`QCC_PR_GenerateBuiltinFunction(def.sym, binum, *fname?fname:def.sym->name)`) with `binum` 0, and `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))` still reads a name after it: `= #"";` is builtin 0 named after the function and `= #"":ex_b;` binds `ex_b`. After a non-empty string a `:name` is an error, as FTE-17.5 says.

An engine name is at most 255 bytes: `QC_strlcpy(fname, ..., sizeof(fname))` into `char fname[256];` keeps the first 255 of a longer string or name. It copies a C string, so a string's name ends at its first NUL byte: `#"ab\x00cd"` binds `ab`, and `#"\x00":ex_b` names nothing before the `:` and binds `ex_b`. Names are bytes, compared with `strcmp`, so two bronze names (`\b`, bytes of 0x80 and above) differ when their bytes do. A name after `:` is `pr_token`, which `QCC_PR_ParseName`'s "name too long" check does not see.

A builtin initialiser makes a builtin function, numbered `binum` and named the engine name or, with none, the definition's name, unless it initialises a definition already initialised and FTEQCC finds one to reuse: `if (basedef && basedef->initialized)` it takes the first function, in the order they were made, with `functions[i].code == -1 && functions[i].builtin == binum` and `!strcmp(functions[i].name, fname)`, or with no `fname` `(!*functions[i].name || !strcmp(functions[i].name, defname))`; `if (!tmp.cast) f = QCC_PR_GenerateBuiltinFunction(def.sym, binum, *fname?fname:def.sym->name);`. The "dupe initialisation" comparison then reports `"incompatible redeclaration"` unless the function is the one the definition has. So a second builtin initialiser is the same value exactly when its number and engine name are those of the first and no function with them was made before the definition's: under this profile it is otherwise `E0206`. `#0:ex_a` then `#0:ex_b`, `#5:ex_a` then `#5:ex_b`, `#5` then `#5:ex_a` and `#0` then `:ex_a` are `E0206`; `:ex_a` then `:"ex_a"`, `#0:ex_a` then `:ex_a`, `#"ex_a"` then `:ex_a`, `#5` then `#5.0`, and, for a definition `f`, `#5` then `#5:f` and `#0` then `:f` are not. After `void() g = #5:ex_a;`, `void() f = #5:ex_a;` given twice is `E0206`, since FTEQCC reuses `g`'s function; a function made for a redeclaration it reuses none for counts as made then. FTEQCC reports the redeclaration only once it has read the initialiser, so a bad literal in it is that error instead; id's `qcc` reports `"%s redeclared"` at the `=`, before it (`PR_ParseDefs`).

A FTEQCC corpus mod (`nuclide`, `freecs`, `freehl`) is accepted under the FTEQCC profile. Every full-dialect construct it contains is covered by a section of this file; the coverage check (`xtask/src/fteqcc_full_coverage.rs`) fails on a class no section names. This statement is what that check pins.

Unlike the rerelease subset, which fits version 6 (`dialect-fteqcc-rerelease.md` FTE-1.1), the full dialect's aggregate and pointer types (FTEF-6, FTEF-9) in general need FTE's version 7 progs format ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-19). Which construct needs version 7 and which lowers to version 6 is a code-generation question, fixed by L-01, not by this parse-and-resolve spec.
Codegen (later): the progs format and opcode set each construct emits are fixed by L-01 and recorded there, against FTEQCC's output. This spec does not state them.

`int` and `integer` both name a 32-bit signed integer type. FTEQCC defines them as `type_integer` (`QCC_PR_NewType("__int32", ev_integer, ...)`), and the two keywords `keyword_int` and `keyword_integer` both resolve to it (`QCC_PR_ParseType`, the C-type branch, `int`/`integer` set `bits = 32`). The corpus declares locals, globals, fields, parameters and return types of this type.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `signed`, `char`, `short` and `long` are types, but their keywords are disabled by default (`nondefaultkeyword` in `compiler_flag[]`), so bare they are "not a type". Replaced by FTEF-2.7 and FTEF-2.8.
**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `double` is a type, but `keyword_double` is disabled by default: the double is `__double`. Replaced by FTEF-2.7 and FTEF-2.8.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said the C words combine in any order C allows, but the loop takes a word only while its test holds (`long int` is 32 bits, `int long` ends at `int`). Replaced by FTEF-2.8 and FTEF-2.9.
**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it said `volatile` is accepted, but `keyword_volatile` is disabled by default. Replaced by FTEF-2.11.
Codegen (later): how each width is stored and which need version 7 is fixed by L-01.

A C type word is matched as `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keywordenabled, string)` matches it: a token that starts with `__` matches its keyword in any case whether or not the keyword is enabled (`if (pr_token[0] == '_' && pr_token[1] == '_') { if (stricmp(string, pr_token+2)) return false; ...`), and a bare word only when its keyword is enabled, case sensitively. By default (`compiler_flag[]`) `int` and `integer` (`typekeyword`) and `unsigned` (`defaultkeyword`) are enabled, `float` and `_Bool` (`QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(true, "_Bool")`) always are, and `double`, `long`, `short`, `char`, `signed`, `register` and `volatile` (`nondefaultkeyword`) are not: `long l;`, `double d;`, `signed x;`, `short s;` and `char c;` are "\"WORD\" is not a type" (`E0203`), and `__long l;`, `__double d;` and `__CHAR c;` are types.

`QCC_PR_ParseType` first looks the word up with `QCC_TypeForName`, which finds the types `QCC_PR_NewType` registers (`float`, `__double`, `__int`, `__int32`, `__uint`, `__uint32`, `__int64`, `__uint64`, `__int8`, `__uint8`, `__int16`, `__uint16`, `__bint`, ...): such a word is the type alone, so in `__int unsigned x;` the name is `unsigned`. Else its loop over C words takes, after an optional leading `register`, each word whose test holds and stops at the first that fails: `signed` and `unsigned` when neither was read; `long` while no width is set, a second making the width `longlongbits` (64); `int` or `integer` while no width is set or it is 16, setting 32 when none is; `short` (16) and `char` (8) while none is set; `_Bool` while none is set and no sign was read, which ends the type as `type_bint` (`__bint`, the `int` keyword being enabled); `float` while no width is set and no `long` was read (32, a float); `double` while no width is set or after `long` (64, or 128 after `long`, a float). A word the loop does not take is the declarator's name, so `int int i;`, `unsigned unsigned u;`, `int float f;` and `__long __long int x;` are errors. With no width set the width is `longbits`, 64, after `long` and 32 otherwise (`flag_ILP32` is set only by `-std=c`); then a float of 64 bits or more is `__double` and else `float`, and an integer of more than 32 bits is `__int64`, of 8 or fewer `__int8`, of 16 or fewer `__int16` and else `__int32`, each unsigned (`__uint64`, `__uint8`, `__uint16`, `__uint32`) after `unsigned`. So `__long int` is `__int32`, `unsigned __long` is `__uint64`, `__short int` is `__int16`, `__register` alone is `__int32` and `unsigned float` is `float`. FTEQCC's `bool` is no keyword: it comes from the engine's extension headers (`fteextensions.qc`), a defined type.

An `unsigned` float is the warning `W0226` "ignoring unsupported unsigned keyword, type will be signed", and a float of more than 64 bits (`__long __double`) "long doubles are not supported, using double", in that order, at the type's first word. The integer branch's "long longs are not supported, using long" is never given: `long long` sets 64 bits, and only more than 64 warns.

In a function body a statement defines locals at a name `QCC_TypeForName` finds or at one of the bare words `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tests with their keyword enabled (`integer`, `unsigned`, `int` and `_Bool` among the C words; FTEF-19.1 lists the others). `STRCMP` compares the bare word, so a `__` C word that names no registered type is a value there: `__long x;` in a body is "Unknown value \"__long\"", and `__int x;` defines a local.

A type may start with `const`, which `QCC_PR_ParseType` reads and ignores with the warning `W0226` "ignoring unsupported const keyword", and then with `volatile`, read and ignored, which by default only `__volatile` spells; a `*` may be followed by `const`, with the same warning (`if (QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_const, "const")) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (WARN_IGNOREDKEYWORD, "ignoring unsupported const keyword");`). A bare `volatile` is a name, so `void(volatile float v) f;` is an error. At file level `__volatile float v;` is a definition; in a body it is a value (FTEF-2.10). How `const` makes a constant is FTE-10.

A number may carry a type suffix: `f`/`F` float, `d`/`D` double, `i`/`I` integer, `u`/`U` unsigned, `l`/`L` long (and `ll`/`LL` long-long), in the combinations `QCC_PR_LexNumber` accepts (length and sign flags in either order). `12i` is an integer literal, `3.5d` a double, `1u` an unsigned.

`0x`/`0X` begins a hexadecimal literal and a leading `0` a base-8 (octal) one; `QCC_PR_LexNumber` reads the digits in that base and `QCC_PR_Lex` dispatches `0x` to it. FTEQCC warns "A leading 0 is interpreted as base-8." on an octal literal.

Without a suffix the type is chosen by the compiler flags: `flag_assume_integer` makes an un-suffixed whole number an integer (widening to `uint`/`int64`/`uint64` as its magnitude needs), otherwise it is a float (`QCC_PR_LexNumber`, the "assume base 10" tail). An un-suffixed number with a `.` is a float, or a double under `flag_assume_double`.
The built-in macro `__NULL__` expands to `0i` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst`), an integer zero used as a null pointer or entity; the corpus uses it.
Codegen (later): how each literal type becomes an immediate is fixed by L-01.

`T *` is the type pointer-to-`T`; one `*` per level, parsed by the `*` loop of `QCC_PR_ParseType` building `QCC_PointerTypeTo`/`QCC_PR_PointerType`. `float *`, `entity *` and `__variant *` all occur. A cast `(T *)expr` reinterprets `expr` as that pointer type.
`&lvalue` is the address of an lvalue, of type pointer-to-its-type (the `&` token in `pr_punctuation[]`). The corpus takes the address of globals and of struct fields.
`ptr->member` dereferences a pointer and selects a member (the `->` token, remapped to `.` in `pr_punctuationremap[]`): `ptr->member` is `(*ptr).member`.

`*ptr` dereferences a pointer to its pointed-to lvalue. FTEQCC's internal dereference operator is `*^` (`QCC_PR_LexPunctuation` notes "fteqcc uses *^ internally"), and `**` is remapped to it under `flag_dblstarexp` for GMQCC compatibility with a warning; in FTEQCC source `*` before a value is the dereference.
Codegen (later): pointers need FTE's version 7 progs ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-19, PROGS-20); the lowering is fixed by L-01.

`T name[N];` declares an array of `N` elements, `N` a constant integer expression. `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType` reads `[N]` with `QCC_PR_IntConstExpr`, and errors "cannot cope with 0-sized arrays" on `N == 0`.
`T name[A][B]...` declares a multidimensional array; `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType` loops over each `[...]` and builds nested array types with `QCC_GenArrayType`. It errors "too many dimensions" past 64.

A sized array may be a struct (FTEF-6) or class member, a local, a global, a parameter (where FTEQCC may demote it to a pointer, FTEF-4) or a field; `QCC_PR_ParseStruct` and the function-type parser both call `QCC_PR_ParseArrayType`.
Codegen (later): array layout and subscript lowering are fixed by L-01 (and for the inferred-size subset, FTE-13.4).

`struct Name { T1 f1; T2 f2; ... };` and the anonymous `struct { ... }` define an aggregate with the named members in declaration order (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` with `structtype == ev_struct`). `struct Name;` with no body is a forward declaration.
`union Name { ... };` is the same with `structtype == ev_union`: every member shares offset 0 and the union's size is its largest member (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct`, the `ev_union` offset branch).

`struct Child : Parent { ... }` inherits: the child begins at the parent's size and adds its own members (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct` reads `:` then the parent name, and sets `newt->size = newt->parentclass->size`). The parent must be a previously defined struct.

A member may itself be an array (FTEF-5), a pointer (FTEF-4), a function type, or a bitfield `T name : bits;` on an integer type (`QCC_PR_ParseStruct`, the `:` bitfield branch, which promotes to 64-bit when `bits > 32` and errors "bitfields must be integer types" otherwise). `v.member` selects a member.
`access.member` on a struct value or through a pointer (FTEF-4.3) reads or writes the member; a brace initialiser `{ a, b }` gives members in order (as FTE-14.3 for the typedef-struct subset).
Codegen (later): struct and union layout, and which need version 7, are fixed by L-01.

`typedef OldType NewName;` defines `NewName` as another name for `OldType`. `QCC_TypeForName` resolves a name to its real type, following an `ev_typedef`'s `aux_type`. The corpus typedefs function types, pointer types and enum/struct types (187 `typedef` occurrences across the three mods).
A typedef name is usable wherever a type is (`QCC_PR_ParseType` resolves it through `QCC_TypeForName`): as a member type, a parameter type, a cast, or the base of a pointer or array.
Codegen (later): a typedef is a front-end alias and emits nothing of its own (its underlying type's codegen applies); confirmed by L-01.

`enumflags { A, B, C };` declares named constants whose unvalued members double rather than increment: FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseEnum(flags=true)`, described in `qccmain.c` as "like enum, but doubles instead of adds 1." So `A, B, C` are 1, 2, 4. The corpus uses it for bit masks.

`enumflags`, like `enum`, takes an explicit value (`A = n`) that sets the running value, and an optional element type (`: int`); the typed and `enum class` forms resolve as FTE-15.2 states. A bare `enum`'s increment-by-one semantics are FTE-15.1.
Codegen (later): each enum name is a folded constant and the enum contributes no global of its own (as FTE-15.3 for the subset); confirmed by L-01.

An `enum` or `enumflags` where a type belongs always has its body: `QCC_PR_ParseType` sends both keywords to `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` (`else if (QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_enum, "enum")) type = QCC_PR_ParseEnum(false);`), which reads an optional `class`, a name or legacy base type and an optional `: type`, then `QCC_PR_Expect("{");` on every path that has not already read the `{` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, `QCC_PR_ParseEnum`). So `enum colour_e c;` and `typedef enum colour_e C;` are "expected {" errors; an enum is named elsewhere by its type name alone (FTE-15.4), `colour_e c;`.

`class Name { ... };` and `class Name : Parent { ... };` define an entity subtype whose members are entity fields, inheriting the parent's fields (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` reads an optional `: Parent`, requires the parent be a class/entity type, and sets `newt->parentclass`). `class Name;` with no body is a forward declaration.

A member function is declared with `virtual`, `nonvirtual` or `static` (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s keyword loop). A `virtual` function becomes an entity field that can be overridden per instance; a `nonvirtual` or `static` function is a global named `Class::member`. FTEQCC warns "`%s::%s` was not qualified. Assuming non-virtual." when a member function has no qualifier. `nonvirtual:` and `virtual:` as a label set the default for the following members (the "fteqcc-specific" `assumevirtual` path).

A non-function member is a field of the entity (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` builds an `ev_field` type per member and unions it into the class's field layout). `self.member` or `this.member` selects it. `const`, `var`, `static`, `ignore`/`strip` and the access labels `public`/`private`/`protected` are accepted qualifiers; access control is not enforced (the labels are read and ignored).

A member function body `Class::member = { ... }` or `= [frame, think] { ... }` defines it. A `nonvirtual`/`static` member has no implicit `this`; a `virtual` or plain member receives `this` as a pointer to the class (`QCC_PR_MakeThiscall` prepends a `this` parameter). A member whose name equals the class name is a constructor; FTEQCC warns if it is not `void`, takes arguments, or is `static`.
For each class with a constructor FTEQCC defines a `spawnfunc_Name` function so maps can spawn it (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass`'s trailing `QCC_PR_GetDef("spawnfunc_%s", ...)`).
Codegen (later): the field layout, vtable and `this`-call lowering, and the version 7 requirement, are fixed by L-01.

`accessor Name : Base { get ...; set ...; };` defines a type `Name` that is stored as `Base` (its parent type) but whose reads and writes go through get and set functions (`QCC_PR_ParseType`'s `accessor` branch builds an `ev_accessor` type whose `parentclass` is `Base` and whose size matches `Base`). `accessor Name : Base;` with no body declares the handle type alone, as `fteextensions.qc` does.

A `get` member defines the read function and a `set` the write (`QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`, keyed by `setnotget`); an optional `[IndexType]` makes it an indexed accessor (`name[i]` calls the getter or setter with the index). `inline` and `&`/`*` on the member select by-reference or by-pointer forms. The functions are named `Name::get_field` and `Name::set_field`.

Inside a `class` (FTEF-9), `get` and `set` members declare accessor members of that class (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` dispatches `isget`/`isset` to `QCC_PR_ParseAccessorMember`). Virtual and static accessors are rejected ("virtual accessors are not supported", "static accessors are not supported").
Codegen (later): an accessor read or write lowers to its getter or setter call; fixed by L-01.

`__variant` is a type that any other type is compatible with: `typecmp_lax` returns "equivalent" whenever either side is `ev_variant` ("variants and args don't make sense, and are considered equivelent(ish)"). It is used for generic parameters and return values, and `__variant *` (FTEF-4) for untyped memory.
An assignment or call that mixes `__variant` with a concrete type resolves without a type error, because of FTEF-11.1; the concrete type governs the operation.
Codegen (later): how a `__variant` value is stored and dispatched is fixed by L-01.

`#pragma TARGET name` chooses the output target (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `TARGET` case, calling `QCC_OPCodeSetTargetName`); it warns "Unknown target ... Ignored." and lists `ID, HEXEN2, FTE, FTEH2, KK7, DP(patched)` for an unknown one. The corpus uses it 28 times.

`#pragma PROGS_DAT path` (and the lowercase `progs_dat`, and `#pragma output`) sets the output file unless the command line named one (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `PROGS_DAT` and `output` cases, calling `QCC_JoinPaths` into `destfile`). `#pragma PROGS_SRC` is accepted and silently ignored. The corpus uses `PROGS_DAT`/`progs_dat` 26 times.

`#pragma sourcefile path` registers an additional source file to compile (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `sourcefile` case, calling `QCC_RegisterSourceFile` for each parsed name). The corpus uses it 9 times.

`#pragma flag name on|off` (the alias `keyword`) enables or disables a compiler flag or keyword mid-compile (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, the `keyword`/`flag` case, over the `compiler_flag[]` table, honouring `FLAG_MIDCOMPILE`); it warns "compiler flag state not recognised", "keyword/flag %s not recognised", or "Cannot enable/disable keyword/flag via a pragma". The corpus uses it 11 times.

`#pragma forcecrc n` forces the progs definitions CRC ([`progs.md`](progs.md) PROGS-5) to `n` (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, both the `#pragma forcecrc` sub-case and the top-level `#forcecrc` directive, setting `ForcedCRC`). The corpus uses it 4 times.

`#pragma noref n` and `#pragma nosave n` set the file-wide defaults for the `noref` and `nosave` qualifiers (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`, setting `defaultnoref` and `defaultnosave`); `nosave` is FTE-12's qualifier applied by default. The corpus uses `noref` 2 times.

FTEQCC recognises further `#pragma` names the corpus does not currently use but which the FTEQCC profile must accept without error (`QCC_PR_Precompiler`'s remaining sub-cases): `optimise`/`optimize`, `opcode`, `autoproto`, `once`, `file`, `line`, `includedir`, `defaultstatic`, `framerate`, `compress`, `copyright`, `wrasm`, `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE`. An unrecognised `#pragma` is accepted with the warning "Unknown pragma '%s'" (as FTE-16.2), not an error.
**Withdrawn** (P2-42, #429): it said a later `#pragma autoproto` reports nothing, but FTEQCC warns for it. Replaced by FTEF-12.10.

`#pragma autoproto` before any definition turns on the autoprototyping of FTE-22.3 for the module, as `-Fautoproto` does, and `#pragma autoproto 0` turns it off: `QCC_PR_Precompiler` sets `autoprototype = *msg?!!atoi(msg):true;` only `if (numpr_globals == RESERVED_OFS)`, and otherwise warns "#pragma autoproto must appear before any definitions". It holds for one module: `QCC_main`, run once per `progs.src`, starts with `parseonly = autoprototyped = autoprototype = false;`. A list-form `progs.src` is read through the preprocessor (`QCC_ContinueCompile` calls `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` before each entry), so a `#pragma autoproto` there, as Copper's `progs.src` has, holds for the whole module. This profile takes a pragma in a compiled file only before the first token of any compiled file. A later one is ignored with the warning `W0108` "#pragma autoproto must appear before any definitions" (`WARN_BADPRAGMA`, on by default) at the directive, once: the check stands inside `if (!autoprototyped)`, so the second autoprototyping pass skips the pragma without a word.

A `#pragma` affects the build and diagnostics, not the token stream; it emits no progs output of its own (as FTE-16.3). Codegen (later): any effect a pragma has on the output (the target format, the CRC, the flags) is realised by L-01.
`::` is one token. `pr_punctuation[]` lists `"::"` before `":"`, as its rule says: "longer symbols must be before a shorter partial match".

A `\` directly before a line break joins the lines: the token is skipped with the break, in `QCC_PR_LexPunctuation`'s `if ((unsigned char)*pr_file_p == (unsigned char)'\\' && pr_file_p[1] == '\r' && pr_file_p[2] == '\n') pr_file_p+=3;` and the same for a lone `\r` or `\n` (`pr_file_p+=2`). The corpus continues declarations this way (`const string g_spray_mat_1 = \`, `shared/environment/Spraylogo.h`).

A `'` opens a character constant when the next byte is `\` (an escape, FTEF-13.13), a byte of 0x80 or more (a UTF-8 sequence, FTEF-13.14), or a byte followed by `'`: `QCC_PR_LexVector` reads `if (*pr_file_p == '\\') {//extended character constant`, the `utf8_check` branch, and `else if (pr_file_p[1] == '\'') {//character constant`. Its value is the character's code, a float unless `flag_assume_integer`. Otherwise the `'` opens a vector, which may stop after two components, the third 0, with FTEQCC's warning "2d vector" (`if (*pr_file_p == '\'' && i == 1)`).

**Withdrawn** (P2-72, #475): it said every code above one byte is written to a string as UTF-8, which only a UTF-8 string does, and that `\{` stops quietly at a byte that is no digit. Replaced by FTEF-13.8 to FTEF-13.11 for strings and FTEF-13.12 for character constants.

This parse-and-resolve profile keeps every number token of FTEF-3 as a float holding its value (an integer rounded to the nearest float), and every character constant as a float holding its code: the literal's FTEQCC type (FTEF-3.1, FTEF-3.3) matters only to type checking and code generation, which are later (L-01).

A vector's components are read by `QCC_PR_LexFloat`, which takes the bytes of a number and then skips one lowercase `f` only: `if (*pr_file_p == 'f') pr_file_p++;` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`, `QCC_PR_LexFloat`). So `'1f 2f 3f'` is the vector `'1 2 3'`, and an `F` after a component is no suffix: it is read as the next component, and the vector is bad (QC-5.2).

A string literal starts at `"`, and at `R"`, `Q"`, `u"`, `U"` and `u8"`: `QCC_PR_Lex` has `if (c == '\"' || ((c == 'R' || c == 'Q' || c == 'u' || c == 'U') && pr_file_p[1] == '\"') || (c == 'u' && pr_file_p[1] == '8' && pr_file_p[2] == '\"')) QCC_PR_LexString ();`. `QCC_PR_LexString` reads parts in a loop, skipping white space and comments before each (`QCC_PR_LexComment`), and takes those prefixes and `L"` too (`(*pr_file_p == 'U' || *pr_file_p == 'u' || *pr_file_p == 'L') && pr_file_p[1] == '\"'`), so `L"..."` is a string only after another part: `"ex_" L"a"` is `ex_a`, and a lone `L"a"` is the name `L` and a string. The prefix belongs to the part's token, and the parts join as FTEF-16.8 says. The vanilla dialect reads each prefix as a name.

A part's prefix sets its `stringtype`: a plain string, with no `-Futf8` (`flag_utf8strings` is off by default), and `R"..."` are 0, "quake output, input is 8bit"; `Q"..."` is 1, "quake output, input is utf-8"; `u8"..."`, `u"..."`, `U"..."` and `L"..."` are 2, "utf-8 output, input is utf-8" (`u`, `U` and `L` with the warning "char32_t/char16_t/wchar_t strings are not supported, treating as u8 prefix (as utf-8)"). A byte of 0x80 or more starts a UTF-8 sequence only in types 1 and 2, read by `utf8_check`: two bytes for 0 (modified UTF-8) or 0x80 to 0x7FF, three for 0x800 to 0xFFFF (surrogates included), four for 0x10000 to 0x10FFFF; any other byte is itself. Type 2 writes each code as UTF-8 (`forceutf8`), in as many bytes as its size needs with no check that it is a Unicode scalar; types 0 and 1 write it as one Quake byte (`forcequake`): a code from 0xE000 to 0xE0FF as its low byte, Quake's glyph, any other as its low byte too (`pr_token[len] = c;`), above 0x7F with the warning "Cannot convert codepoint %#x to quake's charset". So `"\["` is the byte 0x10 and `u8"\["` the three bytes of U+E010, `Q"é"` is 0xE9 and `u8"é"` C3 A9, `"\{256}"` is a NUL and `u8"\xc0\x80"` written as bytes is one NUL. A code of 0x80000000 or more given to `forceutf8` (`\U80000000` or more, in any string, FTEF-13.11) makes FTEQCC loop for ever: `t <<= 5` reaches 0 and `while (c >= t)` never ends; this profile writes it in 7 bytes, and `cargo xtask oracles builtins` counts the pinned FTEQCC, killed after 20 seconds, as differing as this statement says.

A raw string, `R"delim(...)delim"`, takes the bytes up to `(` as its delimiter, at most 62 (`char rawdelim[64]` from index 1, "EOF while parsing raw string delimiter. Expected: R\"delim(string)delim\"" at the end of the file or the 63rd byte, `E0101`), skips a `\` and line break right after the `(` ("generally part of the C preprocessor"), and then keeps every byte as it is, line breaks, backslashes and `"` included, up to the first `)` followed by the delimiter and `"`; the end of the file first is "EOF inside quote".

In a string that is not raw, `\s` and `\b` stand for no character and toggle bronze text for the characters after them (`texttype ^= 0xe080`). A byte read as itself (FTEF-13.8) from a space up gets the high bit (`if (c >= ' ') c |= texttype;`), so a tab stays a tab and a byte of 0x80 or more is unchanged; in types 1 and 2 an ASCII character from a space up becomes the code `0xE080` with it (`cp|0xe080`), a Quake glyph, and a character above ASCII keeps its bytes ("Unable to mask non-ascii chars. Attempting to mask bytes"). So `"\ba"` is 0xE1 and `u8"\ba"` the UTF-8 of U+E0E1. `\.` is `0xe01c | texttype`; the codes of the other escapes take no bronze.

An escape in a string is read by `QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint`: `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\a`, `\v`, `\f` and `\#`, `\"`, `\\`, `\?`, `\'` (FTE-20.4); `\[` and `\]` 0xE010 and 0xE011; `\.`, `\<`, `\-` and `\>` 0xE01C to 0xE01F; `\(`, `\=`, `\)` and `\+` 0xE080 to 0xE083 ("quake specific"); a digit 0xE012 plus the digit under `flag_qcfuncs`, on by default ("yellow numbers"); `\{n}` and `\{xN}` the decimal or hex code up to the `}`, with "Bad character code" at any other byte, the end of the file included; `\u` and `\U` up to four or eight hex digits, then `if (nibbles) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_BADCHARACTERCODE, "Unicode character terminated unexpectedly");`, which the pinned FTEQCC reports as an error; since `while (nibbles --> 0)` leaves `nibbles` at `UINT_MAX` when every digit is read, the only form with no error stops one digit short (`\u041` and a byte that is no hex digit); `\x` one or two hex digits, "Bad character code" with none; a `\` before a line break that break; a `\` before CR the byte after the CR; anything else "Unknown escape char". This profile reports "Bad character code" as `E0103`, the code of "Unknown escape char" (QCD-2.3). The code of `\u` and `\U` is written as UTF-8 in any string ("\u is a utf-8 code regardless of output encoding") and that of `\x` as one byte in any ("an explicit byte regardless of encoding"); any other as FTEF-13.8 says for the string's type.

**Withdrawn** (P2-75, #480): it said this profile takes a character constant's escape with no code of its own as its byte, with no error, and reports no "Bad character code" there. Replaced by FTEF-13.13.

A character constant's escape, `'\c'`, is read as a string's is (FTEF-13.11), errors included: `QCC_PR_LexVector` reads `if (*pr_file_p == '\\') {//extended character constant` and then `pr_immediate._float = QCC_PR_LexEscapedCodepoint();` (`_int` under `flag_assume_integer`), the function a string's escapes go through. The constant's value is the code: `'\n'` is 10, `'\['` 0xE010, `'\.'` 0xE01C and `'\x4'` 4. "Unknown escape char" (`'\s'`, `'\b'` and `'\q'`: only a string reads `\s` and `\b`, as bronze, FTEF-13.10), "Bad character code" (`'\{6z}'`, `'\xg'`) and "Unicode character terminated unexpectedly" (`'\u0041'`; `'\u041'` is 65) are errors, `E0103` as in a string. The end of the file right after the `\` is "EOF inside quote" (`E0101`), and no other error; after a `\` and CR FTEQCC takes the NUL as the byte after the CR (`c = *pr_file_p++;`) and reads on past it, and this profile reports `E0101` there too. Any other byte than `'` after the escape is "Bad character constant" (`if (*pr_file_p != '\'') QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_INVALIDVECTORIMMEDIATE, "Bad character constant");`, `E0104`). FTEQCC stops at its first error; this profile goes on after the escape, and so may also report "Bad character constant" after a bad one.

A character constant at a byte of 0x80 or more is read by `utf8_check` (FTEF-13.8): `int b = utf8_check(pr_file_p, &pr_immediate._int);` then `pr_file_p+=b+1;`. Its value is the sequence's code, a surrogate or the modified UTF-8 NUL included, and the byte after the sequence is skipped unread, as the closing `'` it should be, so `'éx` is 233. A byte that starts no sequence `utf8_check` takes (`*value = 0xFFFD; return 0;`) is the code 0xFFFD and is skipped alone, so a `'` after it opens a vector. Recorded with the pinned FTEQCC (`fteqcc -Tid` on `void() f = :'...';`, reading `f`'s `first_statement`): `'é'` (C3 A9) and `'éx` bind 233, `'\xed\xa0\x80'` 55296, `'\xc0\x80'` 0 and `'\xf0\x90\x80\x80'` 65536; `'\xff;` binds 65533; `'\xff'`, `'\xe9'` and `'\xc1\x81'` are "Bad vector" at the `'` after the byte. The bytes are written here as `\x` escapes.

`#if expr`, `#elif expr`, `#elifdef NAME` and `#elifndef NAME` choose a side as the project graph does (PRJ-5.5): `QCC_PR_Precompiler` evaluates `#if` with `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(PPI_TOPLEVEL);`, and `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf` takes the first `#elif`, `#elifdef` or `#elifndef` that is true, or the `#else`, only while no earlier side was (`if (!hadtrue && !strncmp(pr_file_p, "elif", 4) && level == 1)`). An `#if` inside a skipped side only nests (`if (!strncmp(pr_file_p, "if", 2)) level++;`). The expression is evaluated by the one evaluator the graph uses, so the graph and the preprocessor take the same sides.

**Withdrawn** (P2-81, #492): it said a `//` comment ends a directive, which holds for the directive's text but not for the line `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` skips after it. Replaced by FTEF-14.30 and FTEF-14.24.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a `#warning` or `#error` text is the rest of the line, where `#error`'s stops at a tab too and both start right after the directive's name. Replaced by FTEF-14.38.
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a `#endlist` with no list open is accepted, where FTEQCC reads it as no directive. Replaced by FTEF-14.41.

A macro parameter list whose last parameter is `...` makes the macro variadic: `if (nl == 3 && s[0] == '.' && s[1] == '.' && s[2] == '.') { cnst->varg = true;`. The arguments after the named ones, with the commas between them, replace `__VA_ARGS__` in the body (`if (*pr_file_p == ',' && c->varg && param >= c->numparams) extraparam++;`); a use may give no variadic argument. A use with fewer arguments than named parameters is "macro NAME expects N arguments, found M" (QCD-8.9), as FTEQCC's "Not enough macro parameters" is.

**Withdrawn** (P2-78, #484): it said every macro body reads `#param` as a string and `a ## b` as one token, which only a function-like macro's does, and that a paste is always one token. Replaced by FTEF-14.14 to FTEF-14.16.

When no macro of the name is defined, `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst` expands `__NULL__` to `0i`, `__FILE__` to the file's name as a string, `__LINE__` to the line number and `__LINESTR__` to it as a string, `__FUNC__` and `__func__` to the function's name as a string, `__TIME__` and `__DATE__` to strings, `__RAND__` to a number and `__QCCVER__` to a string. The preprocessor does not know the function a use is in, so this profile expands `__FUNC__` to an empty string; the value is a compile-time string and does not change resolution.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said the build directives produce no token and read only their line, where `#package` ends the text and `#pack` and `#forcecrc` may read into the next line. Replaced by FTEF-14.39.

A use of a function-like macro may give one argument more than its parameters, which is unused: `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` checks the count only at a comma, after counting the argument before it, with `if (param == MAXCONSTANTPARAMS || param > c->numparams) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_TOOMANYPARAMS, "Too many parameters in macro call");`, so the last argument is never counted against the parameters. Two or more extra arguments are "macro NAME expects N arguments, found M" (QCD-8.9). The corpus relies on it (`EVALUATE_FIELD(mins, 0, PLAYER_SIZE)` for a two-parameter macro, `shared/game/Player.qc`).
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a taken side left open is closed at the end of its file, where FTEQCC's count of open sides runs on into the next file. Replaced by FTEF-14.37.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it said a line continuation in an `#if` expression reads as a space and that an expression FTEQCC reports as an error is only false, where FTEQCC stops at the `\` and the preprocessor reports the error. Replaced by FTEF-14.33.

A deliberate divergence: this profile's `#if` reader nests at most 64 levels (`MAX_DEPTH` in `qc-preproc`'s `cond.rs`), each parenthesis, each `!` and each right side of an operator one level deeper (`ParsePrecompilerIf` calls itself for each), and an expression nested deeper is false, as one FTEQCC reports as an error is. FTEQCC's `ParsePrecompilerIf` recurses with no limit; this profile bounds it so that no input can exhaust the stack, as PRJ-5.10 bounds the vanilla reader and QC-27.15 the parser.

A name is a macro use only when the word `QCC_PR_CheckCompConst` reads at it ends with the name: `QCC_PR_Lex` calls it for every name (`if (flag_hashonly || !QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()) QCC_PR_LexName ();`), and it takes the word up to the first NUL, `qcc_iswhite` byte (space, CR, LF, tab, VT) or one of `)(+-*/|&=^~[]"{};:<>,.#` (`for (end = pr_file_p; ; end++)`) and looks that word up (`pHash_Get(&compconstantstable, pr_token)`, then `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst`). So a macro's name, or a built-in constant's (FTEF-14.7), followed directly by any other byte, such as `!`, `?`, `%`, `@`, `$`, `'`, `` ` ``, `\`, a control byte, DEL or a byte of 0x80 or more, is a name: with `#define N 5`, `x = N!=5;` is "Unknown value \"N\"" (`E0301`) and `x = N==5;` is `x = 5==5;`. The byte is the one FTEQCC reads after the name: in a macro's body the body's next byte as stored (QC-9.16), and after an argument the body's byte after the parameter, so `#define A(a) a!=5` used as `A(N)` leaves `N` a name; at the end of an expansion the word ends. FTE-23.10 reads the word after a `#` in the same way, in an expansion as in the source: `#define K #/**/N` then `K` is `5`, as FTEQCC stored the body `#N` (the pinned FTEQCC: "Cannot cast from float to void()" for `void() f = K;`, FTE-23.11). The vanilla preprocessor expands every name that is a macro (QC-9.4).

In a function-like macro's body `a ## b` writes `b`'s text right after `a`'s, with the white space before the `##` dropped (`*bufferlen = whitestart;`), and the result is lexed again with the rest of the expansion: a text that lexes as one token is that token (`x ##_net` with `x` given `health` is the name `health_net`, `#1##6` the builtin 16), and one that lexes as more is the tokens of that text, each against the one before (`J(a, +)` with `#define J(a, b) a ## b` is `a+`, the name and `+`). Either side may be empty, so `##` at the start or end of the body, or beside an empty argument, leaves the other side as it is, and an empty argument after `##` joins nothing to what follows it: `#define P(a, b) a##b` used as `P(#5, )` or `P(, #5)` is `#5`. `##` is two `#` that touch as the body was stored (`if (pr_file_p[1] == '#')`); `# #` is a `#` before a word (FTEF-14.31). An argument beside `##` is copied whole: one after it by `noargexpand`, one before it because `start[0] == '#' && start[1] == '#'`, each with what stands before its `,` or `)`. So the right argument's later tokens touch the joined one (`P(l, bl:)` writes the label `lbl:`), and white space or a comment after the left argument stays between the sides, as `*bufferlen = whitestart` drops only the body's white space: `P(x , y)` is `x y`. A paste whose text opens a comment (`/` and `/`, or `/` and `*`) writes nothing more: the comment runs to the end of the chunk.

**Withdrawn** (P2-80, #491): it said an argument that comes from another expansion's text is written into a `#` string as its tokens touch, one space where they do not, where FTEQCC keeps that text's white space; this profile now keeps it too. Replaced by FTEF-14.31.

An object-like macro's body is included as it was stored (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx(c->value, ...)`), and `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro`, which reads `#` and `##`, runs only for a macro with a parameter list (`if (c->numparams>=0)`). So in an object-like macro `#` and `##` are tokens like any other: `#define P #5:ex_##a` is refused, the pinned FTEQCC reporting it at the `##`.

A macro is not expanded in the chunk of its own expansion (`if (c && (!currentchunk || currentchunk->cnst != c))`, "macros don't expand themselves"), and otherwise is, while fewer than 8 chunks of it are open for an object-like macro (`if (c->inside >= 8)`) or at most 8 for a function-like one (`if (c->inside>8) return false;`). The open chunks are the expansion a token comes from and those that expansion was used in, back to the source: a chunk stays open until its last token is read. So a macro used again through another is expanded again: with `#define A #5 B` and `#define B :A`, `A` is `#5 :#5 :...` eight times over, which the pinned FTEQCC refuses, where QC-9.4's rule leaves `#5 :A`. A built-in constant's value (FTEF-14.7) is a chunk of its own (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx(tok, true, NULL, NULL)`), so it touches neither token beside it. This profile reads FTEQCC macros by this rule and keeps no hide set for them; the vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.4's.

**Withdrawn** (P2-81, #492): it said a comment before a function-like macro's `(` leaves the name as it is, which holds for the source and for an argument's text but not for a macro's stored body, where `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` dropped the comment. Replaced by FTEF-14.29.

**Withdrawn** (P2-83, #494): it said this profile's expansions write at most 2^22 tokens, which it checked before each expansion and counted after it, so one expansion could write far more. Replaced by FTEF-14.28.

In an argument that is not copied whole (FTEF-14.14), `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads each token with `QCC_COM_Parse2` and writes a built-in constant's value in its place (`end = QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst(qcc_token, retbuf, sizeof(retbuf));`, "we should be testing all defines instead of just built-in ones"), in the macro's own chunk: so with `#define K(x) x`, `K(#__LINE__)` is `#` and the line number touching, a builtin, where the line number of a built-in constant read anywhere else is a chunk of its own (FTEF-14.17). Other macros in an argument are expanded only when the expansion is read.

**Withdrawn** (P2-87, #504): it said this profile keeps a file's name whole in `__FILE__`, escaping it, a deliberate divergence while the name was the host's path. The name is now FTEQCC's, written as FTEQCC writes it. Replaced by FTEF-14.32.

A function-like macro's arguments are found in the text after its `(`, which `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads a byte at a time: after the white space and comments that follow the `(` (`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`), a `"` string is passed over (`do { pr_file_p++; } while( (pr_file_p[-1] == '\\' || pr_file_p[0] != '\"') && *pr_file_p && *pr_file_p != '\n' );`), `(` and `)` nest (`plevel`), and a `,` or `)` outside them ends an argument (`paramoffset[param++] = start;`), the white space and comments after a `,` being skipped before the next. Every other byte, a character constant's or a comment's, is part of the argument, so a `,`, `(` or `)` in one ends an argument or nests as any other does: with `#define E(n) :n`, `E(',')` gives `E` the arguments `'` and `'`, and FTEQCC refuses `void() f = E(',');` ("Bad vector"); with `#define M(x) x`, `M(#5 /* ) */)` ends at the `)` in the comment, so its argument `#5 /* ` opens a comment the expansion ends inside, and `M(#5 // )`, a line break and `)` ends at the `)` in the `//` comment; a comment right after the `(` or a `,` is skipped first, so `M(/* ) */ #5)` is `#5`. With `#define S(a) #a`, `:S(e'x)` binds the name `e'x`. The string skip ends only at a `"` with no `\` right before it, a `\\` before it included, so a string whose last byte is a `\` runs on past its `"` to the next `"` or the line's end, and the argument with it: with `#define E(n) n`, `E(:"ex\\")` runs to the end of the file, which FTEQCC reports as "EOF on macro call" (FTEF-14.29), and `E(:"ex\\") ")"` takes `:"ex\\") "` as its argument. A line break, or a `\` before one, is part of an argument like any byte. Reading of the text the use stands in goes on after its `)`, read again from there where a token of the text as first read stood across it. The arguments' text is read as code only where the expansion writes it, so its lexical errors are reported there and nowhere else.

`QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` reads a macro's name with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken`, up to white space, `,`, `;`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `//`, and a parameter list from a `(` right after it as bytes: each parameter runs from after the spaces and tabs that follow the `(` or a `,` to the next `,` or `)`, its trailing spaces and tabs dropped, and the first byte after a `,` and its spaces is passed over before a delimiter is looked for (`if(!*pr_file_p++)`), so `(a,)` reads on past its `)`. A parameter given twice is refused ("duplicate macro paramter name '%s'"), as are a 33rd parameter (`MAXCONSTANTPARAMS` = 32, "May not have more than %i parameters to a macro"), a name of 32 bytes or more (`MAXCONSTANTPARAMLENGTH` = 32, "parameter name is too long"), a `...` that is not last ("varadic argument must be last") and a list the text ends in ("missing ) in macro parameter list"): this profile reports each as "bad parameter list for macro NAME" (`E0115`) and defines nothing. So `#define E(n, n) n` and `#define E(n,n) n` are refused, and `#define E( n ) n` names `n`. `()` is one parameter with no name, so `#define E() #5` takes one argument, and a second (FTEF-14.9). A parameter is its bytes: one that is no word, such as `a b`, is never matched in the body.

`QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` stores a body from after the spaces and tabs that follow the name or the `)` to a line break, the end of the file, or a `//` outside a quote; it drops each `/* */` comment outside a quote ("multi-line c style comments become part of the define itself. this also negates the need for \ at the end of lines. although we don't bother embedding.") and each `\` before a line break (LF, CR or CR LF) with the line break ("read over a newline if necessary"), storing the byte after it whatever it is, and drops the spaces and tabs at the end. Its quote flag flips at every `"`, an escaped one included (`if (*s == '\"') quote=!quote;`), so `#define N :"ex\"_a//"` stores `:"ex\"_a`, whose string the expansion leaves open, and FTEQCC refuses `void() f = N;`. After a `\` and line break, a line whose first byte after spaces and tabs is `#` keeps its line break, and so does the next continued line ("#define hacks however, require that it becomes foo\nbar\nmoo"). `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` then reads to the end of the directive's line, passing over `/* */` comments, strings before any `//`, and each `\` and line break, in a `//` comment too, so after `#define H 1 // c \` the next line is part of the directive and never read. The directive's text is read as code only where an expansion writes it. A function-like macro's name and a `(` that only dropped comments and continuations stand between in a body are apart only by the spaces and tabs around them, so `#define K M /**/ (#5)`, `#define K M/**/ (#5)` and `#define K M \`, a line break and `(#5)` call `M` (FTEF-14.29). `#append NAME ...` (FTEF-14.39) is read the same way and adds a space and its body to the macro's stored body when the parameters are the macro's; with others ("different number of macro arguments in macro append", "arguments differ in macro append") it defines the macro again, with the warning `W0102`.

In a function-like macro's body, and in an argument copied a token at a time (FTEF-14.20), `QCC_COM_Parse2` reads each token after white space and `//` comments: a number (digits and `.`, or `0x` and hex digits and `.`), a word (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits and `_`), or one byte, each kept to its first 1023 bytes (`char qcc_token[1024]`, `if (len >= sizeof(qcc_token)-1) ;`). A parameter is a word that is its name (`!STRCMP(qcc_token, c->params[p])`), so in `#define E(a) #5a` and `#define E(a) #5.a` the `a` is the parameter, and in `#define E(a) #0x5a` it is a hex digit (the builtin 90). A string right after `#` or `##` is read by `QCC_COM_Parse2` too, which writes its text with the escapes `\"`, `\\` and `\n` read and no quotes, and goes on one byte past the closing `"`: so `#define S(a) #"5"` writes `#5`, `#"5"x a` writes `#5` and the argument, the `x` passed over, and `a##"5"` given `#` writes `#5`.

In a variadic macro's body `__VA_COUNT__` is FTEQCC's count of the variadic arguments, `QC_snprintfz(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%i", param-1+extraparam);`: the arguments found less one, and the commas after the named ones. So with `#define V(...) :__VA_COUNT__`, `V()` and `V(a)` are `:0` and `V(a, b)` is `:1`, and with `#define V(a, ...) #5:__VA_COUNT__`, `V(a, b)` is `#5:1`, which FTEQCC refuses ("not a name"); its "__VA_COUNT__ without any variable args" is never reached, since fewer arguments than named parameters are "Not enough macro parameters" first (FTEF-14.5). `__VA_ARGS__` is the variadic argument when one was given (`if (param-1 == c->numparams)`); when none was, after `##` it takes away a `,` written right before it (`if(*bufferlen>0 && (*buffer)[*bufferlen-1] == ',') *bufferlen-=1;`), the white space the `##` drops gone first, so `#define V(a, ...) a,##__VA_ARGS__` and `a , ## __VA_ARGS__` used as `V(#5)` are `#5`, while `a,__VA_ARGS__` keeps the `,`. An empty variadic argument is its text, commas and all: `#define E(...) #5 __VA_ARGS__` used as `E(, )` writes `#5 , `, the declaration `#5` and a `,` before the `;` (FTEF-15.8).

A built-in constant an argument copies as its value (FTEF-14.20) is written in place of the white space and `//` comments `QCC_COM_Parse2` passed over before it too (`end` is written, not `argstart` to `argend`), so with `#define E(n) n`, `E(# __LINE__)` is `#2`, the builtin 2, as `E(#//`, a line break and `__LINE__)` is the builtin 3. The line a built-in constant has is `pr_source_line`, or in a macro's chunk `currentchunk->currentlinenumber`, the line FTEQCC was reading when `QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx` included the chunk (`chunk->currentlinenumber = pr_source_line;`). A use in a file includes its expansion at the line of its `)`, or of its name for an object-like macro, which is also the line of a constant its arguments copy; reading a chunk counts its lines from 1 (`pr_source_line = 1;`), so a use in a chunk includes its expansion at 1 and a line for each line break of the chunk before the use's end, and a constant its arguments copy has the line of the chunk the use is in. So `#define L :__LINESTR__` and `#define M L` used as `M` on line 3 bind the name `1`, and `#define M(x) :__LINESTR__ x` used as `M(`, a line break and `)` from line 2 binds `3`.

A deliberate divergence: FTEF-14.17 lets an expansion grow exponentially (`#define A B B` and `#define B A A` expand to 2^16 names), and one expansion of a body that names its parameter `n` times, given an argument of `m` tokens, writes `n` times `m` (a body of 8000 `x` given 8000 tokens is 64000000), and FTEQCC builds it all. So this profile makes at most `FTE_MAX_EXPANSIONS` = 2^20 macro expansions in one file and writes at most `FTE_MAX_EXPANDED_TOKENS` = 2^22 tokens with them: an expansion's text is written only while it holds no more bytes than the tokens left under the bound, a token being at least one byte, and its tokens are counted when it is lexed. The first use past either bound is reported once, as "macro expansion too large" (`E0120`), and it and later uses are left as written. No program of the corpus comes near it. The vanilla dialect has the same bound (`language.md` QC-9.18).

A function-like macro takes its arguments only from the text of the chunk its name is in: `QCC_PR_CheckCompConst` skips spaces and tabs after the name (`while(*pr_file_p == ' ' || *pr_file_p == '\t')`) and expands it only `if (*pr_file_p == '(')`, so a line break or a comment before the `(`, in the source or in an argument's text copied into an expansion, or the end of the expansion the name is in, leaves the name as it is (`M\n(#5)` is the name `M`; with `#define N M`, `N(#5)` is too), while in a macro's stored body the comments and continuations between a name and its `(` are gone (FTEF-14.24); and `QCC_PR_ExpandPreProcessorMacro` reads the arguments up to the `)` within that text (FTEF-14.22), reporting "EOF on macro call" (`if (!*pr_file_p) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_EOF, "EOF on macro call");`) when it ends first. This profile reports that as "unterminated argument list for macro NAME" (`E0117`): with `#define L(x) x:` and `#define LL L(lbl`, `LL) goto lbl;` is `E0117`, as is the end of the file inside a use's arguments.

**Withdrawn** (P2-94, #507): it said only `#define` and `#append` read on past a `\` and line break in a `//` comment, a known difference for the other directives. Every directive now ends its line where `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it. Replaced by FTEF-14.35.

In a function-like macro's body `#param`, `param` a named parameter, is a string of the argument's text as written, from after the white space and comments that follow its `(` or `,` (`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`) to its `,` or `)`: `QCC_PR_ExpandStrCatMarkup` copies `paramoffset[p]`, white space and comments included, with `\` before each line break, `\`, NUL and `"`. So `#define S(a) #a` used as `S( ex_a )` is `"ex_a "`, `S(ex a)` is `"ex a"`, `S(ex/**/a)` is `"ex/**/a"`, `S(ex\a)` is `"ex\\a"` and `S()` is `""`; every byte is kept, one of 0x80 or more included; the argument's text is a string's, so no lexical error in it is reported unless the body also writes the argument as code. `...` has no name (the loop compares `c->params[p]`), so `#__VA_ARGS__` is a `#` before the word `__VA_ARGS__`. A `#` before a word that is no parameter writes `#` and that word with nothing between (`QCC_PR_ExpandStrCat(..., "#", 1);` then `qcc_token`), so `#define S(a) # 5` is `#5`, a builtin; a `#` at the end of the body writes nothing (`if (!pr_file_p) break;`). An argument that comes from another expansion's text is that text as the expansion wrote it, white space and all.

A built-in constant (FTEF-14.7) is the text `QCC_PR_CheckBuiltinCompConst` writes for it, read as a chunk of its own (FTEF-14.17): `0i` for `__NULL__`, the line (`%i`) for `__LINE__` and in quotes for `__LINESTR__` (FTEF-14.27), `""` for the constants this profile does not know, and for `__FILE__` `QC_snprintfz(retbuf, retbufsize, "\"%s\"", s_filen);` in `char retbuf[256]`, so at most 255 bytes, ended at its first `:` (`erk = strchr(retbuf, ':'); if (erk) { erk[0] = '\"'; erk[1] = 0; }`) with nothing in the name escaped: a `\` in the name starts an escape, a `"` ends the string, a line break is "newline inside quote" (`E0102`) and a name of 254 bytes or more leaves the string open. Its lexical errors are reported at the constant's name. `s_filen` is the name of the file being read: for a compiled file the name it is compiled by (`QCC_PR_CompileFile (char *string, char *filename)`), which the preprocessor takes as its caller gives the path, so a caller gives it as `progs.src` wrote it; for an `#include`d file the bytes between its quotes joined by `QCC_JoinPaths` to the compiled file's name, after its last `/` or `\`, or alone when they start with one (`QCC_FindBestInclude(msg, compilingfile, false);`), so a file another included file includes is named beside the compiled file; and from a `#pragma file(NAME)` or `#pragma file NAME` (any case of `file`) to the end of that file, NAME (`s_filen = e = qccHunkAlloc(strlen(m)+1);`), the pragma's text being bytes to the end of its line, read from after a space or tab or from a `(`, its trailing white space dropped and, from a `(`, ended at the first `)`, and never lexed as code. In a macro's chunk `s_filen` is the file's name, the line and the macro's name joined by `:` (`QC_snprintfz(p, b, "%s:%i:%s", ...)`), which the `:` cut ends at the file's name. So with `progs.src` listing `t.qc`, `void() f = :__FILE__;` binds the name `t.qc`, after `#pragma file(ex_a:b)` `ex_a`, and after `#pragma file(e\\x)` `e\x`; with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, the pinned FTEQCC names them `src/a.qc`, `src/x/b.qh` and `src/c.qh`. The semantic model gives the preprocessor each file's path as its input names it, the `progs.src` entry only where the caller makes it so (P2-95).

An `#if` or `#elif` expression is read as `ParsePrecompilerIf` reads it, not with the C precedence of PRJ-5.5, by the preprocessor and by the graph of a module of this dialect. `||` and `&&` share one level and group to the right, the right side read first: `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(level)||eval;` and `eval = ParsePrecompilerIf(level)&&eval;` under `case PPI_LOGICAL:`, so `0 && 0 || 1` is `0 && (0 || 1)`, 0, where C makes it 1. The comparisons `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `!=` and `==` share the level below in the same way (`eval = eval <= ParsePrecompilerIf(level);` under `case PPI_COMPARISON:`), so `1 < 2 == 1` is `1 < (2 == 1)`, 0. A value (`PPI_VALUE`) is a parenthesised expression, `!` and a value, `defined` and a name with or without parentheses, or a word as `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads it, up to white space, `,`, `;`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `//`, whose macro's text, or else the word itself, is read with `atoi`: `1||0` is one word, 1. The reader starts after `#if`'s name (`pr_file_p = directive+2`) or `#elif`'s, reads within the line, as its white space is all but a line break (`qcc_iswhite(*pr_file_p) && *pr_file_p != '\n'`), and stops after the whole expression; a `\` is a byte like any other, so `#if 0 \`, a line break and `|| 1` is 0, and the line's end is then read as FTEF-14.35 says, which makes the `\` there "unexpected tokens at end of line".
