Where FTEQCC reports an error, "unclosed bracket condition", "unclosed defined condition" or "unexpected end-of-line" (`#if` with nothing after it), the preprocessor reports it (`E0121`) and takes the expression as false; the graph takes it as false.

**Withdrawn** (P2-103, #520): it said the preprocessor reports FTEQCC's "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined NAME" as `E0121` for a `#` that stands first on its line of the output, where the semantic model would drop the line as a directive's. The semantic model now parses the output with no directive lines (QC-9.19). Replaced by FTEF-14.52.

After a directive's operand `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` reads to its line's break, passing over `/* */` comments, which may span lines, strings before any `//`, and each `\` and line break (LF or CR LF), in a `//` comment too, so after `#undef X // c \` or `#ifdef X // c \` the next line is part of the directive, never read as code. For `#define`, `#append`, `#undef`, `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#else`, `#endif`, `#package`, `#pack`, `#forcecrc`, `#merge`, `#includelist`, `#include`, `#output`, an `#elif` that is taken (FTEF-14.37) and `#endlist` (FTEF-14.41) it is called with `errorifnonwhite`, so a byte outside a comment and before any `//` that is no white space, a string's `"` included, is the error "unexpected tokens at end of line" (`E0121`; `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_UNKNOWNPUCTUATION, ...)` reports an error code as an error): `#ifdef X Y`, `#endif X`, `#else X` and `#include "b.qh" X` are refused. A `#pragma`'s line ends at its break (FTEF-14.43). Reading goes on at the break, which ends the line, so the next line may start a directive.

`#undef` reads a name with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` after the spaces and tabs after its name, and removes the macro, a name of no macro reporting only FTEQCC's warning "Precompiler constant %s was not defined", which this profile does not report. `#ifdef` and `#ifndef` read a name in the same way, after a white-space byte that must follow their name; a missing name is no macro's, so `#ifdef` alone is false and `#ifndef` alone true. `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` with a byte that is no white space right after the name (`if (!qcc_iswhite(*pr_file_p))`), as in `#ifdefX`, `#iffy` and `#if(1)`, is FTEQCC's warning "Unknown pragma", which this profile does not report, and opens no block: reading goes on as code after the word `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads from the name, so `#if(1)` leaves `(1)`.

FTEQCC counts the sides that are open and taken in one `static int ifs`, kept from file to file of a module, included files and the second autoprototyping pass included: a true `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` adds one; a false one is skipped by `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf(false, ...)`, which adds one if it stops at a side it takes. That function reads a line at a time: after spaces and tabs a `#` and spaces and tabs before a word starting `endif` closes a level and one starting `if` opens one (`if (!strncmp(pr_file_p, "if", 2)) level++;`); at the block's own level, while no side was taken, a word starting `else` takes the next side, its line read with `errorifnonwhite`, and one starting `elif`, `elifdef` or `elifndef` is tested, which needs a space or a tab after `elif`, `elifdef` or `elifndef` ("malformed #elif", `E0121`), and is taken when true, its line read with `errorifnonwhite` after the test; every line ends where `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it, so a `//` comment ending in `\` hides the next line's `#endif`, and the end of the text is "#if with no endif" (`E0110`) at the conditional. On a taken side `#else` and `#elif` (and `#elsewhere`) take one from the count, read their line (`#else`'s with `errorifnonwhite`) and skip to the block's end with `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf(true, ...)`, which takes no side, so a second `#else` there is skipped too; `#endif` takes one. Either with nothing open is "#else outside of #if" or "unmatched #endif" (`E0109`). A taken side left open at the end of a file is closed by an `#endif` in a file read after it, and is not reported.

`#error` is the error `E0118` "#Error: TEXT" (`QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_HASHERROR, "#Error: %s", msg);`), `#warning` the warning `W0103` "#warning: TEXT" and `#message` reports nothing. TEXT is the bytes from right after the directive's name, a space before the text included, to the first NUL or line break, at most 1023, and for `#error` to a tab too (`pr_file_p[a] != '\t' && pr_file_p[a] != '\n'`), for `#warning` and `#message` to a CR too; the line is then read without `errorifnonwhite`. So `#warning Toggle doesn't work` is "#warning: Toggle doesn't work", and no `'` in it opens a vector.

The build directives change the build, not the text read, but each reads its line as FTEQCC does: `#copyright` and `#message` read it without `errorifnonwhite`; `#forcecrc` reads a number with `QCC_PR_LexInteger`, which takes the byte after the name whatever it is and then digits, `.` and `a` to `f`, so `#forcecrc` at a line's end takes the line break and reads the next line as its own; `#pack id` passes over `id` and one byte more, and `#pack N` reads `N` with `QCC_PR_LexInteger` and one byte more, a number above 5 being "No more than 5 packs are allowed" (`E0121`); `#output` and `#merge` read a string with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetString`; and each then reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`. `#package` reads its line so and then ends the text (`pr_file_p += strlen(pr_file_p);`), as `#eof` ends it (`pr_file_p = NULL;`). `#datafile` reads a string, one byte more, and the bytes to the next line break. `#append NAME text` adds `text` to the body of macro `NAME`, or defines it when it is not defined (`append with no previous define is treated as just a regular define`).

`#include` takes the bytes between `"` and `"`, or `<` and `>`, after the spaces and tabs after its name ("Not a string literal (on a #include)" for another byte, "#include continued over line boundry" for a line break first, each `E0113`), reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`, and `QCC_FindBestInclude(msg, compilingfile, false)` finds the file: the bytes joined with `QCC_JoinPaths` to the name of the file being compiled, then to each include directory in order, the first that names a file being read (`if (FileSize(fullname) == -1) { includepath++; continue; }`), none being "Couldn't open file" (`E0111`). The file being compiled is the one `progs.src` or an `#includelist` lists, never an included one, so a file an included file includes is found beside the compiled file: with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, the pinned FTEQCC reads `src/c.qh` and refuses the program when only `src/x/c.qh` exists. An empty name includes nothing, and a name `#pragma once` marked is not read again (FTEF-14.44). The file is read next, as text of its own, after the directive's line. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.2.

`#includelist` reads its line with `errorifnonwhite`, then words: before each, white space and comments are read as `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` reads them, which runs the directives at the starts of their lines (FTEF-14.45); a word is what `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` reads, a byte it stops at with no word is passed over, and the word `#endlist`, wherever it stands, ends the list, its line read with `errorifnonwhite`. Every other word names a file the graph compiles (PRJ-5.3); the preprocessor produces no token for the list. The end of the text before `#endlist`, reached or made by a directive in the list (`#eof`, `#package`, `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE`), is FTEQCC's "eof in includelist", which the preprocessor reports as `E0406` "#includelist without #endlist" at the `#includelist`. `#endlist` outside a list is no directive (FTEF-14.52).

`QCC_PR_DefineName` refuses a macro name of 64 bytes or more (`if (strlen(name) >= MAXCONSTANTNAMELENGTH || !*name) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NAMETOOLONG, "Compiler constant name length is too long or short");`, `#define MAXCONSTANTNAMELENGTH 64` in `qcc.h`), for `#define` and `#append`: this profile reports it (`E0121`) and defines nothing. A name of 63 bytes is defined. `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` reads the directive's own word first with `QCC_PR_SimpleGetToken` and the name after it, so `#defined N 5` defines `N`, `#defineN 5` defines `5` and `#define/**/N 5` defines `5`, and a refused definition's line is read with no error of its own, as FTEQCC's compile stops at the first.

`#pragma`'s name is the bytes after its spaces and tabs up to the first space, tab or `(` met while the name read so far is empty, and its text the bytes after (from the `(`, or after the space or tab) to the line's break, its white space at the end dropped; a pragma's name is matched in any case (`QC_strcasecmp`). `#pragma line(N)` and `#pragma line N` number the line after the pragma `N`: `pr_source_line = strtoul(m, &m, 0)-1;`, `m` the text after a `(` it starts with, and the pragma's line break adds one. `strtoul` reads a sign, `0x` and hex digits, `0` and octal digits, or decimal digits, nothing being 0, a value too large `ULONG_MAX` and a `-` negating it, on a 64-bit `unsigned long`, and FTEQCC's `int` keeps its low 32 bits: so `#pragma line 0x10` numbers the next line 16, `#pragma line 010` 8, `#pragma line -1` -1 and `#pragma line 4294967297` 1. The lines after it count on from there to the end of the file or chunk the pragma is in, which `__LINE__` and `__LINESTR__` write (FTEF-14.27) outside a macro's expansion (in one, FTEF-14.46), and an `#include`d file's numbering ends with it (`QCC_PR_UnInclude` restores `pr_source_line`). FTEQCC's diagnostics report the line too; this profile's diagnostics keep the place of their text, a deliberate divergence, as a span in the file says more than a line FTEQCC was told.

Of the other pragmas, these change what the preprocessor reads: `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over the rest of the text a byte at a time after white space read as `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)` reads it, so the directives at the starts of its lines still run, an `#error` refusing the program; `once` marks the file being compiled (`strcpy(onced->name, compilingfile);`), not the file it is in, so a header's `#pragma once` keeps nothing from being read twice; `includedir` adds the directory its first token (`QCC_COM_Parse`) names, a `/` after it unless it ends in one, joined to the file being compiled, after the others, at most 8 (`MAXINCLUDEDIRS`); `noref` and `autoproto` take their text with `atoi` (FTEF-12.6, FTEF-12.10), so `#pragma noref(1)` is 0; and `warning STATE NAME ...` sets FTEQCC's setting of each warning named, of which this profile keeps F303's (FTEF-14.46): `enable` and `on` warn, `disable`, `off` and `ignore` ignore, `error` errs, and `toggle` sets `!!` of the setting, a warning for an error. The rest, `COPYRIGHT`, `compress`, `forcecrc`, `framerate`, `file` (FTEF-14.32), `line` (FTEF-14.43), `nosave`, `defaultstatic`, `wrasm`, `optimise` and `optimize`, `sourcefile`, `TARGET`, `PROGS_SRC`, `PROGS_DAT`, `opcode`, `keyword` and `flag`, change the build, and an unknown one is FTEQCC's warning "Unknown pragma", which this profile does not report.

`QCC_PR_LexWhitespace(false)`, which reads the white space and comments after a function-like macro use's `(` and after each `,` of its arguments (FTEF-14.22), and before each word of an `#includelist` and each byte `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over, calls `QCC_PR_NewLine(false)` at each line ending, which runs a directive at the next line's start (FTEF-14.52): so with `#define M(x) x`, `M(`, a line break, `#define Y #5`, a line break and `Y)` defines `Y` and expands to `#5`, and `M(`, a line break, `#ifdef Q`, `zz`, `#endif` and `#5)` is `#5`. The directive's line is no part of the argument, which starts after the white space. A line break in the middle of an argument is part of it (FTEF-14.22), so a directive on the next line is the argument's text, run where the expansion holds it (FTEF-14.46). A directive that ends the text, `#eof` or `#package`, ends the arguments, which is "EOF on macro call" (`E0117`), and the pinned FTEQCC crashes on `#eof` there. A use refused with its arguments read, for "EOF on macro call", too many parameters (`E0116`) or the bound of FTEF-14.28, is an error where FTEQCC's compile stops; this profile then reads the use again as it is written, unless a directive ran among its arguments, when reading goes on after the text the arguments took (after the `)`, or at the end of the text), so that no directive runs twice: with `#define M(x) x`, `M(`, a line break, `#append A 2`, a line break and `1, 2, 3) A` appends to `A` once.

A macro's expansion is read as a chunk of text (FTEF-14.17), and a `#` that starts a line of it, after a line break in it and spaces and tabs, is a directive there, where its text's line breaks are those `QCC_PR_PreProcessor_Define` kept in the body before a continued line starting with `#` (FTEF-14.24) or an argument held; a `#` at the chunk's start is none. Such a body is FTEQCC's warning F303 "preprocessor directive within preprocessor macro NAME" at the first such `#`, once for the definition (`if (!cnst->evil)`), an error by default (`qccwarningaction[WARN_EVILPREPROCESSOR] = WA_ERROR;`, `E0122`), a warning after `#pragma warning enable F303` (`W0109`) and nothing after `#pragma warning disable F303`. With F303 off, `#define D \`, a line break, `#define Y #5 \`, a line break and `Y` makes `D` define `Y` and expand to `#5`. In the chunk a `#pragma file` names, and a `#pragma line` numbers, the rest of that chunk only, and `#eof` and `#package` end it; the pinned FTEQCC crashes on `#eof` in a chunk, where this profile ends the chunk. The chunk's own `__LINE__` and `__LINESTR__` still write the line of its use (`if (currentchunk && currentchunk->cnst) line = currentchunk->currentlinenumber;`), so the lines a `#pragma line` numbers there are those of the uses after it in the chunk, whose expansions write them: with F303 off, `#define L __LINE__`, a `D` whose body is `#pragma line(30)` and `L __LINE__` on lines of their own, and `D __LINE__` on line 6, are `30 6 6`.

Deliberate divergences of this profile's directives: an `#include` met among a use's arguments, in a macro's expansion, in an `#includelist` or in the text `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` passes over is refused, as "#include where this profile does not follow it" (`E0121`), where FTEQCC reads the file as the text it goes on reading there, which ends the arguments or list it is in; an `#eof` run anywhere but at the start of a file, in a chunk too, ends the text it is in, where the pinned FTEQCC crashes, as `QCC_PR_LexComment` and `QCC_PR_LexWhitespace` read on from the null `pr_file_p` it leaves (`cargo xtask oracles builtins` counts those cases as differing as this statement says: an FTEQCC case that holds `#eof` after its first byte, refused by FTEQCC and accepted here with no error); an `#include` of a file already being read is "recursive #include of PATH" (`E0112`), where FTEQCC reads it again until it runs out of memory; a macro name in an `#includelist` is read as a file's name, where FTEQCC expands it (`QCC_PR_CheckCompConst()`), as the graph reads the list (PRJ-5.3); `#merge` and `#datafile` open no file, where FTEQCC refuses a missing one, as the files are the build's; and a directive met while 64 others are being run inside the readings they started, an `#includelist` or `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` inside another, is "directives nested too deeply" (`E0121`) and ends the reading, where FTEQCC's recursion has no bound, so that no input can exhaust the stack.

Before the first file FTEQCC's `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` defines `FTEQCC` and `__FTEQCC__` with empty bodies (`QCC_PR_DefineName("FTEQCC", NULL); QCC_PR_DefineName("__FTEQCC__", NULL);`), so `#ifdef FTEQCC` is true and `#if FTEQCC` 0, and `#undef` removes them. It runs again before the second autoprototyping pass (FTE-22.3), which so starts with those two macros only, no include directory but the module's (FTEF-14.49), no `#pragma once` mark (`QCC_PR_CloseProcessor`), and F303 an error again; the count of open sides (FTEF-14.37) is kept, being `QCC_PR_Precompiler`'s own.

A module's include directories (PRJ-5.2) are FTEQCC's `-I` options: `QCC_PR_CommandLinePrecompilerOptions` gives each to `QCC_PR_AddIncludePath(name)` (`else if ( !strncmp(myargv[i], "-I", 2) )`), which keeps it as `#pragma includedir` does (FTEF-14.44): a `/` after it unless it ends in one, at most 8. `QCC_SetDefaultProperties` calls it after `QCC_PR_CloseProcessor`, so they are the first include directories, before any `#pragma includedir` adds one, and they are there again for the second autoprototyping pass (FTEF-14.48). `QCC_FindBestInclude` tries them after the file being compiled (FTEF-14.40), so with `progs.src` listing `src/a.qc`, which includes `x/b.qh`, which includes `c.qh`, and only `src/x/c.qh` there, `-Isrc/x` reads it, as Rad-Therapy's `client/Makefile` gives `-I../shared` for `shared/defs.h`'s `#include "Weapon.h"`.

FTEF-14.43's `strtoul` is the host C library's, and the pinned FTEQCC reads a `#pragma line` number otherwise where `unsigned long` is 32 bits (LLP64, 64-bit Windows): there a value of 2^32 or more is `ULONG_MAX` = 4294967295, so `#pragma line 4294967297` numbers the next line -1, where an LP64 host (64-bit Linux and macOS) numbers it 1. This profile reads the number as an LP64 build does on every host, a deliberate divergence from the LLP64 build, so that a project reads the same wherever it is opened; the builtin differential records the LP64 outcomes and lists the cases a 32-bit `strtoul` reads otherwise as expected where the oracle ran on an LLP64 host.

Under this profile the syntax tree, which shows a file as written and runs no directive (both sides of a conditional are parsed), makes a directive node of the text the preprocessor reads as one directive (`qc_preproc::fte_directive_end`). It starts at a `#` that `QCC_PR_NewLine` reaches (FTEF-14.52), the file read as one being compiled, so a `#` after spaces and tabs on its first line starts one too, and it ends where the preprocessor reads on after it with nothing run: at the end of its line as `QCC_PR_SkipToEndOfLine` ends it (FTEF-14.35), after the operand the directive reads, a `#define`'s body (FTEF-14.24) or an `#if` expression (FTEF-14.33) among them, and for an `#elif`, `#elifdef` or `#elifndef` after its test, as `QCC_PR_FalsePreProcessorIf` reads one after the side before it was skipped (FTEF-14.37), so `#elif (1/*)` ends at its `)`; at a `#pragma`'s line break (FTEF-14.43); after the word of an `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` with no white space after its name (`#if(1)`, FTEF-14.36); and at an `#eof`'s line break, as FTEQCC reads nothing after it. So `#undef X // c \`, a line break and `float y;` is one node of two lines, and `#pragma p // c \` ends at its line break. A `#` after a `/* */` comment on its line or in the middle of a line, and a `#` whose name matches no directive (`#foo`), are read as code (FTE-23.10). Unless only white space stands between the end and the token before it, the text from the end is lexed again as the preprocessor lexes it where it reads on (`qc_preproc::relex_from`, FTEF-14.22), so `#if"a b"` is a node `#if"a` and the code ` b"`. A lexical error the first lexing found in a node's text, as the unclosed string of `#define X "a`, is reported by neither, as the preprocessor reads that text as bytes. The text an `#if` or `#else` skips, an `#includelist`'s list (FTEF-14.41) and what `#eof`, `#package` and `DONT_COMPILE_THIS_FILE` leave unread are parsed as code. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-9.1's node: a `#` first on its line before a name on that line, to the first line break after it. A rendering of the preprocessor's output has no directive lines in either dialect (QC-9.19).

`QCC_PR_Precompiler` reads a directive at a `#` that `QCC_PR_NewLine` reaches: the first byte after a line ending (LF, or a CR not before a LF, `qcc_islineending`) that the white-space reader passes, a `//` comment's included, and the spaces and tabs after it (`while (*pr_file_p==' ' || *pr_file_p == '\t') pr_file_p++;`), or the start of a file being compiled after its spaces and tabs (`QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_NewLine` first). An `#include`d file is read with `QCC_PR_Precompiler()` at its first byte and no spaces skipped, so ` #define N 5` on its first line is no directive. A `#` after a `/* */` comment on its line, or after one that spans lines, or in the middle of a line, is none. After the `#` every byte up to `' '` but a line break is passed over (`for (directive = pr_file_p+1; *directive; directive++)`, `if (*directive > ' ') break;`, a byte of 0x80 or more too, as FTEQCC's `char` is signed), so `# define` and `#` and a tab or a vertical tab before `define` are directives; a line break first is "Hanging # with no directive" (`E0121`). The name is matched by its first bytes (`if (!strncmp(directive, "define", 6))`), in FTEQCC's order: `define`, `append`, `undef`, `if`, `else` and `elif`, `endif`, `eof`, `error`, `warning`, `message`, `copyright`, `package`, `pack`, `forcecrc`, `merge`, `includelist`, `include`, `datafile`, `output` and `pragma`. So `#defined`, `#iffy`, `#elsewhere`, `#endiff`, `#eofx`, `#errors`, `#includes` and `#pragmas` are those directives. A name that matches none, `#endlist` and `#foo` among them, leaves the `#` to be read as code (FTE-23.10), `#NAME` a macro's use, and FTEQCC's "Explicit precompiler usage when not defined NAME" when `NAME` is no macro, which this profile refuses where the parser reads the `#`, first on its line of the output too (QC-9.19): `E0209` in a builtin initialiser (FTE-23.10), the parser's other errors elsewhere. Each directive's operand is read from its name's end as its own name's length gives it (`pr_file_p = directive+5;` for `undef`), so `#undefine N` undefines `ine`.

In code a `\` directly before a line break joins the lines (FTEF-13.2) with no `QCC_PR_NewLine`: `QCC_PR_LexPunctuation` passes over both (`else if ((unsigned char)*pr_file_p == (unsigned char)'\\' && (pr_file_p[1] == '\r' || pr_file_p[1] == '\n')) pr_file_p+=2;`, and `pr_file_p+=3;` for a CR LF) and calls `QCC_PR_Lex()`, whose white-space reader meets no line ending before the next line's first byte, so a `#` there, after spaces and tabs too, is no directive (FTEF-14.52) but code: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `float g; \`, a line break and `#define N 1`, `#undef N` or `#include "b.qh"` ("Explicit precompiler usage when not defined define", and `undef` or `include`), and with `#define undef 6;` and `#define N`, `float g = \`, a line break, `#undef N` and `#ifdef N` takes the `#ifdef`'s side. A `\` in a `//` comment joins nothing, as the white-space reader ends the comment at its line break and calls `QCC_PR_NewLine`; nor does a `\` that another line ending follows before the `#`, which the white-space reader passes, nor one in a directive's text, after which reading goes on at or after the line break (FTEF-14.35, FTEF-14.43). The rule holds wherever FTEQCC lexes code: a file the preprocessor reads, a macro's expansion, whose text holds a `\` and a line break only from an argument (FTEF-14.22, FTEF-14.24), so with `#define M(x) x`, `void() f = M(#5 \`, a line break, `#define Y 6` and `);` is refused, and the project graph's code (PRJ-5.13); the syntax tree makes no directive node of such a `#` (FTEF-14.51).

A source file is read as the text FTEQCC's `QCC_LoadFile` (`qcc_cmdlib.c`) hands its lexer, by the preprocessor and by the project graph (PRJ-5.13), a compiled file and an `#include`d one alike. `QCC_SanitizeCharSet` decodes a file that starts with the byte order mark of UTF-32LE (`ff fe 00 00`), UTF-32BE (`00 00 fe ff`), UTF-16LE (`ff fe`) or UTF-16BE (`fe ff`), tested in that order, to UTF-8 with `decodeUTF`, skips a UTF-8 one (`mem += 3;`), and leaves any other file as it is. `decodeUTF` reads whole code units only (`chars = inbytes / w;`), joins a high surrogate to a low one after it (`if (inc >= 0xd800u && inc < 0xdc00u && i+1 < chars)`), writes any other surrogate in three bytes as any value of U+0800 to U+FFFF, and makes a value past U+10FFFF U+FFFD (`if (inc > 0x10FFFF) inc = 0xFFFD;`). Then every NUL byte of the text is a space (`else if (!mem[check])`, `mem[check] = ' ';`), so the text goes on past a NUL where QC-1.1 ends it: the pinned FTEQCC refuses `void() f = #5;`, a line break, a NUL and `zz zz zz` ("\"zz\" is not a type"), refuses `#define N #5`, a NUL, `zz`, a line break and `void() f = N;`, and binds `f` to builtin 5 after `#ifdef Q`, a line break, `zz`, a NUL, a line break and `#endif`. A NUL first in a compiled file is a space `QCC_PR_NewLine` passes over, and first in an included file a byte before its `#`, so no directive starts there (FTEF-14.52). After a UTF-8 byte order mark a directive starts a compiled file's first line, after spaces and tabs too, and an included file's first byte; FTEQCC binds `f` to builtin 5 from `#define N #5` and `void() f = N;` after one, with and without two spaces before the `#`, and from `void() f = #5;` written as UTF-16LE after its mark. A diagnostic's place in the file is the bytes its text came from: 3 bytes on after a UTF-8 mark, and in a decoded file the code unit each byte came from (`qc_preproc::SourceFile::file_span`). FTEQCC also warns "file contains null bytes" (`WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT`) once for a file with a NUL, which this profile does not, as the warning changes nothing that is compiled. `QCC_LoadFile` then writes a line break after the text (`mem[len] = '\n';`), which this profile does not add: its readers take the end of the text for the end of its last line, as the directive family's cases of each directive at the end of a file with no line break show. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-1.1: a file's bytes, its text ending at the first NUL.

FTEQCC's `atoi` is the host C library's, and this profile reads it as an LP64 host (64-bit Linux and macOS) does, on every host: `(int)strtol(s, NULL, 10)` (glibc `stdlib/atoi.c`, `return (int) strtol (nptr, (char **) NULL, 10);`; Apple Libc `stdlib/FreeBSD/atoi.c`, `return (int)strtol_l(str, (char **)NULL, 10, __current_locale());`, FTEQCC setting no locale), which passes over the bytes the C locale's `isspace` takes (space, tab, LF, VT, FF and CR), reads a sign and decimal digits, holds a value past a 64-bit `long` at `LONG_MAX` or `LONG_MIN`, and keeps the low 32 bits in the `int`. It is the `atoi` of each FTEQCC reading that names one: an `#if` value (FTEF-14.33), whose `int eval` (`eval = atoi(pr_token);`, `eval = atoi(c->value);`) is compared and negated as an `int`; `#pack`'s number (`QCC_PR_LexInteger`, `return atoi (pr_token);`, FTEF-14.39); the `noref` and `autoproto` pragmas (FTEF-12.6, FTEF-12.10); and `$framevalue` (`pr_macrovalue = atoi(pr_token);`, FTEF-18.16). So, as the pinned FTEQCC reads them on macOS arm64, `#if 4294967296`, `#if -99999999999999999999` and `#define X 4294967296` then `#if X` are false; `#if 4294967297 == 1`, `#if 2147483648 < 0`, `#if -2147483649 > 0` and `#if 99999999999999999999 == -1` are true; `#if` or a `#define X` body of U+00A0, U+3000 or U+0085 before `1` is false, as `strtol` passes over none of their bytes; `#pack 4294967296` is one pack; and `$framevalue 4294967301` numbers the next frame 5, `$framevalue 99999999999` 1215752191. Where `long` is 32 bits (LLP64, 64-bit Windows) `strtol` holds a value past an `int` at `INT_MAX` or `INT_MIN`, so there `#if 4294967296` is true: a deliberate divergence from that build, as FTEF-14.50's, so that a project reads the same wherever it is opened, and the builtin differential lists a case whose directive holds a number the two read otherwise as expected where the oracle ran on an LLP64 host, a project graph case among them (PRJ-5.13). The vanilla dialect's expressions keep PRJ-5.5.

Under this profile the syntax tree reads its directive nodes (FTEF-14.51) in the text `QCC_LoadFile` gives (FTEF-14.54), at the file's own offsets (`qc_preproc::qcc_load_in_place`), so that it makes a node of each directive the preprocessor runs and stays the file's bytes: each NUL byte is read as a space, so the text goes on past it and a directive on a later line is a node, and a directive's start is found in the text after a UTF-8 byte order mark at the file's start, so `#define N 1` on the first line after one is a node, after spaces and tabs too. Only that first mark is skipped: after a second one the `#` starts no line, as FTEQCC reads it. The NUL and the mark stay in the tree as white space, and a value read from a token's text, an engine name's string among them (`ast::Builtin::engine_name`, FTE-17.5), reads a NUL as that space. Text a preprocessor wrote (`qc_syntax::parse_preprocessed`) is no file the loader read and still ends at its first NUL. A file that starts with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte order mark is read by the tree as its bytes to the first NUL, as under the vanilla dialect (QC-1.1): the preprocessor reads its decoded text (FTEF-14.54), whose offsets are not the file's, so how such a file is shown is the semantic model's choice, not the tree's. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-1.1.

A declaration may start with qualifiers, read by the loop at the start of `QCC_PR_ParseDefs`: `extern`, `static`, `shared`, `const`, `var`, `nonstatic`, `noref`, `nosave`, `strip`, `inline`, `wrap` and `weak`, and also, written with a leading `__`, `auto`, `register`, `unused`, `used`, `ignore`, `accumulate` and `deprecated`, which may take a `("reason")`. `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` matches any keyword written with `__` whether or not it is enabled ("lets just always go insensitive with a leading underscore pair"). Then comes a type. At file level a name that is no statement word starts a declaration when a name, a `*` or a parameter list follows it, since a type name is followed by its declarator; a name alone is still "not a type" (FTE-21.1).

A function's return type may be any type: `QCC_PR_ParseType` ends with `if (flag_qcfuncs && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))` after any type, a user type or a pointer included. A function may be initialised with a value as well as a body or a builtin, as `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` does with `tmp = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);`: another function, or `0`.

A parameter (`QCC_PR_ParseFunctionType`) has optional qualifiers `optional`, `__in`, `__out` and `__inout`; a type; an optional `&` ("accept c++ syntax"); then a name, a function pointer `(*name)(params)`, or nothing, since `else if (pr_token_type == tt_name) name = QCC_PR_ParseName ();` takes a name only when there is one; array suffixes; and a default value. A lone unnamed `void` is no parameter (`else if (paramlist[numparms].type->type == ev_void) break; //float(void) has no actual args`). `...` ends the list, after a type or alone, and may be followed by the name of the argument count.

A function type has at most `MAX_PARMS+MAX_EXTRA_PARMS` parameters ("Too many parameters. Sorry. (limit is %i)"), with `#define MAX_EXTRA_PARMS 128` and id's `MAX_PARMS` of 8 (`LIMIT_MAX_PARMS`, QC-27.7): 136 under this profile, not 8.

`wrap`, `weak` and `accumulate` let a function be defined again: a `wrap` definition replaces the one before it and may call it as `prior` (`PIF_WRAP`, "wrapper function does not wrap anything" when there is none), a `weak` one gives way to a later definition, and an `accumulate` one is extended by later ones. `extern` says the body is elsewhere ("function is external, don't error or warn if the body was not found"). A `var` function-typed name is a variable that holds a function, not a function to define: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` makes "functions and fields ... always ... consts even when not initialised", unless `var`.
`T a, *b` declares `b` a pointer, and `struct { ... } a[4], *p;` declares variables of an unnamed struct, as C does; each `*` before a declarator's name is a level of pointer (FTEF-4.1).

A name is "name too long" (`E0202`) from 255 bytes, not id's 63 (QC-3.3): `QCC_PR_ParseName` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reports `if (strlen(pr_token) >= MAX_NAME-1) QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_NAMETOOLONG, "name too long");` with `#define MAX_NAME 256` in `qcc.h`. So a name of 254 bytes is accepted in a declaration, after `#number:`, in an expression and after `::`, and one of 255 is the error; the pinned FTEQCC, built by `cargo xtask oracles build`, gives the same for `float n...;`, `void() f = #5:n...;` and `x = n...;` in a body, at 254 and 255 bytes. The name after a lone `:` is no `QCC_PR_ParseName` (FTE-23.6), so it has no limit. The vanilla dialect keeps QC-3.3.

A declaration's declarators may end with a `,` before its `;`: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`) reads them in `do { ... } while (QCC_PR_CheckToken (","));`, each starting with `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (";"))`, which ends the declaration. So `void() f = #5, ;` and `void() g, f = #5,;` declare `f` the builtin 5, as the pinned FTEQCC compiles them, and so does `#define E(...) #5 __VA_ARGS__` used as `E(, )` (FTEF-14.26); `void() f = #5, , ;` is refused, a `,` being no name. The vanilla parser is unchanged.

A statement declares locals when it starts with a qualifier (FTEF-15.1), a C type word (FTEF-2), a `.`, or a name followed by a name, by `*`s, a name and a `;`, `=`, `,` or `[`, or by a parameter list and a name. FTEQCC decides by `QCC_TypeForName`; no expression statement has these shapes, except a product `a * b` alone, which this profile reads as an expression unless a declarator's end follows.

`(type) e` is a cast to any type: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `(`, then `newtype = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false)`, and, after `)`, `e = QCC_PR_Expression (UNARY_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` or, before `{`, an initialiser of the type. This profile takes a cast where `(` holds a type word, a `.` or a C type word; or a name and `*`s or a function type's parameter list, closed by `)` and followed by a term; or a lone name in parentheses followed by a term. `(visible(head))` and `(sin(x))` stay parenthesised calls.

`[x, y, z]` builds a vector of three expressions, the missing ones 0 ("and to not need the 2nd/3rd parts if you're lazy - [5] or [5,6]"); a fourth is an error, since `QCC_PR_Expect("]")` follows the third.

`Class::member` names a member of a class or its parents, `super::member` one of the parent of the class whose member function it is, and `::name` a name of the global scope (`if (QCC_PR_CheckToken("::")) { assumeclass = NULL;`).
`if not (e)` takes the statement when `e` is false: `int negate = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_not, "not")/*hexenc*/;`.
A call may be followed by a subscript, a member or another call; in vanilla a call ends the term (QC-15.8).
A term may start with `++` or `--` (`QCC_PR_RefTerm`'s `preinc`), `&` (an address, FTEF-4.2) or `*` (a dereference, FTEF-4.4); the operand is a term with its postfix forms.
Adjacent string literals are one string: `QCC_PR_LexString` reads strings in a loop that skips whitespace and comments and ends only where no `"` follows (`else if (first) ... else break;`).
A clause of a `for` header may hold several expressions separated by `,`, and the first clause a declaration after them (`v = 0, int i = 1`).
A call's result may be assigned to, as in the chain `a = f() = b` the corpus writes; FTEQCC reports no error there, so neither does this profile.
An aggregate initialiser may name the member each value initialises, `{ .name = value, ... }`.
A `case` or `default` label may stand in a block nested in the `switch` body, as C allows; the corpus does so (`client/viewmodel.qc`).

A class, struct, union, typedef, enum or accessor names a type, and its name may be used where a value is (`spawn(ncTimer)`, `sizeof(graphNode_t)`). A type's name may be declared again: a class forward and then with its body, a typedef in two headers.

A class's members are found through the class and its parents (`QCC_PR_ParseEntClass` keeps each class's members, with `newt->parentclass`). `Class::member` defines the member the class or a parent declares, or adds one, and its name refers to the member's declaration. In a member function's body a name is the function's own local or parameter, then a member of its class or a parent (`assumeclass`), then a global; a class's own name there is the class, as `spawn(Thing)` takes it, not its constructor.

The name after `.` or `->` is a member of the class of what the access is made on, when that is known from a name's declared type, `this`, a cast or a call's return type; else an entity field the name defines; else a member of any class with the name. A vector's `x`, `y` and `z`, `.length`, and a field of a struct or accessor name no definition, and a name that is a value but no field is not checked; any other name is "Unknown value" (QCD-4.1).

`this`, `super` and, in a `wrap` function, `prior` are no names a program defines, and neither are the intrinsics `QCC_PR_ParseRefValue` declares on demand ("intrinsics, any old function with no args will do"): `nil`, `randomv`, `alloca`, `entnum`, `autocvar`, `used_model`, `used_sound`, `va_arg` and `_`, with `sizeof` and `_length`. `autocvar(name, default)` takes the cvar's name, which is no value, and `sizeof` may take a type word.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-70): it compared a builtin by its number alone, but FTEQCC reuses a builtin function only for the same number and engine name; replaced by FTEF-17.10.

A name initialised again is accepted when the "dupe initialisation" comparison finds the two values equal word by word: this profile compares two literals by value (FTE-22.5), a builtin by its number and engine name as FTE-23.7 says, any other initialiser, a builtin FTEQCC binds no number for among them, by its text, token for token. An enum's names are never redeclared: `QCC_PR_ParseEnum` makes each with `QCC_PR_DummyDef`, which looks for no earlier definition. A function body is never equal to another.

**Withdrawn** (P2-117, #545): it took every type name for one whose meaning the model does not follow, but a typedef's name is the type it names (`QCC_TypeForName`, FTEF-19.9). Replaced by FTEF-17.12.

**Withdrawn** (P2-84, #495): it said a function with no body is an error only where the module refers to it, but the check's `d->unused` is the `noref` mark, so FTEQCC reports every bodyless function that is not both `noref` and unreferenced. Replaced by FTEF-17.11.

A definition marked `noref` or `unused`, by its qualifier or a `#pragma noref 1` before it (FTEF-12.6), may be initialised again with another value: the "dupe initialisation" comparison runs only `if (basedef->initialized && !basedef->unused ...)`. The corpus's `fteextensions.qc` sets `#pragma noref 1` and a later file binds `getgamedirinfo = #0` again.

A function that has a body, given a builtin number again, keeps its body, with the warning `W0206` "incompatible redeclaration. Ignoring replacement of qc function with builtin.": the "dupe initialisation" comparison of `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` has `else if (!def.sym->arraysize && def.cast->type == ev_function && functions[QCC_SRef_DataWord(def, i)->_int].code>-1 && functions[QCC_SRef_DataWord(tmp, i)->_int].code==-1)` before its "incompatible redeclaration" error. As FTEF-17.8, the comparison is not made for a definition marked `noref`. Copper's client module defines `sin` in `maths.qc` and then reads `float(float angle) sin = #60;` in `csdefs.qc`.

A function with no body is an error ("function %s has no body", `E0211` here) unless it is marked `noref`, by its qualifier or a `#pragma noref 1` (FTEF-12.6), and the module does not refer to it: FTEQCC's check (`qccmain.c`) skips a definition only `if (d->unused && !d->used)`, `unused` being the `noref` mark, before `QCC_PR_Warning(ERR_NOFUNC, d->filen, d->s_line, "function %s has no body",d->name);`. So `void() f = #5;` then `void() g;` is an error, as are `void() f = #5, g;` and `#define V(a, ...) a,##__VA_ARGS__` used as `V(#5, g)`, and the pinned FTEQCC refuses each; `noref void() g;` compiles, and a `noref` function that is called is an error. A member function is not checked, and a class's `spawnfunc_Name` (FTEF-9.5), whose body FTEQCC writes when the program does not, is never undefined.

Under this profile a redeclaration is a type mismatch only when neither type, with each typedef's name read as the type it names (`QCC_TypeForName`: `if (t && t->type == ev_typedef) return t->aux_type;`, FTEF-19.9), involves another type name (a class, struct, union, accessor or enum), a pointer or an unknown type, whose meaning the model does not follow; otherwise QC-11.5 holds, with the differences FTEF-19.6 and FTEF-19.7 accept. So `typedef float t; t x; float x;` is no mismatch and `typedef float t; t x; vector x;` is one.

A definition's initialiser may be any expression: past its special cases `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` reads `tmp = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA); tmp = QCC_EvaluateCast(tmp, type, true);`, so `float IT_ALL = IT_AXE | IT_SHOTGUN;` is a global with a folded value. A global's value must still be constant: `QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType` reports "initializer for '%s' is not constant" when `!tmp.sym->constant`. This parse-and-resolve profile parses any expression there and checks only the names in it (FTE-10.2, P2-34); whether it folds is checked with constant folding (P2-06).

A function-typed local may be given a body inside a function body: the `if (pr_scope)` branch of `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal` saves the outer function's locals, calls `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements` for the inner body ("generate a goto statement around the nested function, so that nothing is hurt"), and restores them, so the inner function is a function of its own, `void() g = { ... };` with or without `local`.

A state's frame and next function are expressions: `QCC_PR_ParseState` reads `s1 = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` for the frame, converted to float, and then `def = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` for the next function, which is "Type mismatch" unless it is a function or null. A missing `,` between them is the warning "missing comma in state definition" (`WARN_UNEXPECTEDPUNCT`), not an error.

**Withdrawn** (P2-39, #423): it called a constant range against its direction a warning, but FTEQCC raises it with `QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_STATETYPEMISMATCH, ...)`, and `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints any code `if (type >= ERR_PARSEERRORS)` as an error and counts it in `pr_error_count`. Replaced by FTEF-18.19.

An expression statement may hold several expressions separated by `,`, each evaluated and the last one kept: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` ends with `QCC_PR_DiscardExpression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`, and `QCC_PR_RefExpression` continues `if (!(exprflags&EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA) && priority == TOP_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken (","))`, warning "Statement does not do anything" when the expression before the `,` has no effect. Initialisers, arguments, state parts and `case` values pass `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA`, so a `,` there separates rather than sequences.

**Withdrawn** (P2-42, #429): it gave a function defined inside another labels of its own, but FTEQCC shares one list between them and clears it at the end of either. Replaced by FTEF-18.23 and FTEF-18.24.

`return = e;` sets the value the function returns without returning: "return = foo; sets the value that will be returned when the function finally exits, without returning now. return; returns that value now". A return type larger than a vector is the error "'%s' not supported when returning %s".

`if !(e)` takes the statement when `e` is false, like `if not (e)` (FTEF-16.5): `if (!negate && QCC_PR_CheckToken("!"))` sets `negate = 2`, with the warning "if !() is specific to fteqcc" (`WARN_FTE_SPECIFIC`).

`until (e) s` repeats `s` while `e` is false, and `do s until (e);` is the `do` loop with the test reversed: `wasuntil = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_until, "until"); if (wasuntil || QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_while, "while"))`, and in `do`, `until = QCC_PR_CheckKeyword(keyword_until, "until"); if (!until) QCC_PR_Expect ("while");`. `until` is a keyword only for the Hexen II targets (`nondefaultkeyword` in the keyword table, forced on `if (qcc_targetformat == QCF_HEXEN2 || ...)`), or when written `__until`, which `QCC_PR_CheckKeyword` matches whether or not the keyword is enabled (FTEF-15.1); otherwise `until (e)` is a call of a function named `until`.

A `case` label may give a range, `case a .. b:`, matched when the value is from `a` to `b` inclusive: after the first value `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tries `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(".."))` and reads a second with `QCC_PR_RefExpression (&pr_casesref2[num_cases], TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);`, and for a float the switch tests `OP_GE_F` against `a` and `OP_LE_F` against `b`.

`a ?: b` is `a` when `a` is true and `b` otherwise, `a` evaluated once: after `if (priority == TERNARY_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("?"))` the conditional tries `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(":"))` before reading a middle operand.

`sizeof` takes a type or an expression, with or without parentheses: `QCC_PR_RefTerm` reads `pbool bracket = QCC_PR_CheckToken("("); t = QCC_PR_ParseType(false, true, false);`, and when no type follows, `r = QCC_PR_RefExpression(&refbuf, TOP_PRIORITY, 0); //formulas are accepted weirdly enough, its not just terms.` The value is the size in bytes, an unsigned integer constant; for a string literal it counts the terminating NUL.

A frame macro reference (`$name`, QC-8.5) ends at whitespace or at the first `,`, `;`, `&`, `|`, `(`, `)`, `]` or `..`: `QCC_PR_LexMacroName` copies bytes `while ( (c = *pr_file_p) > ' ' && c != '\n' && c != ',' && c != ';' && c != '&' && c != '|' && c != ')' && c != '(' && c != ']' && !(pr_file_p[0] == '.' && pr_file_p[1] == '.'))`, where id's qcc stops only at whitespace, `,` and `;` (QC-8.6). So `$a||x`, `($b)` and `[$a, th]` name the frames `a` and `b`.

`$framesave` defines frame names exactly as `$frame` does (QC-8.2): `QCC_PR_LexGrab` takes `if (!STRCMP (pr_token, "frame") || !STRCMP (pr_token, "framesave"))` to `QCC_PR_ParseFrame`, which numbers each name on the line from the running frame count.

A function type may return a function: after the type, `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` loops `while(QCC_PR_CheckToken ("("))` over parameter lists ("qc-style function... possibly returning a function."), so `float(float)(string) f;` declares `f` as a function taking a string and returning a `float(float)` function.

Besides `$frame` and `$framesave`, `QCC_PR_LexGrab` knows these `$` commands, each followed by words read as frame macro names are (FTEF-18.13). `$cd`, `$origin`, `$base`, `$flags`, `$scale` and `$skin` are ignored with their words: `while (QCC_PR_LexMacroName ()) ;`, which stops at the end of the line or at the first word that ends at once, where id's qcc drops the rest of the line (QC-27.14). `$flush` numbers the next frame name 0 (`QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros(true)`); `$frame_reset` also forgets every frame macro (`QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros(false)`, "full reset of all frame macros"); `$framevalue N` numbers the next one `N` (`pr_macrovalue = atoi(pr_token);`); `$framerestore NAME` numbers it as the macro `NAME` is, which must exist ("Unknown frame macro"); and `$modelname NAME` first makes the previous model name a frame macro of the current number (`QCC_PR_MacroFrame(pr_framemodelname, pr_macrovalue, true)`), then takes `NAME` as the model name and, when `i = QCC_PR_FindMacro(pr_framemodelname)` is not 0, numbers the next frame `i`, which is -1 for a name with no macro. Under the vanilla profile each of these is a frame macro reference (QC-8.5). Copper's `m_knight.qc` begins with `$flush`.

Frame macros are kept from file to file (FTE-22.4), and the number of the next frame name, `pr_macrovalue`, starts at 0 in each file (`QCC_PR_CompileFile` calls `QCC_PR_ClearGrabMacros (true);`) and goes up by one for each name (`QCC_PR_MacroFrame(pr_token, pr_macrovalue++, false)`), a name already defined in the same file keeping its first number. The limit is on the macros of the whole program, not of one file: with `#define MAX_FRAMES 8192`, `QCC_PR_MacroFrame` reports `if (pr_nummacros >= MAX_FRAMES) QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_TOOMANYFRAMEMACROS, "Too many frame macros defined");`, which this profile reports as `E0504` (QCD-6.4) at the name that reaches it. Under the vanilla profile the limit stays 256 frames in one file (QC-27.5). Arcane Dimensions' `mon_bossmammoth.qc` defines more than 256 frames.

`..` is one token: `pr_punctuation[]` lists `"...", "..", "."`, longest first. So `..T` is a field of a field, which `QCC_PR_ParseType` reads `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken (".."))` as two field levels ("so we don't end up with the user specifying '. .vector blah'"), and a number ends before `..`: `QCC_PR_LexNumber` takes a fraction only `else if (c == '.' && pr_file_p[1]!='.')`, so `1..5` is `1`, `..` and `5`.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-93): it named its form after the withdrawn FTEF-18.4; replaced by FTEF-18.28.

The sequences of FTEF-18.5 are read wherever FTEQCC reads an expression with no `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA` at `TOP_PRIORITY`: a returned value and `return =` (`e = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`), the conditions of `if`, `while`, `until`, `do` and `switch`, a parenthesised expression (`r = QCC_PR_RefExpression(retbuf, TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` before `QCC_PR_Expect (")")`), a subscript (`tmp = QCC_PR_Expression (TOP_PRIORITY, 0);` after `QCC_PR_CheckToken("[")`), the middle of `?:` (`val = QCC_PR_Expression(TOP_PRIORITY, 0);`) and the expression of `sizeof` (FTEF-18.12). The last arm of `?:` passes `EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA`.

A frame macro is looked up by its name and then, when no macro has it, by the name in any case: `QCC_PR_FindMacro` searches `for (i=pr_nummacros-1 ; i>=0 ; i--)` with `STRCMP` and then again with `stricmp`, the second time with the warning `W0104` "Case insensitive frame macro (using %s)" (`WARN_CASEINSENSITIVEFRAMEMACRO`), so the macro defined last of those that match is used. The lookups of a reference, `$framerestore` and `$modelname` (FTEF-18.16) are all `QCC_PR_FindMacro`'s.
**Withdrawn** (P2-94 to P2-99, #507 to #512): it cited the withdrawn FTEF-18.4 for an error code `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints as an error. Replaced by FTEF-18.29, which cites FTEF-18.28.

A statement may be a label, written `name:` (the C style, taken `if (pr_token_type == tt_name && pr_file_p[0] == ':' && pr_file_p[1] != ':')`) or `:name` (the FrikQCC style, `if (QCC_PR_CheckToken(":"))`), and `goto name;` jumps to one (`goto` is a default keyword in the `qccmain.c` keyword table); a label name that is not a name is "invalid label name". FTEQCC keeps one list of labels, `pr_labels`, which the end of every function clears (`if (num_labels) num_labels = 0;` in `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements`), a function defined inside another (FTEF-18.2) included: that one is read by the same `QCC_PR_ParseImmediateStatements` in the middle of the enclosing body, with the note "FIXME: make sure gotos/labels/cases/continues/breaks are not broken by this." So a label read since the end of the last function is the warning `W0312` "Duplicate label NAME" (`QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_DUPLICATELABEL, "Duplicate label %s", pr_token);`) at its name, and is not added again: a label of the enclosing function read before an inner function is a duplicate for a label of that name in the inner one, and is forgotten after it. The preprocessed text this profile parses keeps a name and the `:` after it together when the source does, so the C style is found there too.

At the end of each function, a function defined inside another included, every `goto` read since the last function's end must name a label read since then (FTEF-18.23): `for (i = 0; i < num_gotos; i++) { for (j = 0; j < num_labels; j++) if (!strcmp(pr_gotos[i].name, pr_labels[j].name))`, and otherwise `QCC_PR_ParseError(ERR_NOLABEL, "Goto statement with no matching label \"%s\"", pr_gotos[i].name);`, after which `num_gotos = 0;`. This profile reports each such `goto` as `E0308` at its label name, where FTEQCC stops at the first. A label later in the same function is found and one of another function is not. A function defined inside another checks, and clears, the enclosing function's `goto`s read before it, against the enclosing function's labels read before it and its own: a label after the inner function does not help them, and a `goto` after it does not find a label before it.

FTEQCC's flag `qcc_usefulstatement` says whether the expression being read does something: a call sets it (`if (priority == FUNC_PRIORITY && QCC_PR_CheckToken ("(") ) { qcc_usefulstatement=true;`, before the arguments are read), and so do an assignment of any of the operators of FTE-6 and FTEF-16, once its right side is read, a prefix `++` or `--` (`QCC_PR_RefTerm`), and a postfix `++` or `--` still pending when the expression is discarded (`QCC_PR_DiscardRef`), that is, the expression itself, in parentheses or as the last of a sequence. A discarded expression with none of these is the warning `W0313` "Statement does not do anything" (`WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT`, on by default) at that expression: - an expression statement, and the first and last clauses of a `for`: `QCC_PR_DiscardExpression` saves the flag, clears it, reads the expression, and warns `if (ref->cast->type != ev_void && !qcc_usefulstatement)`, then restores the flag. The first clause's expressions, separated by `,`, are each discarded so (`QCC_PR_DiscardExpression(TOP_PRIORITY, EXPR_DISALLOW_COMMA);` in a `do ... while(QCC_PR_CheckToken(","))` loop); the last clause is one sequence. This profile takes an expression as `void` only when it is a cast to `void` (`QCC_TryEvaluateCast`: "anything can be cast to void, but only do it explicitly."), or one in parentheses; - each expression before the `,` of a sequence (FTEF-18.5, FTEF-18.20), wherever the sequence is: `QCC_PR_DiscardRef(lhsr); if (!qcc_usefulstatement) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_POINTLESSSTATEMENT, "Statement does not do anything"); qcc_usefulstatement = false;`, with no exception for `void`. Outside an expression statement and a discarded `for` clause the flag then carries what came before, a call in an earlier condition included, since only the discarding and the `,` clear it; this profile keeps the flag over one file.

Under this profile the nesting limit of QC-27.15 counts the FTEQCC constructs too: the operand of a prefix `-`, `+`, `~`, `++`, `--`, `&` or `*` (FTE-19.4, FTEF-16.7), of a cast (FTEF-16.2) and of `sizeof` (FTEF-18.12) is one level inside it, as the operand of `!` is, each `*` and each parameter list of a type (FTEF-4.1, FTEF-18.15) nests the type one level deeper, and so does each `*` before a declarator's name (FTEF-15.6). QC-27.16 then holds as for vanilla: a prefix `++` or `--` it unwinds through is read as no postfix one, and a type or a declarator takes no further `*` or parameter list. FTEQCC has no such limit.

This profile's error recovery (QCD-1.4) treats the full dialect's bodies as a function body: a struct's fields, a class's members and an accessor's members end at a declaration line, a token at column 0 that has a declaration's shape or is one of `typedef`, `class`, `accessor`, `enum`, `enumflags`, `struct` and `union`, as well as at their `}`; and a class member's recovery stops at the `}` that closes the class. So a body that lost its `}` damages no declaration after the next. FTEQCC reads each body to its `}`; a field or member written at column 0 in the shape of a declaration therefore ends its body here, as a statement at column 0 ends a function body, and none of the codebases the corpus job resolves under this profile writes one.

A frame cycle, `[++ first .. last]` or `[-- first .. last]` (`if ((isinc=QCC_PR_CheckToken("++")) || QCC_PR_CheckToken("--"))`), has `first` and `last` as expressions separated by `QCC_PR_Expect("..")`; `(w)` or `(W)` after the `++` or `--` cycles `weaponframe` instead of `frame` (`OP_CWSTATE`). Two constant frames against the direction, `if (first->_float > last->_float)` after `++` or `<` after `--`, are the error `E0212` "Forwards State Cycle with backwards range": FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseWarning` with `ERR_STATETYPEMISMATCH`, an error code, prints an error. This profile compares two frames written as single numbers.

FTEQCC tells the readings of source apart by `s_filen`, a string it makes anew (`qccHunkAlloc`) for each compiled file (`QCC_PR_CompileFile`), each `#include` of a file, and each macro expansion (`QCC_PR_IncludeChunkEx`, given a `CompilerConstant_t`), and it compares the pointers, so each of these is a reading of its own; the file that includes another is the same reading again after the include. A frame macro keeps the reading that defined it (`pr_framemacro[].file`), and: - a use of a frame macro that another reading defined is the warning `W0105` "Stale macro used (NAME, defined in FILE)" (`WARN_STALEMACRO`, on by default), where FILE is the defining file's path: `QCC_PR_FindMacro` checks `if (pr_framemacro[i].file != s_filen)` after each of its two lookups (FTEF-18.21), for a reference, `$framerestore` and `$modelname` alike; - a frame name the same reading already defined keeps its first number with the warning `W0106` "Duplicate macro defined (NAME). Rename it." (`WARN_DUPLICATEMACRO`): in `QCC_PR_MacroFrame`, `if (pr_framemacro[i].file == s_filen && !force)`; a name another reading defined takes the new number and this reading silently ("old file, override it"), and so does the model name `$modelname` defines, with `force` set (FTEF-18.16). This is what "the same file" of FTEF-18.17 and FTE-22.4 means; - a new frame name of 64 bytes or more is the error `E0119` "Name for frame macro NAME is too long" and is not defined: `if (strlen(name)+1 > sizeof(pr_framemacro[0].name)) QCC_PR_ParseWarning(ERR_TOOMANYFRAMEMACROS, ...)`, with `char name[64];`, an error code, which `QCC_PR_PrintWarning` prints as an error (FTEF-18.28). The frame number still goes up by one for it; - a `$modelname` of 64 bytes or more is cut to its first 63 with the warning `W0107` "$modelname name too long": `if (!QC_strlcpy(pr_framemodelname, pr_token, sizeof(pr_framemodelname))) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (WARN_STRINGTOOLONG, ...)`, with `char pr_framemodelname[64];`.

A frame macro whose number is below 0 is unknown where it is expanded: a reference and `$framerestore` take their number from `QCC_PR_ExpandMacro`, which refuses any negative one as it refuses a name with no macro, `QCC_PR_FindMacro`'s `-1`: `int i = QCC_PR_FindMacro(pr_token); if (i < 0) QCC_PR_ParseError (ERR_BADFRAMEMACRO, "Unknown frame macro $%s", pr_token);`. So `$framevalue -5`, `$frame a` and `x = $a;` is the error `E0106` "Unknown frame macro $a" at `$a` (QCD-2.6), as is a `$framevalue` whose `atoi` is negative (FTEF-14.55): `-99999999999` is -1215752191 and `2147483648` is -2147483648 on an LP64 host. The lookup's warnings (FTEF-18.21, FTEF-18.29) come first, as `QCC_PR_FindMacro` gives them. A refused `$framerestore` leaves the number of the next frame name as it was. `$modelname` calls `QCC_PR_FindMacro` itself (FTEF-18.16), so a negative model name macro still numbers the next frame. Under the vanilla profile frames are numbered from 0 (QC-8.5) and none is negative. The cases are in the directive family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`FRAME_VALUES` in `xtask/src/oracles/builtins/directives.rs`).

Parameters and locals are found in their function first (`QCC_PR_GetDef` scans `localstable` when `scope` is set). A parameter given twice, or named as a component of an earlier vector parameter, is the error `E0215` "Duplicate definition of NAME.": the parameters are made with `QCC_PR_GetSRef (type->params[u].type, pr_parm_names[u], pr_scope, 2, 0, 0)`, and `if (allocate == 2) QCC_PR_ParseErrorPrintDef (ERR_TYPEMISMATCHREDEC, def, "Duplicate definition of %s%s%s.", ...)`. A vector parameter after a parameter named as its component is no error: `QCC_PR_DummyDef` makes the components with no lookup. A local declared again with its type is the warning `W0207` "NAME duplicate definition ignored", or "nonstatic redeclaration of NAME ignored" after a `static` one, and the same definition; a `static` local declared again is neither; another type is `E0205`. A new parameter or local named as a global of the same kind of type (`def->type->type == type->type`) is the warning `W0208` "Local \"NAME\" hides global with same name and type"; a global of another kind gives none. A parameter of a function with a body that has no name is the warning `W0222` "Parameter N of NAME is not named", N counted from 1; a lone `void` is no parameter (FTEF-15.3). In a function body a statement defines locals when it starts with `local`, a type, a type name, `.`, or one of the words `QCC_PR_ParseStatement` tests with their keyword enabled: `var`, `noref`, `static`, `extern`, `const`, `typedef`, `class`, `struct`, `union` and `enum` (`register`, `volatile` and `auto` are disabled keywords, `nondefaultkeyword`); `shared`, `nosave`, `inline` and the `__` words start no definition there, so `shared float x;` is "Unknown value \"shared\"".

A value initialiser, a parameter's default value and a function initialised with a value are cast to the definition's type by `QCC_EvaluateCast(tmp, type, true)`, which refuses with the error `E0213` "Cannot cast from A to B", A and B as `TypeName` writes them (`__int32`, `__double`, `.float`, `void()`, `entity*`; parameter names, which the model does not keep, are left out). A literal's type is `QCC_PR_LexNumber`'s (FTEF-3.1; a character constant is a float); a name's is its definition's, and in a member function a field's name is `this.field`, of the field's type. The C type words name the type FTEF-2.8 makes, and a registered type name its type (`__int32`, `__double`); an 8- or 16-bit integer and `__bint` are types this profile does not follow. `QCC_TryEvaluateCast` with `implicit` set casts: a type to itself; a null, an integer, unsigned or float constant whose word is 0 (`QCC_SRef_IsNull`), to any type but a struct or union; numbers among the float, integer, unsigned, 64-bit and double types; a float or an integer to a vector, with the warning `W0220` "Implicit cast from A to B"; pointers, strings, integers, unsigned and functions among themselves, and an integer to an entity and back, the casts "acceptable but probably an error", with `W0220` but between the two integer types. Nothing else casts: `float x = "a";`, `entity e = 1;`, `void() g = 5;`, `string s = 5l;`, `vector v = 5u;` and `entity e = 0d;` are `E0213`, and `entity e = 0;`, `string s = -0;` and `void() g = 0;` cast. A string initialised with `_(...)` takes one string literal, else the error `E0232` "_() intrinsic accepts only a string immediate". An initialiser that is no literal and no name is not typed by this profile (FTEF-19.17).

A definition is a constant when its first declaration makes it one, `GDF_CONST`: `const`, or at file level and not `var`, initialised, a function or a field (`if (isconstant || (!isvar && !pr_scope && ((isinitialised && !flag_assumevar) || type->type == ev_function || type->type == ev_field)))`); an enum's value and a `const` local are constants, a `static` local and an `autocvar_` are not. A later declaration does not change it (`// def->constant = isconst;` is commented out) and warns `W0212` "Redeclaration of NAME would change to const." (or "non-const.") when initialised, "Redeclaration of NAME changes const." when not; a new definition is compared with the constness it gets, which differs only for an initialised `autocvar_` (FTEF-19.16), so `float autocvar_x = 1;` gives the warning too. A name initialising a global or a `static` that is no constant is the error `E0214` "initializer for 'NAME' is not constant" (`QCC_PR_GenerateInitializerType`, `if (!tmp.sym->constant)`); a plain or `const` local's initialiser is not checked. A constant that has no value yet gives the warning `W0219` "initializer for NAME is not initialised yet, NAME will be treated as 0", and the value 0; a field always has its value (fields are "initialised behind the scenes") and a function not yet defined is filled in once it is (`$relocf`), so neither warns.

A body given to a definition already initialised, by a builtin, a body, `extern` or `shared`, is the error `E0216` "redeclaration of function body" (`else if (basedef->initialized == 1 && !(flags & PIF_STRONGER))`), reported before the "incompatible redeclaration" the two different functions then give (`E0206`); a body after a `weak` one, or for an `accumulate` function, is none, and a body after a `wrap` one is. A body replacing the builtin of `anglemod` or `crossproduct` is the warning `W0217` "NAME already declared as a builtin" instead, and the builtin is marked unused. A `wrap` body with nothing initialised to wrap is the error `E0222` "wrapper function does not wrap anything", and one that does not use `prior` the error `E0223` "Wrapper function \"NAME\" does not refer to its prior function". An `accumulate` declaration of a function initialised before without it is the warning `W0218` "NAME redeclared to accumulate after initial declaration".

The "dupe initialisation" comparison of FTE-22.5 and FTEF-17.10 compares the words the two initialisers give: a number literal's value as FTEQCC's lexer reads it, so `0x10` and `16` are equal; a constant's name, the constant's value (`float y = 2; float x = y; float x = 2;` compiles); a vector's components, which `QCC_PR_DummyDef` gives the vector's initialised state and words (`d->initialized = def->initialized;`), so `vector v = '1 2 3'; float v_x = 1;` compiles and `float v_x = 2;` is `E0206`; and a `const` or `static` local's, as a global's. `parseentitydata` given another builtin after `#608` or `#613` is accepted with the warning `W0223` "incompatible redeclaration. Please validate builtin numbers. parseentitydata is #613" ("dpextensions is WRONG").

A default value must be a constant (`if (!ref.sym->constant) QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "Default value not a constant\n");`, `E0217`) with a value (`QCC_PR_ParseError(0, "Default value not initialized yet\n");`, `E0218`, but with autoprototyping), cast to the parameter's type (FTEF-19.2). Two function types are the same only if, where both give a default value, the values are equal (`typecmp`, `(a->type == ev_function && (a->params[i].defltvalue.cast && b->params[i].defltvalue.cast))`), so `void(float a = 1) g;` and `void(float a = 2) g = #6;` are `E0205`; a value given on one only is no difference. A parameter with a default value is not `optional`.

At file level a redeclaration whose type differs (`typecmp`) but agrees under `typecmp_lax`, the return types and the shared parameters agreeing and every parameter one list has beyond the other `optional`, whether either is variadic aside, is the warning `W0209` "Optional arguments differ on redeclaration of NAME. A, should be B", unless the two have the same parameters and only the first is variadic, and the definition takes the type with more parameters. A redeclaration of `droptofloor`, `callfunction` or `trailparticles` with another type is the warning `W0210` "NAME builtin was wrongly redefined as TYPE. ignoring later definition", and in a file named `*extensions.qc` (any case) of a function "NAME builtin was redefined as TYPE. ignoring alternative definition": the first type stays and the declaration goes on. A global marked unused that nothing refers to, `def->unused && !def->referenced`, is replaced by a declaration of another type, with the warning `W0211` "Type redeclaration of TYPE NAME replaces existing variable": a builtin a body replaced (FTEF-19.4) is one. A `noref` mark is a reference too (`if (noref) { def->unused = true; def->referenced = true; }`), so a `noref` global declared again with another type is `E0205`. A function declared again as `T(...)` with no parameters is no difference ("c89-style dumb redeclarations"). Any other difference is `E0205`, with FTEQCC's text "Type mismatch on redeclaration of NAME. A, should be B".

A redeclaration's array size, where it gives one, is the definition's: `if (def->arraysize != arraysize && arraysize>=0)` is the error `E0220` "Array sizes for redecleration of NAME do not match (A->B)" (in a function body "(A -> B)"), a declaration that is no array giving 0, so `float x[2]; float x;` is the error. `[]` gives no size, and an unsized definition takes the size a later one gives; an unsized array's initialiser sizes it (`QCC_PR_ParseDefArray` counts the elements of `{ ... }`, and a string's bytes and its terminator, `dim[0] = pr_immediate_strlen+1;`). A size that is no number literal is not compared (FTEF-19.17). An array is initialised with `{ ... }`, or an array of an 8-bit integer (`__int8`, `__uint8`, `__char`: `def.cast->type == ev_bitfld && def.cast->bits == 8`) with a string: anything else is the error `E0204` "expected {, found X" (`QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType_Internal`, `QCC_PR_Expect("{");`). A string of more bytes than the array's size is the error, not fatal, `E0233` "initializer-string too long" (`if (pr_immediate_strlen > arraysize) QCC_PR_ParseWarning (ERR_BADARRAYSIZE, ...)`), so `__char c[2] = "ab";` is no error.

A `typedef` of a name a typedef already names must name the same type, as `QCC_TypeForName` resolves a typedef to its type (`if (t && t->type == ev_typedef) return t->aux_type;`): else the error `E0219` "Cannot redeclare typedef NAME from A to B", so `typedef float t; typedef int t;` is the error and `typedef float t; typedef t t;` is not. A redeclaration compares a typedef's name as the type it names (`typedef float t; t x; vector x;` is `E0205`). A typedef with a storage qualifier is the error `E0224` "bad combination of modifiers with typedef (defining NAME)", `static`, `noref` and `nosave` among them, as no `#pragma` makes them the default here; `typedef;` and `typedef float;` define nothing, with the warning `W0215` "typedef defines no types". A `typedef` in a function body is a definition statement (FTEF-19.1), checked as one at file level, whose type name this profile reads as any other type name.

An enum's names are constants of the enum's base type, `float` unless `: type` gives another, made with `QCC_PR_DummyDef`. A name's value is the one after its `=`, a number or a numeric constant converted to the base type, or the one before it plus 1; under `enumflags` times 2, starting at 1, and 1 after a 0 (`if (!next_i) next_f = next_i = 1;`). Each enum starts its count again. After a value this profile does not compute (FTEF-19.17) the names that follow have no value it compares. A string or vector after `=` is the error `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got string." (`QCC_SupplyConversion`), a name that is no constant with a value the error `E0228` "enum - NAME is not a compile-time constant", and a base type that is no number with no value the error `E0229` "values for enums of this type must be initialised". An `enumflags` value that is no whole number is the warning `W0225` "enumflags - VALUE not an integer value", and one with more than one bit set "enumflags - 0xV(V) has multiple bits set". A base type before the `{` with no `:` is the warning `W0224` "legacy enum base type. Use \"enum [class] [name_e]:type\" instead", and so is a named enum declared again, whose name `QCC_PR_ParseType` then reads as that base type. A later declaration of an enum's name compares its initialiser with the name's value (FTEF-19.5). The names of an `enum class` are not referable alone (`QCC_PR_DummyDef(..., !strictenum, ...)`), only as `Name::value`, and are of the enum's own type, which casts to no other: `float x = E::A;` is "Cannot cast from enum E:float to float".

A `shared` definition is initialised by its declaration (`if (!def->initialized && shared) ... def->initialized = true;`), and giving it a value, then or later, is the error `E0221` "shared values may not be assigned an initial value". An `extern` function is initialised by its declaration too (FTEF-19.4); `extern` on what is no function is ignored, with the warning `W0214` "extern keyword may only apply to qc functions.".

A `static` global is visible only in its unit, the compiled file and the files it includes (`if ((def->isstatic||(flags&GDF_STATIC)) && strcmp(def->unitn, scope?scope->unitn:s_unitn))`), so another unit's lookup finds the next definition of the name, or none; `static` on a name another file defined is the error `E0231` "can't redefine non-static as static".
A use of a definition marked `__deprecated` is the warning `W0314` "Variable \"NAME\" is deprecated", followed by ": REASON" when `__deprecated("REASON")` gives one.

`QCC_PR_ParseState` reads a state header's frame before its next function, so the frame sees no name the header declares (`[h, h]` with `h` not declared before is "Unknown value \"h\""). The frame is converted to a float, a string or vector being `E0227` "Implicit type mismatch. Needed float, got string."; a next function that is a literal but 0 is the error `E0309` "Type mismatch: string, should be void()".

`Scope::name` defines a member of the class `Scope`, or, with the warning `W0216` "Scope::name is not part of class Scope", a new one (`WARN_MEMBERNOTDEFINED`); of a struct, the global `Scope::name` an earlier definition made, else the error `E0226` "Scope::name is not part of class Scope" (`ERR_NOTDEFINED`); and a scope that is neither, a typedef or an enum included, is the error `E0225` "Scope is not a class". After either error this profile still defines the global `Scope::name`, for navigation (QCD-1.4).

A name is looked up as a definition first and only then as an intrinsic (FTEF-17.4), `random` among them ("returning a float just in case people declare things in the wrong order"). Outside a member function `this` is the error `E0310` "Cannot use 'this' outside of an OO function" and `super` `E0311` "Cannot use 'super' outside of an OO function"; in a member function of a class with no parent `super` is `E0312` "class NAME has no super", where the pinned FTEQCC crashes (signal 11), refusing the program as the profile does. A local named `autocvar_...` is a global, with the warning `W0213` "Autocvar \"NAME\" defined with local scope. promoting to global."; a constant or static one is made neither, with "defined as constant. attempting to correct that for you." or "defined as static. ...". A definition named as an enabled keyword (`var`, `for`, `switch`, `case`, `local`, `default`, `goto`, `continue`, `string`, `float`, `entity`, `vector`, `const`, `asm`, and `break` for what is no function) is the warning `W0221` "\"NAME\" keyword used as variable name - coexisting", the keyword keeping its meaning. `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` warns `W0214` "Conflicting storage classes." for more than one of `extern`, `static`, `shared` and `auto`, "Conflicting constness." for `const` and `var`, and "function modifier on non-function." for `inline`, `wrap`, `weak` or `accumulate` on what is no function, which `accumulate` makes the error `E0230` "accumulate applies only to functions, not NAME".

These parts of the path are not modelled by this profile, each for its reason: the types and values of initialisers, default values, array sizes and enum values that are expressions other than a literal, a name or `_()`, which FTEQCC folds and types as it compiles them, the compiler's work (P2-06, constant folding P2-08), so the profile compares such an initialiser by its text (FTEF-17.10) and checks no type of it; the output target, under which `-Tid` makes an `extern` function the error "extern is not supported with this target format" (`QCC_PR_FinishCompilation`) that a target with extern support (`QCF_FTE`) does not give, a code-generation choice (`#pragma target`, P2-07), the FTEQCC corpus mods that use `extern` targetting FTE; the warnings FTEQCC gives as it writes the program rather than as it defines a name, a definition never referred to ("no references", `WARN_NOTREFERENCED`), a function returning a large type (`WARN_SLOW_LARGERETURN`), a field allocated twice ("Field def already has a value", "Inconsistant field def") and the end_sys checks, which belong to the compiler's output (QC-25); struct and union initialisers (designated members, "member ... was already ininitialised", "inherited structs must use designated initialisers", "initializer-string too long") and a definition of a struct type not yet defined ("redeclared with different storage type"), whose checks need the members' layout, the compiler's (QC-21); FTEQCC's reacc and hexenc syntaxes (`flag_acc`, `var name : type`, a field `alias`), which `-Tid` does not enable; attributes `[[...]]`, which `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` reads only after a qualifier or with `flag_attributes`, as the profile's parser does not, the pinned FTEQCC refusing `[[alias("y")]] float x;` as the profile does; and the lexer flags `#pragma flag` sets (`qccx`, which allows float, string and entity casts, `assumeint` and `assumevar`), which the profile reads as off, their `-Tid` defaults.

The definitions family of `cargo xtask oracles builtins` (`xtask/src/oracles/builtins/declarations.rs`) compiles programs that bind `f` and then make the definitions these statements and QC-11 to QC-13 describe, under both profiles, and the FTEQCC warning programs with `-Werror -Wno-Q208`, for which every warning of the profile is an error, so a warning one compiler gives and the other does not changes the outcome (Q208, "no end_sys_fields defined", is what every program without system definitions gets). Its run of 2026-10-21 (macOS arm64) agrees on every case but the vanilla `float k = 7; float y; float x = y;`, which differs as QC-27.8 says.

The locals a `for` statement defines, in its first clause or anywhere in its body, leave scope at its end: `QCC_PR_ParseStatement_For` keeps `subscopestart = pr.local_tail` and, when `pr_subscopedlocals` is off (only `extern "C"` sets it), `subscopestop = pr.local_tail->nextlocal`, which is the end of the list, and after the statement removes every local after `subscopestart` from `localstable` ("remove any new locals from the hashtable. typically this is just the stuff inside the for(here;;)"). So after the loop the name is the global again, or "Unknown value", and a local of the name is a new definition of any type: `for (float i = 0;;) {} for (string i = "";;) {}` is two locals. A local the statement found again (`float i; for (float i = 0;;) {}`, FTEF-19.1) was not made there and stays. Only `for` does this: a block, `while`, `do`, `if` and `switch` keep their locals.

A name that is a definition's type, or part of it (a field's, a pointer's, a function's return or parameter type), must be a type at that point: C type words (FTEF-2.8), a name `QCC_PR_NewType` registers (`variant`, `__variant`, `__string`, `__vector`, `__entity`, `__bfloat` and the scalars of FTEF-2.8), or a class, struct, union, typedef, enum or accessor declared before it, at file level or, for a local, by a `typedef` earlier in the same body (`QCC_TypeForName` finds a typedef whose `scope` is `pr_scope`). Else `QCC_PR_ParseType` gives the error `E0203` "\"NAME\" is not a type", which ends the declaration, so `foo x;`, `.foo x;`, `foo *p;` and `t x; typedef float t;` are errors and `class C; C c;` is not. In a body FTEQCC reads such a statement as an expression ("Unknown value \"NAME\"", FTEF-2.10); this profile, whose parser cannot tell a type name from a value, reports the same `E0203` there and makes no local, an error either way. A type of more than one word that is no run of C words (`struct tag`, an inline `enum` or `struct`) and the types of a class's or struct's members are not checked (FTEF-19.17).
