After a qualifier the type may be left out: `QCC_PR_ParseDefs` sets `hadmodifier` for each storage class or modifier it reads and calls `QCC_PR_ParseType (false, hadmodifier, ...)`, whose `silentfail` returns no type instead of "not a type", and then `if (hadmodifier) { //banned since c99... basetype = type_integer; }`. So `const x = 5;`, `static y;`, `noref z;`, `var v;`, `__register r;` and, in a body, `static y;` define `__int32`s, checked as any definition is (`const x = 5; float x;` is a type mismatch, `const k = "a";` the warning "Implicit cast from string to __int32"). The parser reads the type as left out when a qualifier is followed by a name and then `;`, `,`, `=` or `[`; a name that is a type there (`static t;` after `typedef float t;`) is not told apart, and is read as the name.

A differential run executes one scenario (DIFF-2) in the oracle runner, whose VM is id's `PR_ExecuteProgram`, and in QuakeC Studio's runner, whose VM is `qc-vm`. Each writes one trace ([`trace.md`](trace.md)) of the whole scenario, and the two traces are compared by DIFF-9. Neither program links, calls or generates code from the other: this page and the specs it cites are the whole contract between them.

The oracle's VM is `WinQuake/pr_exec.c` compiled unchanged, built as [`vm.md`](vm.md) "Reference build" requires. Everything around it is the mock engine of this page, written by each side on its own: the edicts, the system globals, the builtin table (`pr_builtins`, 79 entries), the host that calls `PR_ExecuteProgram`, and the `Host_Error` and `Sys_Error` that `PR_RunError` and the builtins call.

Where this page or [`edicts.md`](edicts.md) and [`builtins.md`](builtins.md) say the mock does what an id function does, the oracle may compile that function from the pinned commit (for example `ED_Alloc`, `ED_Free`, `ED_LoadFromFile`, `SV_RunThink` or a class pure `PF_` function), and QuakeC Studio uses its own port. Where those specs fix an answer that id's C leaves undefined or platform-dependent (BUILTIN-2.5, BUILTIN-2.7, BUILTIN-2.10, BUILTIN-7.5, BUILTIN-7.6, BUILTIN-7.7, BUILTIN-8.3, BUILTIN-12.6, BUILTIN-16.3, EDICT-8.3), both mocks implement the fixed answer, so for that case the oracle does not run id's code. The float to integer conversion of BUILTIN-2.2 is the exception: its fixed answer is what id's code gives on x86, so the oracle may use C's conversion. `pr_exec.c` is never changed, so the VM's own undefined cases stay id's and are expected divergences (DIFF-10.1).

A run is deterministic: its trace depends only on the scenario's files. It reads no clock, environment variable, system random source or file the scenario does not name, and running the same scenario twice in the same program writes the same bytes.

The mock engine stands in for id's server; it does not model it. Nothing moves and nothing collides (DIFF-5.8, DIFF-7), so a scenario shows that the two VMs execute the same QuakeC the same way, not that a mod behaves as it does in Quake. The server simulation (`qs-sim`, [#238](https://github.com/quakecstudio/editor/issues/238)) is checked against id's engine by its own suite ([#239](https://github.com/quakecstudio/editor/issues/239)).

A scenario file is lines of bytes ended by a line feed, or a carriage return and a line feed. A `#` and everything after it on the line is a comment. A line that is empty after removing the comment, spaces and tabs is skipped. Every other line is a directive: a key, then its arguments, separated by one or more spaces or tabs. A path is relative to the directory holding the scenario file and cannot contain a space, a tab or a `#`.
The directives are:

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-16: it did not say which texts are numbers, so the two runners could read one scenario differently: C's `strtod` and Rust's `f64` parsing both accept `+0.1` and `inf`, and `strtod` accepts hexadecimal; replaced by DIFF-2.7 (integers), DIFF-2.8 (numbers) and DIFF-2.9 (refusal).

The mock's settings are `skill`, `deathmatch`, `coop` and `teamplay`, with the texts `1`, `0`, `0` and `0`, and each name a `cvar` line gives; a `cvar` line for one of the four replaces its text, and a later line for a name replaces an earlier one. A setting's value is its text read by `Q_atof` (BUILTIN-11.7). There are no other settings: `cvar` of any other name returns 0 and `cvar_set` of it changes nothing (BUILTIN-11.8).

The entities file holds the text of a BSP entity lump, read as `ED_LoadFromFile` reads it (EDICT-8), byte for byte, with a NUL after its last byte. How the runner makes it, for example from a `.map` file with the brushes removed, is not part of this spec: both runners read the same file.

An `input` line is `input <frame> <edict> <field> <values>`: `<frame>` from 1 to `frames`; `<edict>` from 1 to `clients`; `<field>` one of `button0` and `button2` with one value, 0 or 1, `impulse` with one integer from 1 to 255, or `v_angle` with three numbers.

An integer (the arguments DIFF-2.2 and DIFF-2.6 call integers, and the values of `button0`, `button2` and `impulse`) is an optional `-` followed by one or more of the digits `0` to `9`, and nothing else: no `+`, no `.`, no exponent. Its value is the digits read in base 10, leading zeros included, and a value outside the argument's range is refused.

A number (the argument of `frametime`, the six of `model` and the three of `v_angle`) is, in order: an optional `-`; one or more digits, with at most one `.` before, among or after them; and optionally an exponent, `e` or `E`, then an optional `+` or `-`, then one or more digits. Nothing else is a number: not a leading `+`, `inf`, `infinity` or `nan` in any case, hexadecimal, or a `.` without a digit. `frametime` is the `double` nearest the exact decimal value of the text, and a `model` or `v_angle` number the `f32` nearest it, ties to even, each rounded once (never through `double` on the way to `f32`); a value whose magnitude rounds below the smallest subnormal is a zero with the text's sign. A `model` or `v_angle` number whose nearest `f32` is infinite is refused, so every number a scenario gives is finite; `frametime` is refused unless its `double` is greater than 0 and at most 1.

A scenario with an unknown key, a missing or extra argument, a value that is not an integer or a number as DIFF-2.7 and DIFF-2.8 say or is out of range, a repeated key that may appear once, a model name repeated, or no `progs`, is refused before anything runs, and no trace is written.

The runner loads the progs by [`progs.md`](progs.md) with the header CRC checked (PROGS-3). A progs that is refused, or that has fewer than 92 global slots or 105 field slots (EDICT-2.4, EDICT-3.3), ends the scenario with that error before the trace header: no trace is written.

The runner then writes the trace header (TRACE-1.3, TRACE-2.1), and sets the engine state: the setting `deathmatch` becomes `0` when the value of `coop` is non-zero; the skill is `(int)(skill + 0.5)` clamped to 0 to 3 and becomes the value of `skill`; the 600 edicts are all zero with none free and `freetime` 0 (EDICT-1.8); `num_edicts` is `maxclients + 1`; the clock is 1.0; the server is loading; no `changelevel` has been issued; no client slot is active; the 64 lightstyles hold no string; the three message buffers of DIFF-6.5 are empty; `checkclient`'s last choice and its time are 0 (DIFF-7.3); and the random state is the seed (DIFF-6.2).

The sound precache list holds only entry 0, the empty string. The model precache list holds entry 0, the empty string; entry 1, `maps/<map>.bsp`; and entries 2 to `submodels + 1`, the names `*1` to `*<submodels>` (BUILTIN-10.3).

The world's fields are set by EDICT-4.1, its `model` an engine string with the text `maps/<map>.bsp`. Then the globals of EDICT-11.4: `coop` to the value of the `coop` setting when it is non-zero, and otherwise `deathmatch` to the value of the `deathmatch` setting; `mapname` to an engine string with the text `<map>`; `serverflags` to 0. These writes, and `time` set to 1 by EDICT-8.1, appear in the change set of the trace's first run record (TRACE-4.1), after the string records of their engine strings (TRACE-4.10).

The map's entities are spawned from the entities file by EDICT-8, using the value of the `deathmatch` setting and the skill of DIFF-3.2 for EDICT-8.4. Each spawn function is a run. The messages EDICT-8 prints are console output and are not compared.

The server then becomes active and runs the two settle frames of EDICT-8.9 as physics frames of 0.1 seconds (DIFF-5.3), without setting `frametime`, emptying a buffer or clearing muzzle flashes. Then the clients enter (DIFF-4), then `frames` server frames run (DIFF-5.1), and the scenario ends.

A scenario that ends normally runs no more QuakeC: no `ClientDisconnect`, no `SetChangeParms`. What the host writes after the trace's last record, such as the last frame's muzzle-flash clearing, is in no change set and is not compared.

Each engine string (EDICT-13.1) gets a value outside the string table, by EDICT-13.3, and a string record when its text is set (TRACE-4.10). Its number is each runner's own; DIFF-9.4 compares the text.

DIFF-3.8 holds for the strings a builtin sets as for the host's: `ftos` and `vtos` write their one buffer (BUILTIN-7.4) and return its value, so each call whose text differs from that value's latest string record writes a string record before the `CALL`'s step record, whose change set first shows the value in `OFS_RETURN`. A call that sets the same text again writes none, as the oracle's `qs_emit_string_records` skips an unchanged text (`oracles/vm/host.c`). Without the record the value has no text in its trace (TRACE-7.3), and DIFF-9.4 compares the two runners' different numbers as bits.

Client slots 0 to `clients - 1` enter in order. For each, as `SV_ConnectClient` does: run `SetNewParms`, with nothing set before it (EDICT-9.1), then copy the globals `parm1` to `parm16` into the slot's spawn parms. Then, as `Host_Spawn_f` does: set every field of the slot's edict to 0 without changing its free flag; set `colormap` to the edict's number, `team` to 1 (the colours are 0, EDICT-5.2) and `netname` to an engine string with the text `player` (`DIFF_CLIENT_NAME`); copy the spawn parms to `parm1` to `parm16`; set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict; run `ClientConnect`; then run `PutClientInServer` with nothing set between the two.

A slot whose player has entered is active and spawned from then on: it counts as connected for the builtins (BUILTIN-11, BUILTIN-12.7), the physics frame (DIFF-5.4) and `checkclient` (DIFF-7.3). The other slots never have a player.

At the start of server frame `k` (DIFF-5.1), the `input` lines for frame `k` are applied in file order to their edict, as `SV_ReadClientMove` stores a move: `button0` and `button2` set that field to the value, `impulse` sets `impulse` to the value, and `v_angle` sets its three slots to the three values. Nothing else of client input runs: no `SV_ClientThink`, so no field other than these is written.

A server frame of length `T` (the `frametime` directive): sets the global `frametime` to (f32)`T`; empties the unreliable datagram; applies the frame's input (DIFF-4.3); runs a physics frame of length `T` (DIFF-5.3), never paused; empties the reliable datagram; and clears `EF_MUZZLEFLASH` in `effects` on edicts 1 to `num_edicts - 1` (EDICT-10.7), converting `effects` to an integer and back (BUILTIN-2.1, BUILTIN-2.2).

Server frames are numbered from 1. Frame `k` starts with the clock at 1.0 plus 0.1 twice (the settle frames) plus `T` `k - 1` times, each addition made in `double` at the end of a physics frame (DIFF-5.3), so about 1.2 when frame 1 starts.

A physics frame of length `T`, as `SV_Physics`: set `self` and `other` to the world and `time` to (f32)clock, and run `StartFrame`. Then for `i` from 0 while `i` is less than `num_edicts`, read again after each edict: skip edict `i` if it is free; link it (DIFF-5.7) if `force_retouch` is not 0; then give it its turn: an edict from 1 to `maxclients` by DIFF-5.4; otherwise one whose `movetype` equals 7 (`MOVETYPE_PUSH`) by DIFF-5.5; otherwise one whose `movetype` equals 0, 8, 4, 6, 10, 5 or 9 by thinking (DIFF-5.6) and nothing else; otherwise the fatal error `SV_Physics: bad movetype <n>`, `<n>` the integer conversion of `movetype`. The comparisons are of floats, so a `movetype` of 7.5 is a bad movetype. After the last edict, when `force_retouch` is not 0 it is decreased by 1 in `f32`; then the clock advances by `T`.

A client edict's turn does nothing when its slot has no player. Otherwise, as `SV_Physics_Client` without the move: set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict and run `PlayerPreThink`. Then, by the integer conversion of `movetype`: 0, 3, 5 or 8 thinks (DIFF-5.6) and ends the turn if the edict is then free; 6 or 10 thinks and goes on even if the edict is then free, because `SV_Physics_Toss` returns into the turn; any other value is the fatal error `SV_Physics_client: bad movetype <n>`. Then link the edict (DIFF-5.7), set `time` to (f32)clock and `self` to the edict, and run `PlayerPostThink`.

A `MOVETYPE_PUSH` edict's turn, the world's included, is `SV_Physics_Pusher` with `SV_PushMove` reduced to its branch for a pusher with zero velocity, whatever the velocity is: in `f32`, `oldltime` is `ltime` and `thinktime` is `nextthink`; if `thinktime` is less than `ltime + T` (in `double`), `movetime` is `thinktime - ltime`, or 0 if that is negative, and otherwise (f32)`T`; if `movetime` is not 0, `ltime` becomes `ltime + movetime`. Then if `thinktime` is greater than `oldltime` and not greater than `ltime`, set `nextthink` to 0, `time` to (f32)clock, `self` to the edict and `other` to the world, and run `think`. Nothing moves or is pushed, and `solid` is not changed.

Thinking is `SV_RunThink` (EDICT-10.3): when `nextthink` is greater than 0 and not greater than `clock + T` (in `double`), set `time` to `nextthink`, or to (f32)clock if `nextthink` is less than the clock, then `nextthink` to 0, `self` to the edict and `other` to the world, and run `think`. A `nextthink` of exactly (f32)`(clock + T)` can be just above `clock + T` and then waits a frame.

Linking an edict, from a turn or a builtin, is `SV_LinkEdict` without the area tree: for an edict that is not the world and not free it writes `absmin` and `absmax` by EDICT-12.2, and it runs no `touch` function, even where id's call would touch triggers.

The mock frame leaves out everything that needs the map or another entity's box: client movement (`SV_ClientThink`), gravity, `SV_CheckVelocity`, water checks, the moves of every movetype, pushing and blocking, trigger and impact touches and `blocked` functions, and the client updates. So `origin`, `velocity`, `angles`, `groundentity`, `flags`, `waterlevel` and the other fields of EDICT-12 that physics writes change only when QuakeC or a builtin writes them; `touch` and `blocked` are never called; and nothing runs `ClientKill`, `SetChangeParms` or `ClientDisconnect` except DIFF-8.3.

The mock's builtin table has the numbers 0 to 78 of BUILTIN-5. Builtins of class pure, state and output (BUILTIN-4) behave as [`builtins.md`](builtins.md) says, with the engine state of DIFF-2 to DIFF-5 and DIFF-6.3 to DIFF-6.5 as the fixture BUILTIN-4.2 names; the class world builtins behave as DIFF-7 says; the numbers with no builtin fail as BUILTIN-1.2 says.

The C library's `rand` is replaced by a 32-bit unsigned state, which starts at the scenario's seed: each call sets the state to `state * 1103515245 + 12345` modulo 2^32 and returns `(state >> 16) & 0x7fff`. `random` (BUILTIN-6.6) is the only mock builtin that calls it, once per call.

`precache_model` never fails to load a model (BUILTIN-10.4's fatal error does not happen). The bounds of a model list entry, for `setmodel` (BUILTIN-9.4), are: for entry 0, `'0 0 0'` and `'0 0 0'`; for a name given by a `model` directive, its bounds; for any other name ending in the four bytes `.mdl`, `'-16 -16 -16'` and `'16 16 16'`; and for every other name, the world, the submodels and sprites among them, `'0 0 0'` and `'0 0 0'`.

The command buffer that `localcmd` and `changelevel` append to (BUILTIN-11.5, BUILTIN-11.6) is never run: no command executes and the map never changes. `changelevel` still records that it was issued.

The mock keeps the size in bytes of three buffers and nothing else of the output: the unreliable datagram (`MSG_BROADCAST`, `sound`, `particle`), the reliable datagram (`MSG_ALL`), each of `LIMIT_MAX_DATAGRAM` bytes, and the signon buffer (`MSG_INIT`, `ambientsound`, `makestatic`) of `BUILTIN_SIGNON_SIZE` bytes. It counts what BUILTIN-11 to BUILTIN-13 append, so it drops a sound or particle and fails with `SZ_GetSpace: overflow without allowoverflow set` where id's buffers would (BUILTIN-12.2, BUILTIN-12.5, BUILTIN-13.3). A client slot's reliable message is not kept, never overflows and never drops the client. No output, console text included, is compared.

The errors that builtins.md fixes where id's C is undefined are runtime errors (VM-19.7) with these messages in the mock, so both mocks write the same error record: `invalid entity` (BUILTIN-2.7), `invalid string` (BUILTIN-2.5), `invalid field` (BUILTIN-8.3) and `invalid lightstyle` (BUILTIN-12.6).

No mock builtin starts a nested run: `walkmove` and `movetogoal` touch nothing (DIFF-7.7, DIFF-7.8). `traceon` and `traceoff` change only the trace flag (BUILTIN-16.4), which does not change what a runner writes to the trace.

`traceline(v1, v2, nomonsters, forent)` writes `trace_allsolid` 0, `trace_startsolid` 0, `trace_fraction` 1, `trace_endpos` a copy of the three slots of PARM1, `trace_plane_normal` `'0 0 0'`, `trace_plane_dist` 0, `trace_ent` the world, `trace_inopen` 1 and `trace_inwater` 0, and nothing else.
`pointcontents(v)` returns -1 (`CONTENTS_EMPTY`).

`checkclient()` chooses as `PF_checkclient` and `PF_newcheckclient` do, with no PVS: when the clock minus the time of the last choice (both `double`, 0 at map start) is at least 0.1 (`BUILTIN_CHECKCLIENT_INTERVAL`), it takes `check`, the last choice clamped to 1 to `maxclients`, and looks at edicts from `check + 1` (from 1 when `check` is `maxclients`), wrapping from `maxclients + 1` to 1 and stopping at `check`, for the first that is not free, has `health` above 0 and has no `FL_NOTARGET` (128) in its `flags` converted to an integer; the choice is that edict, or `check` when none qualifies, and its time is the clock. It returns the world when the chosen edict is free or its `health` is 0 or less, and the chosen edict otherwise. It does not read `self`.
`checkbottom(e)` returns 1. `aim(e, speed)` returns a copy of the three slots of `v_forward`.

`droptofloor()` leaves `self`'s `origin` as it is, links `self` (DIFF-5.7), sets `flags` to the integer conversion of `flags` with `FL_ONGROUND` (512) set, converted back to a float, sets `groundentity` to the world, and returns 1.

The step of `walkmove` and `movetogoal` along a yaw `a` by a distance `d` is: `y = (f32)(a * M_PI * 2 / 360)` computed in `double`; `move_x = (f32)(cos(y) * d)` and `move_y = (f32)(sin(y) * d)`, in `double`; and `origin_x` and `origin_y` of `self` become `origin_x + move_x` and `origin_y + move_y` in `f32`. `origin_z` is not written.

`walkmove(yaw, dist)` returns 0 and changes nothing when `self`'s `flags`, converted to an integer, has none of `FL_ONGROUND` (512), `FL_FLY` (1) and `FL_SWIM` (2). Otherwise it steps along `yaw` by `dist` (DIFF-7.6), links `self` (DIFF-5.7) and returns 1. It writes no other field.

`movetogoal(step)` writes 0 to `RETURN` and changes nothing else when `self`'s `flags` has none of the three flags of DIFF-7.7. Otherwise it turns `self` as `ChangeYaw` does (BUILTIN-15.4); computes the step along `ideal_yaw` by `step` (DIFF-7.6), applied only when `angles_y - ideal_yaw` (`f32`) is not strictly between 45 and 315; links `self` (DIFF-5.7); and writes nothing to `RETURN`. It does not read `goalentity` or `enemy`, and does not call `rand`.

Every error writes an error record (TRACE-4.6): a runtime error (BUILTIN-3.1), a host error (BUILTIN-3.2, and VM-2.1 raised by `PR_ExecuteProgram`) and a fatal error (BUILTIN-3.3). For an error raised by a statement or by the builtin it called, the function and statement are TRACE-4.7's, which for a builtin is the `CALL`. For an error the host raises outside any run (DIFF-5.3's and DIFF-5.4's bad movetype, EDICT-8.8's parse errors, `ED_ParseEdict: parse error`, `ED_Alloc: no free edicts` while spawning the map), the function is 0 and the statement is -1.

The message is the error's text: for a runtime error, the message `PR_RunError` is given (TRACE-4.8); for `error` and `objerror`, the joined text of BUILTIN-7.3, not id's `Program error`; for VM-2.1, `PR_ExecuteProgram: NULL function`; for a fatal error, the text `Sys_Error` is given.

After a runtime or host error, when the server is active (from the settle frames on), the host shuts the server down as `Host_ShutdownServer` does: for each client slot in order whose player has entered, it saves `self`, sets `self` to the slot's edict, runs `ClientDisconnect` and restores `self` (EDICT-9.2). Then the scenario ends. While the map is loading the server is not active, and the scenario ends after the error record.

The shutdown's runs start where the error left the VM. After a runtime error the call depth is 0 (VM-19.1); after a host error it is still the depth at the error, since neither `Host_Error` nor `PF_error` resets it (BUILTIN-3.2, VM-2.1). Either way the local stack keeps the slots the aborted functions saved (VM-19.6). Each `ClientDisconnect` run takes that depth as its exit depth (VM-2.3), so after `error` called 30 calls deep its first QC call reaches `LIMIT_MAX_STACK_DEPTH` and fails with `stack overflow`.

An error during the shutdown writes its error record and ends the scenario at once: id's `Host_Error` is then entered a second time and calls `Sys_Error ("Host_Error: recursively entered")`, so the later slots' `ClientDisconnect` does not run.
A fatal error writes its error record and ends the scenario with no shutdown: `Sys_Error` prints, calls `Host_Shutdown`, which runs no QuakeC, and exits.

Two traces of one scenario are equal when their headers have the same version, `progs_crc`, `entityfields` and `numstrings` (`edict_size` and `field_offset` may differ), they have the same number of change-carrying records (TRACE-3), and each pair of corresponding change-carrying records, the `n`th of each, agrees by DIFF-9.2 and DIFF-9.3. String records are not paired with each other; they are used only to read values (TRACE-7.3).

Corresponding records have the same tag, and: run records the same function; step records the same function, statement, opcode and builtin number, or both no builtin; error records the same function, statement and message, byte for byte.

After each pair, every global slot and every field (edict number and field slot) listed in either record's change set has equivalent values in the two traces (DIFF-9.4). A trace's value of a slot at a record is the value in the latest change set up to and including that record that lists the slot; if none does, it is the progs file's value for a global (PROGS-12.1) and 0 for a field (TRACE-3.4).

A value `a` of trace A and `b` of trace B are equivalent by the first rule that applies: if each is an engine string of its trace (a value from outside 0 to `numstrings - 1` with a string record before the record being compared, TRACE-7.3), they are equivalent exactly when the latest texts are the same bytes; otherwise they are equivalent when their bits are equal, when both are NaNs (VM-4.3), when both name the same edict `n` below `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` by TRACE-7.1, or when both name the same field slot of the same edict `n` below `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` by TRACE-7.2, each through its own trace's header.

The first divergence is the first pair of corresponding records that fails DIFF-9.2 or DIFF-9.3, or, when one trace has fewer change-carrying records, the first record the shorter one lacks. Comparison stops there. A divergence in a run record's change set is a difference in the host's own writes, which are the mock engine's (TRACE-4.1), not the VM's.
A divergence that DIFF-10.1 lists is reported as expected; any other is a failure.
These are the expected divergences between the oracle and QuakeC Studio:
NaN payloads (VM-4.3), the edict header size (EDICT-1.3) and engine string numbers (EDICT-13.3) are not divergences: DIFF-9.4 compares through them.

No other divergence is expected. One that DIFF-10.1 does not list is a defect in `qc-vm`, `qc-edict`, the mock engine or the oracle runner, and is fixed there. A row is added only with a statement elsewhere in `docs/spec/` that makes the divergence deliberate and gives its reason ([`../porting.md`](../porting.md)).
A statement is executed in a trace when a step record has its index. The statements of a progs are 1 to `numstatements - 1`.

The statement coverage of a progs over a set of scenarios is the number of distinct statements executed in any of their traces divided by `numstatements - 1`. It is measured on QuakeC Studio's traces, counting only the records before the first divergence of each, so a statement counts only once both VMs agree on it.

For the report, a QC function's statements are those from its `first_statement` up to, not including, the next larger `first_statement` of a QC function (`first_statement` above 0), or `numstatements` for the last; a statement before the first QC function belongs to none.

An edict is `EDICT_HEADER_SIZE` (96) bytes of engine state followed by `entityfields` 4-byte field slots (PROGS-13.1). The edict size is `96 + 4 * entityfields` bytes; for id 1.01's 105 field slots it is 516.

The header holds, in order: the free flag, the area links, the BSP leaf count and up to 16 leaf numbers (`LIMIT_MAX_ENT_LEAFS`), the network baseline, and `freetime`, the server time the edict was last freed (an `f32`). QuakeC cannot address the header: field slot 0 is the first byte after it.

id computes the header size as `sizeof(edict_t) - sizeof(entvars_t)`, which depends on the build. This spec fixes 96, the size on the 32-bit x86 build id shipped; a 64-bit build of the same code has 108. The header size is visible to QuakeC only through entity and pointer values (EDICT-1.5, EDICT-1.6), so a comparison with an oracle built for 64 bits compares those values as edict numbers and field slots; the trace header records each VM's edict size and field offset for this (TRACE-2.1).

The array has `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` (600) edicts, numbered from 0. Edict 0 is the world (EDICT-4) and edicts 1 to `maxclients` are the client slots (EDICT-5). `num_edicts` starts at `maxclients + 1` (EDICT-1.8) and grows by one each time allocation takes a new edict (EDICT-6.2); it never shrinks, and edicts at or above it have not been used on this map.
An entity value is the edict's number times the edict size (PROGS-17.4): with 105 field slots, edict 3 is 1548. Edict 0 is 0, so the world is the "null" entity.
A pointer value made by `OP_ADDRESS` for field slot `f` of edict `n` is `n * edict size + 96 + 4 * f` (PROGS-17.7).

Turning a number into an edict fails with `EDICT_NUM: bad number <n>` when the number is negative or not less than 600. Turning an edict back into a number fails with `NUM_FOR_EDICT: bad pointer` when the number is negative or not less than `num_edicts`. An entity value is not checked when QuakeC uses it (`PROG_TO_EDICT` only adds); what one that names no edict (EDICT-1.9) does is in VM-11.4, VM-12.5 and BUILTIN-2.7.

Every map gets a new array: `SV_SpawnServer` reloads the progs, which resets every global to its value in the file (PROGS-12.1), and allocates the edicts zero-filled, so every field of every edict is 0 and no edict is free until the map's entities are spawned (EDICT-8). `num_edicts` starts at `maxclients + 1`.

An entity value **names an edict** when it is `n` times the edict size for a whole number `n` from 0 to `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS - 1` (599); it names edict `n`. It does so whether or not `n` is below `num_edicts` and whether or not edict `n` is free: the array holds all 600 edicts (EDICT-1.4), so id's code reads and writes such an edict as any other. Any other value, negative, not a multiple of the edict size, or 600 edicts or more, names none: id's `PROG_TO_EDICT` (`(edict_t *)((byte *)sv.edicts + e)`) then gives an address that is not the start of an edict in the array, so what it reaches depends on the header size (EDICT-1.3) or lies outside the array. The edict size is the VM's own (TRACE-2.1), so the same edict number is a different value in a 32-bit and a 64-bit build.
The engine's system globals are the 64 slots from 28 (`PROGS_RESERVED_OFS`) to 91, at these slots, with these types:

The only check that a progs puts these globals at these slots is the header CRC (PROGS-3.2, PROGS-5): qcc's `progdefs.h` lists, in order, every global declared before the one named `end_sys_globals`, so a progs whose CRC is 5927 declared exactly these names and types in this order. `end_sys_globals` itself is not a system global, and the engine does not use its slot.

When the CRC check is skipped (PROGS-15.8), the system globals are still the slots of EDICT-2.1, whatever the progs' definitions say is there, as id's engine would read them; they are never resolved by name.

A progs with fewer than 92 global slots cannot hold the system globals. id's engine would read and write past the end of the globals, which is undefined; this spec fixes the answer: such a progs is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up. A progs id's qcc wrote with CRC 5927 always has at least 92.
The engine's system fields are the 105 field slots from 0 to 104, at these slots, with these types; a mod's own fields follow from slot 105:

As for globals, only the header CRC ties a progs' field definitions to these slots: `progdefs.h` lists every field declared before the one named `end_sys_fields`. The engine never looks a system field up by name, and with the CRC check skipped (PROGS-15.8) the system fields are still the slots of EDICT-3.1. `end_sys_fields` takes a field slot of its own (QC-21.3) that the engine does not use.

A progs whose `entityfields` is less than 105 cannot hold the system fields. id's engine would write them past the edict's fields into the next edict, which is undefined; this spec fixes the answer: such a progs is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up. A progs id's qcc wrote with CRC 5927 always has at least 105.

The engine reads these non-system fields by name, and only if the progs defines them: `gravity` (scales gravity, `SV_AddGravity`), `items2` (`SV_WriteClientdataToMessage`), and the mission-pack ammo fields set by the `give` cheat (`Host_Give_f`). Lookup is by exact name over the field definitions, first match (`ED_FindField`); a missing field is skipped, not an error.

With more than 894760 field slots, `LIMIT_MAX_EDICTS` edicts of EDICT-1.1's size take more than 2147483647 bytes, so an entity value (EDICT-1.5), a 32-bit integer, cannot name every edict, and id's `PR_LoadProgs` computes `entityfields * 4` as an `int`, which overflows for a large enough count, which is undefined. This spec fixes the answer: a progs whose `entityfields` is greater than 894760 is refused with a typed error when the edict store is set up, whether or not the header CRC was checked. No progs a compiler writes comes near it. 894760 is `(2147483647 / 600 - 96) / 4`, each division rounded down.

Before the map's entities are parsed, the engine zeroes edict 0's fields, clears its free flag, and sets `model` to the world model's name (`maps/<map>.bsp`), `modelindex` to 1, `solid` to `SOLID_BSP` (4) and `movetype` to `MOVETYPE_PUSH` (7).

The map's first entity is parsed into edict 0 without clearing it first, so the four fields of EDICT-4.1 keep their values unless the entity's keys set them. Every later entity is cleared first (EDICT-8.2).

QuakeC may store into the world's fields only while the map is loading; once the server is active, `OP_ADDRESS` on edict 0 fails with `assignment to world entity` (VM-12.2; a pointer made while loading still writes later, VM-12.6). Engine code writes the world's fields at any time.
The world is never handed out by allocation (EDICT-6.1), is never linked into the area tree, and gets physics like any other edict: `MOVETYPE_PUSH` (EDICT-10.4).
The global `world` (slot 30) is never written by the engine; it is entity 0 because qcc writes an uninitialised global as 0.
`remove(world)` is not refused: edict 0 is freed by EDICT-7 like any other, and from then on the physics loop skips it. id's engine has no check, and this spec keeps its behaviour.
Edicts 1 to `maxclients` belong to the client slots in order: client slot `i` (from 0) is edict `i + 1`, whether or not a player is connected. `maxclients` is 1 to 16.

When a player enters a map that was not loaded from a saved game, the engine zeroes the client edict's fields and sets `colormap` to the edict's number, `team` to the player's bottom colour plus 1 (`(colors & 15) + 1`) and `netname` to the player's name. It does not change the edict's free flag.
A client edict is never handed out by allocation (EDICT-6.1), even when it is free or no player uses it. When a player disconnects the edict keeps its fields ("the body stays around").

The physics loop runs a client edict only while its slot has a connected player, and skips it when it is free. A client edict freed by `remove` stays free until the next map, since EDICT-5.2 does not clear the flag.

Allocation scans edicts `maxclients + 1` to `num_edicts - 1` in increasing order and takes the first one that is free and whose `freetime` is less than 2 or more than 0.5 seconds before now (`freetime < 2 || sv.time - freetime > 0.5`).

If no edict qualifies, it takes edict `num_edicts` and adds one to `num_edicts`. If `num_edicts` is already 600, it fails with `ED_Alloc: no free edicts`, even when free edicts exist that are too recently freed to qualify.

The comparison is made in double precision between the server clock and the `f32` `freetime`, and is strict: an edict freed at time t is reused at t + 0.6 but not at t + 0.5. Because `freetime` is rounded to `f32`, the delay measured on the clock can differ slightly from 0.5: an edict freed at 100000.3 has `freetime` 100000.296875 and is reused at 100000.8.
An edict freed while `freetime` is below 2 (in the first second of a map, whose clock starts at 1, EDICT-8.1) can be reused at once.
The edict handed out has every field slot set to 0 and its free flag cleared. Its header is otherwise left as it was, including `freetime`, the leaf links and the baseline.

`spawn` returns the new edict's entity value. An edict allocated while the physics loop is running gets its turn in the same frame if its number is above the edict being run (EDICT-10.2), and waits for the next frame otherwise.

Freeing an edict unlinks it from the area tree, sets its free flag, sets `freetime` to the server clock rounded to `f32`, and sets these fields: `model`, `takedamage`, `modelindex`, `colormap`, `skin`, `frame`, `origin`, `angles` and `solid` to 0, and `nextthink` to -1.
Every other field keeps its value: `classname`, `think`, `touch`, `owner`, `health` and the rest can still be read through an entity value that refers to a freed edict.

Nothing else changes: entity values elsewhere that refer to the freed edict are not cleared (id's comment: "FIXME: walk all entities and NULL out references to this entity"), and `num_edicts` does not shrink.
Freeing an edict that is already free does it all again, so `freetime` moves to the later time and the reuse delay starts over.
`remove` frees its argument by EDICT-7.1. `makestatic` frees its argument after sending it to clients as a static entity. `objerror` frees `self` before stopping the map with its error.

A map starts with the server clock at 1. The engine sets the globals of EDICT-11.4, sets the `time` global to 1, and spawns the entities of the BSP's entity lump in file order. `time` is not set again between entities.

The first entity goes into edict 0 (EDICT-4.2); each later one into an edict from allocation (EDICT-6), which clears it. Each `"key" "value"` pair is then applied in order, a later duplicate key overwriting an earlier one: - the key `angle` is renamed `angles` and its value `v` becomes `0 v 0`, and the key `light` is renamed `light_lev`; - trailing spaces are removed from the key; - a key starting with `_` is ignored; - a key that names no field is ignored, with the message `'<key>' is not a field`; - otherwise the value is converted by the field's type: a string becomes a new engine string with the escapes of EXAMPLE-1, a float is C `atof`, a vector is three `atof` values separated by single spaces, an entity is the entity value (EDICT-1.5) of edict `atoi(value)` (id's `EDICT_TO_PROG(EDICT_NUM(atoi (s)))`, so a number out of range is EDICT-1.7's `EDICT_NUM: bad number <n>`), a function is the function of that name, and a field is the value of the global whose slot is the named field's offset (id reads `G_INT(def->ofs)`, the field's offset in the entity used as a global slot). An unknown function or field name is the error `ED_ParseEdict: parse error`.
A vector value with fewer than three space-separated components reads past the end of the value in id's code, which is undefined; this spec fixes the answer: the missing components are 0.

After its keys are applied, an entity is freed (EDICT-7) instead of spawned, and counted as inhibited, when deathmatch is on and its `spawnflags` has `SPAWNFLAG_NOT_DEATHMATCH` (2048); or when deathmatch is off and the skill is 0 with `SPAWNFLAG_NOT_EASY` (256), 1 with `SPAWNFLAG_NOT_MEDIUM` (512), or 2 or more with `SPAWNFLAG_NOT_HARD` (1024). The skill is the `skill` setting rounded (`(int)(skill + 0.5)`) and clamped to 0 to 3 when the map starts. `spawnflags` is truncated to an integer for the test.

An entity with no `classname`, or whose `classname` names no function, is freed with the message `No classname for:` or `No spawn function for:` followed by the entity's fields. Function names are matched exactly and the first match wins.
Otherwise the engine sets `self` to the entity and calls the function named by its `classname`, then moves on to the next entity. Nothing else (no `other`, no `frametime`) is set.
Because the clock is 1 while entities spawn, an inhibited or classless entity's edict is reused by the very next allocation (EDICT-6.4).

Text that is not `{` where an entity should start is the error `ED_LoadFromFile: found <token> when expecting {`; running out of text inside an entity is `ED_ParseEntity: EOF without closing brace`; a `}` where a value should be is `ED_ParseEntity: closing brace without data`.

After the last entity the server becomes active and runs two physics frames of 0.1 seconds each (EDICT-10), so play starts with the clock at 1.2. The `frametime` global is not set for these two frames: it keeps the progs file's value, or whatever the spawn functions stored.
The engine calls QuakeC only at these points:

`touch` from a trigger (`SV_TouchLinks`) and from a collision (`SV_Impact`) save `self` and `other` before the call and restore them afterwards, as does `ClientDisconnect` for `self`. No other entry point restores anything.

A trigger's `touch` runs only if the trigger is `SOLID_TRIGGER` (1) and `touch` is not 0. A collision runs each side's `touch` only if it is not 0 and the side is not `SOLID_NOT` (0), the moving entity first.

The engine calls the function in the global or field even when it is 0 or out of range, which fails with `PR_ExecuteProgram: NULL function` (VM-2.1): a progs with no `StartFrame` fails on the first frame, and an entity with `nextthink` due and `think` 0 fails when it would think. The function global `main` is never called.

A server frame does, in order: set the `frametime` global to the frame's length; read each client's input and apply its movement (`SV_RunClients`, which calls no QuakeC); run the physics frame unless paused; send the updates to clients. In single player the physics frame does not run while the console or a menu has focus.

A physics frame calls `StartFrame` (EDICT-9.1), then visits edicts 0 to `num_edicts - 1` in increasing order, reading `num_edicts` again after each one, and skips free edicts. Each visited edict gets its turn: client edicts 1 to `maxclients` by `SV_Physics_Client`, and every other edict by its `movetype`. On an edict that is not a client, a `movetype` other than `NONE` (0), `STEP` (4), `FLY` (5), `TOSS` (6), `PUSH` (7), `NOCLIP` (8), `FLYMISSILE` (9) or `BOUNCE` (10) is the error `SV_Physics: bad movetype <n>`; on a client edict, one other than `NONE`, `WALK` (3), `FLY`, `TOSS`, `NOCLIP` or `BOUNCE` is the error `SV_Physics_client: bad movetype <n>`. After the last edict, the server clock advances by the frame's length.

An entity thinks when its `nextthink` is greater than 0 and not more than the clock plus the frame's length (so up to one frame early). The engine sets `nextthink` to 0, sets `time` to `nextthink`, or to the clock if `nextthink` is earlier, sets `self` and `other`, and calls `think`. A `nextthink` of 0 or less never thinks, which is why a freed edict (`nextthink` -1) does not.

A `MOVETYPE_PUSH` entity thinks by its own clock `ltime` instead: when `nextthink` is less than `ltime` plus the frame's length, it moves only up to `nextthink` (not at all if `nextthink` is behind `ltime`); after the move, if `nextthink` is above the old `ltime` and not above the new one, it sets `nextthink` to 0, `time` to the server clock (not `nextthink`), `self` and `other`, and calls `think`. A pusher that is blocked does not advance `ltime`, so it does not think.

Where in its turn an entity thinks depends on `movetype`: `MOVETYPE_NONE`, `NOCLIP`, `TOSS`, `BOUNCE`, `FLY` and `FLYMISSILE` think before moving and do not move if the think freed them; `MOVETYPE_STEP` thinks after moving. A client edict thinks after `PlayerPreThink` and before its move; with `MOVETYPE_TOSS` or `BOUNCE` it moves by the toss physics, which also thinks first.

If `force_retouch` is non-zero when the loop reaches an edict, the edict is relinked with trigger touching before its turn. After the loop, a non-zero `force_retouch` is decreased by 1. A negative value therefore relinks every frame and keeps decreasing.
After the updates are sent each frame, the engine clears the muzzle-flash bit (`EF_MUZZLEFLASH`, 2) of `effects` on edicts 1 to `num_edicts - 1`, free or not.

`self`, `other`: written by the engine before each call into QuakeC as EDICT-9.1 says. The `walkmove` builtin saves `self` before its move, which can run touch functions, and restores it after. The engine reads `self` in builtins that act on it.
`world`: never written by the engine (EDICT-4.5).
`time`: written by the engine before each call into QuakeC as EDICT-9.1 says. The engine reads it only in `OP_STATE` (VM-17.1).

`deathmatch`, `coop`, `mapname`, `serverflags`: written once per map, before the entities spawn. If the `coop` setting is non-zero the engine writes `coop` from it and leaves `deathmatch` alone (the `deathmatch` setting is forced to 0); otherwise it writes `deathmatch` from its setting and leaves `coop` alone. `mapname` is the map's name without `maps/` or `.bsp`, and `serverflags` the value saved from the previous map (EDICT-11.6).
`frametime`: written by the engine at the start of each server frame (EDICT-10.1), not during the spawn frames (EDICT-8.9).

`serverflags`: QuakeC writes it; the engine reads it at `changelevel` to carry it to the next map, and sends its low 4 bits to clients as the sigils of the status bar (bits 28 to 31 of the items) unless the progs defines `items2`. The `map` command starts a new game with it 0.
`force_retouch`: QuakeC writes it; the engine reads it and decreases it by 1 each physics frame while it is non-zero (EDICT-10.6).

`teamplay`, `total_secrets`, `total_monsters`, `found_secrets`, `killed_monsters`: never written by the engine. The four counters are read when a player enters the map, to send them to that player's status bar; `teamplay` is not read (the engine uses its `teamplay` setting).

`parm1` to `parm16`: written by the engine from the client's saved parms just before `ClientConnect` (EDICT-9.1) and by the `setspawnparms` builtin. Read by the engine into the client's saved parms just after `SetNewParms` and after each `SetChangeParms`.
`v_forward`, `v_up`, `v_right`: written only by the `makevectors` builtin; `v_forward` is read by the `aim` builtin.

`trace_allsolid`, `trace_startsolid`, `trace_fraction`, `trace_endpos`, `trace_plane_normal`, `trace_plane_dist`, `trace_ent`, `trace_inopen`, `trace_inwater`: written only by the `traceline` builtin, all together; `trace_ent` is the world when the trace hit nothing. Never read by the engine. Movement that collides does not write them.
`msg_entity`: never written by the engine; read by the `Write*` builtins when the destination is one client.

`main`, `StartFrame`, `PlayerPreThink`, `PlayerPostThink`, `ClientKill`, `ClientConnect`, `PutClientInServer`, `ClientDisconnect`, `SetNewParms`, `SetChangeParms`: never written by the engine; each holds the function the engine calls by EDICT-9.1, and `main` is never read.
`modelindex`, `model`: written by the `setmodel` builtin, by freeing (to 0), and for the world when the map starts (EDICT-4.1).

`absmin`, `absmax`: written by the engine whenever it links the entity into the area tree (`setorigin`, `setsize`, `setmodel` and physics): `origin + mins` and `origin + maxs`, widened by 15 on x and y for an entity whose `flags` has `FL_ITEM` (256) and by 1 on every axis otherwise. Not written for the world or a free edict.
`ltime`: written by physics for `MOVETYPE_PUSH` entities, advanced by each move that is not blocked (EDICT-10.4).

`movetype`, `solid`: `movetype` is written for the world (EDICT-4.1) and by the `noclip` and `fly` cheats; `solid` for the world, by freeing (to 0), and by physics, which sets a `MOVETYPE_PUSH` entity's `solid` to `SOLID_NOT` while it pushes each entity and then to `SOLID_BSP` (4), whatever it was before.

`origin`: written by the `setorigin` and `droptofloor` builtins, by physics and client input, and by freeing (to 0). `oldorigin`: written by physics for client entities (`SV_CheckStuck`) to the last position that was not stuck.

`velocity`: written by physics (gravity, clipping, `sv_maxvelocity`, a NaN component becomes 0) and client input. `avelocity`: written by physics, set to 0 with `velocity` when a `TOSS`, `BOUNCE`, `FLY` or `FLYMISSILE` entity lands on a floor, unless it bounces (`BOUNCE` with an upward speed of 60 or more).

`angles`: written by the `changeyaw` builtin (and `movetogoal` through it), by physics from `avelocity`, by client input (pitch and yaw from `v_angle` unless `fixangle` is set, roll from movement), and by freeing (to 0).

`punchangle`: decayed toward 0 by client input. `v_angle`, `button0`, `button2`, `impulse`: written by client input from the player's last move; `impulse` only when the move carries a non-zero impulse, so QuakeC must clear it. `button1` is never written by the engine.

`classname`: never written by the engine except by map keys. `frame`, `skin`: written by freeing (to 0); `frame` also by `OP_STATE` (VM-17.2). `effects`: its `EF_MUZZLEFLASH` bit is cleared after every frame's updates (EDICT-10.7).

`mins`, `maxs`, `size`: written by the `setsize` and `setmodel` builtins (`size` is `maxs - mins`). When a pusher is blocked by a `SOLID_NOT` or `SOLID_TRIGGER` entity, physics sets that entity's `mins` x and y to 0 and `maxs` to `mins`, without changing `size`.

`touch`, `use`, `blocked`, `target`, `targetname`, `message`, `sounds`, `noise`, `noise1` to `noise3`, `deadflag`, `max_health`, `armortype`, `aiment`, `spawnflags`, `owner`, `movedir`, `enemy`, `goalentity`, `yaw_speed`, `view_ofs`, `weaponmodel`, `weaponframe`, `currentammo`, `frags`, `armorvalue`, `dmg_inflictor`, `takedamage` (except freeing, to 0): never written by the engine. Of these the engine reads `touch` and `blocked` (EDICT-9.1), `message` and `sounds` of the world (sent to clients as the level name and CD track), `spawnflags` (EDICT-8.4), `owner` (collision filtering), `enemy`, `goalentity` and `yaw_speed` (the movement builtins), `view_ofs` (water level, the `checkclient` builtin and the client update), `movedir` (water jumps), `takedamage` (the `aim` builtin), `frags` and the status-bar fields (client update). `use` is never read.
`think`, `nextthink`: `think` is written only by `OP_STATE` (VM-17.3); `nextthink` by `OP_STATE` (VM-17.1), set to 0 just before each think (EDICT-10.3, EDICT-10.4), and set to -1 by freeing.
`groundentity`: written by physics and by the `droptofloor`, `walkmove` and `movetogoal` builtins when the entity lands on something.

`health`, `weapon`, `items`, `ammo_shells`, `ammo_nails`, `ammo_rockets`, `ammo_cells`: written by the engine only through the `give` cheat; read for the client update, and `health` also by `kill` (EDICT-9.1) and client input (a player with 0 or less does not move).
`chain`: written by the `findradius` builtin, which links its results through it.

`fixangle`, `dmg_take`, `dmg_save`: cleared to 0 by the client update once it has sent them (the view angles if `fixangle` is set; the damage indicator if either damage field is non-zero). `idealpitch`: written during each client update, on the edict of the last client whose input was read (id's `SV_SetIdealPitch` uses `sv_player`, not the client being updated; with one player they are the same).
`netname`, `colormap`, `team`: written when a player enters the map (EDICT-5.2); `netname` also by the `name` command and `team` by the `color` command; `colormap` set to 0 by freeing.

`flags`: the engine sets and clears `FL_ONGROUND` (512), `FL_PARTIALGROUND` (1024) and `FL_WATERJUMP` (2048) in physics, client input and the `droptofloor`, `walkmove` and `movetogoal` builtins; the `god` and `notarget` cheats toggle `FL_GODMODE` (64) and `FL_NOTARGET` (128). It does so by converting `flags` to an integer and back, so a fractional part is lost.
`teleport_time`: cleared to 0 by client input when a water jump ends. `waterlevel`, `watertype`: written by physics from the contents at the entity's position.
`ideal_yaw`: written by the `movetogoal` builtin as it picks directions.

A string value the engine makes (`mapname`, `netname`, the world's `model`, and every string value set from a map key) is the address of engine-owned text minus the address of the string table (PROGS-11.6). It is not 0 and does not lie inside the string table; its number depends on memory layout and is not part of this spec. The strings builtins return are in `builtins.md`.
An engine-made string value is true in a condition unless its text is empty (`OP_NOT_S` tests both the value and the first byte).

QuakeC Studio represents engine-made strings in a range of values that cannot be a string-table offset, so that EDICT-13.1 and EDICT-13.2 hold; the differential comparison (`differential.md`, P1-27) compares their text, not their numbers.
An entity value the engine makes is always EDICT-1.5's value for that edict; the engine never makes a pointer value.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it built the database from three files, but ADR-0015 added DarkPlaces' `csprogsdefs.qc` and `menudefs.qc`; replaced by ENGT-1.4.

Generation is reproducible: `cargo xtask engines` fetches each pinned file and writes the tables, and `cargo xtask engines --check` writes nothing and fails when the checked-in tables differ from what the sources give. A fetched file or license file whose SHA-256 is not the pinned one is an error, and nothing is written.
The `rerelease` pin is the corpus manifest's `quake-rerelease-qc` pin (`corpus/manifest.toml`): the same commit and the same SHA-256 for `quakec/defs.qc` and `COPYING.txt`. A difference is an error.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it built the database from five files, but ADR-0016 added the five C files of QuakeSpasm, Ironwail and vkQuake; replaced by ENGT-1.5.

The database is built from the ten files above, each pinned by repository, commit and SHA-256 together with its repository's license file, and from id's vanilla table of `qc-builtins` (BUILTIN-5). The generated `crates/qc-engines/src/tables.rs` records every pin, so the checked-in tables carry their source checksums.

Only facts are kept: for each builtin its key (ENGT-2.4), its QuakeC name, its signature and the extensions it belongs to (ENGT-2.7), and for each file its extension names (ENGT-2.6). No comment text, no code and no other declaration is kept.

A `//` comment runs to the end of its line and a `/* */` comment may span lines; a string literal is code, so a `//` inside one starts no comment. Comments are read only for the extension names of ENGT-2.6 and ENGT-2.7.

`#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#else` and `#endif` are evaluated, with `#if` expressions built from `defined(NAME)`, `defined NAME`, `!`, `&&`, `||`, parentheses and decimal numbers, over the macros the source defines before it is read (`NQSSQC` and `SSQC` for `fteqw`, choosing its server QuakeC builtins; none for the others) and the `#define` and `#undef` lines of the parts that are read. Only those parts are read. `#pragma` is ignored; any other directive, an `#if` that cannot be read, an `#else` or `#endif` with no open block, or a block still open at the end of the file is an error.

A statement `TYPE NAME = #N`, with `N` at least 1, is the builtin with key number `N`; `TYPE NAME = #0:ENGINE_NAME` is the builtin the engine looks up by `ENGINE_NAME`. `TYPE` is a function type, and its whitespace is collapsed to single spaces; the C-like form `RET NAME(PARAMS) = #N` gives the signature `RET(PARAMS)`. A `#0` with no name, a number that is not decimal digits, or a builtin whose name or type cannot be read is an error. When a file declares one key twice, the first declaration is kept.
The deprecation markers `DEP`, `DEP_CSQC`, `FTEDEP(...)` and `__deprecated(...)` before a builtin's type are dropped, with their argument.

A file's extension names, each kept once in file order, are the names of its `#define NAME` lines with no parameters and no body and the comment lines that hold nothing but a name, when the name has the shape of an extension: upper-case ASCII letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, with an underscore, and not ending in one.

A builtin's extensions are the names after `Part of ` in the comment on the line where its declaration ends, separated by commas, up to the first word that is not upper-case letters, digits, underscores and `?`; without one, the last comment-line name of ENGT-2.6 above it; without either, none.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it read every source for server QuakeC, but the DarkPlaces client and menu sources of ADR-0015 give only a client or a menu table; replaced by ENGT-2.10.

A statement ends at a `;` outside a string literal, or at a `}` outside parentheses that closes the statement's outermost `{`, so a function body with no `;` after it ends at its closing brace; a `{` or `}` inside parentheses, as in FTEQW's `enumflags:float{...}` parameter types, ends nothing. A comment line is read for an extension name (ENGT-2.6) only outside a statement: when no code of an unfinished statement precedes it and no brace or parenthesis is open.

Each source is read once per module kind (PRJ-3.1) it gives a table for, each reading by ENGT-2.1 to ENGT-2.7 and ENGT-2.9 with its own predefined macros, giving its own builtins and extension names. `fteqw` is read for server QuakeC (`ssqc`) with the macros of ENGT-2.3, for client QuakeC (`csqc`) with `CSQC` alone defined and for menu QuakeC (`menuqc`) with `MENU` alone defined, the macros its own `#if` lines test for those kinds; `darkplaces` and `rerelease` are read for server QuakeC, `darkplaces-client` for client QuakeC and `darkplaces-menu` for menu QuakeC, each with no macro defined. `sources.toml` lists each source's readings as `tables`; a source with no table, a table of any other kind, or two tables of one kind is an error, and nothing is written.

A source whose file is C (`.c`) is read by ENGT-2.12 to ENGT-2.17 instead of ENGT-2.2 to ENGT-2.7 and ENGT-2.9, which read the QuakeC (`.qc`) sources. A reading of a QuakeC source gives its `defines` and no C column; a reading of a C source gives the `array` it reads and no `defines`; a file of any other kind, or a reading that does not fit its file, is an error, and nothing is written. In a C file a `//` comment runs to the end of its line and a `/* */` comment may span lines; both are dropped unread, so no comment text of a C source is ever kept. String and character literals are single tokens, and a line whose first non-blank character is `#` is a directive, continued by a final `\`.

`#define NAME BODY`, `#define NAME(PARAMS) BODY` (function-like when the `(` follows the name directly) and `#undef NAME` take effect in file order. In the array's initialiser a name that is a macro is replaced by its body, a function-like macro followed by `(` with each parameter replaced by its argument, and the result is expanded again with that macro left alone; Ironwail's `PF_SSQC(x)` becomes `x,NULL`, and vkQuake's `D(typestr, desc)` becomes `typestr, desc`. Conditional directives are not evaluated: using a macro defined inside an `#if`, `#ifdef` or `#ifndef` block, or one whose body has `#` or `##`, is an error. Outside the initialiser any other directive is passed over; inside it, any directive but `#define` and `#undef` is an error.

The array is the first `NAME [ ] =` followed by a braced initialiser. Its elements are split at the commas outside brackets, a final comma ending no element; an element in braces is a row, whose columns are split the same way. A column a row does not have is zero, as in C: no function, the number 0, no type string and no extension. An array that is not found, or an initialiser with no end, is an error.

A reading with no `name` column reads a positional array: element `N` is the builtin with key number `N`, named by its C function, with no signature and no extensions, unless the function is one the reading lists as `absent`; element 0 is no builtin, and an element that is not one name is an error. The engines index these arrays by builtin number: QuakeSpasm's `PR_ExecuteProgram` (`pr_exec.c`, at the pinned commit) runs `int i = -newf->first_statement; if (i >= pr_numbuiltins) PR_RunError("Bad builtin call number %d", i); pr_builtins[i]();`, and its `PF_Fixme` is `PR_RunError ("unimplemented builtin");`. `quakespasm` is read for server QuakeC from `pr_builtin`, and `vkquake` for server QuakeC from `pr_ssqcbuiltins` and for client QuakeC from `pr_csqcbuiltins`, each with `PF_Fixme` absent; vkQuake's `PF_NoCSQC` and `PF_CSQCToDo` are macros for `PF_Fixme` there.

A reading with a `name` column and no `target` column reads an array of rows. A row's name is its string literals, joined as C joins them, and must be a QuakeC name; a row whose name is `NULL` ends the list. A reading with a `function` column takes no builtin from a row whose function is missing or listed as `absent`. A `number` of at least 1 is the key number; 0, or no `number` column in the row, keys the builtin by its name, `#0:NAME`, since both engines map a `#0` function to the row of its name (Ironwail's `PR_InitBuiltins`: `if (!strcmp (name, def->name)) { func->first_statement = -def->number;`; vkQuake's `PR_EnableExtensions`: `if (!strcmp (extensionbuiltins[j].name, name))`, then `qcvm->functions[i].first_statement = -extensionbuiltins[j].number;`). A row with a number is keyed by the number alone, as ENGT-2.4 keys a QuakeC declaration, though the same lookup maps a `#0` function of its name to it too. A negative number is an error. The signature is the last line of the `signature` column's type string, split at `\n`, with whitespace collapsed, and must end in `)`; without that column it is empty. The `extension` column, one name with the shape of ENGT-2.6, is the builtin's one extension. When a key repeats, the first row is kept. A row that cannot be read is an error. `ironwail` is read from `pr_builtindefs` for server QuakeC with column 1 (the server function of `PF_SSQC`, `PF_CSQC` and `PF_BOTH`) and for client QuakeC with column 2, number column 3 and extension column 4, `NULL` absent; `vkquake-ext` from `extensionbuiltins` for server QuakeC with column 1 and for client QuakeC with column 2, number column 3 and type string column 4, `NULL` and `PF_NotImplemented` absent, since `PF_NotImplemented` is an empty "placeholder for intentionally not-implemented functions" (`pr_ext.c`).

A reading with a `target` column reads name patches, and needs `name`, `number` and `target` columns and a `target_of` naming an earlier source with a reading of its kind; otherwise it is an error. A row whose `number` is 0 says the engine gives the `#0` function of its name the builtin `#N` of its `target`, written `-N`: it is the builtin with key `#0:NAME`, with the signature and extensions of `#N` in the `target_of` reading, and no builtin when that reading lacks `#N`. A row with any other `number` renumbers a numbered builtin and gives no key; a `target` that is not a negative number is an error. `quakespasm-rerelease` is read for server QuakeC from `exbuiltins`, with name column 0, number column 1, target column 2 and `target_of` `quakespasm`, as QuakeSpasm's `PR_PatchRereleaseBuiltins` (`pr_edict.c`) applies them: `f = ED_FindFunction (ex->name); if (f && f->first_statement == ex->first_statement) f->first_statement = ex->patch_statement;`. So `ex_bprint` is `#23`, and `ex_draw_point` to `ex_draw_cylinder`, patched to the `PF_Fixme` slots 81 to 89, are no builtin.

A C reading's extension names are the string in the first column of each row of its `extension_array`, each kept once in file order; a row whose first column is not a string with the shape of ENGT-2.6 is an error. A C reading without an `extension_array` has no extension names. `vkquake-ext` takes both readings' extension names from `qcextensions`.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it gave QuakeSpasm id's table alone and Ironwail and vkQuake id's and the rerelease's builtins, but ADR-0016 made their own tables fact sources; replaced by ENGT-3.9.

KEX's table is exactly what the rerelease `defs.qc` declares, so it has no number 23, 24 or 73: the rerelease declares `bprint`, `sprint` and `centerprint` as `#0:ex_bprint`, `#0:ex_sprint` and `#0:ex_centerprint` instead, and is silent on the numbers.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it gave vkQuake no extension names, but ADR-0016 made its `qcextensions` list a fact source; replaced by ENGT-3.10.

Each engine has a display name (`Vanilla`, `QuakeSpasm`, `Ironwail`, `vkQuake`, `FTEQW`, `DarkPlaces`, `KEX`) and an id (`vanilla`, `quakespasm`, `ironwail`, `vkquake`, `fteqw`, `darkplaces`, `kex`); reading any other id gives no engine.
A project file's target (PRJ-2.9) selects an engine: `quake` is Vanilla, `rerelease` KEX, `fte` FTEQW and `dp` DarkPlaces.
The targets `quakespasm`, `ironwail` and `vkquake` (PRJ-2.9) select QuakeSpasm, Ironwail and vkQuake, so every engine of ENGT-3.9 is the engine of some target.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it gave only FTEQW client and menu QuakeC tables, but ADR-0015 made DarkPlaces' `csprogsdefs.qc` and `menudefs.qc` fact sources; replaced by ENGT-3.8.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it gave only FTEQW and DarkPlaces client QuakeC tables, but ADR-0016 made Ironwail's and vkQuake's client builtins fact sources; replaced by ENGT-3.11.

There are seven engines, in this order: Vanilla (id's engine), QuakeSpasm, Ironwail, vkQuake, FTEQW, DarkPlaces and KEX (the 2021 rerelease). Each engine's server QuakeC table is the union of these layers, the first layer that has a key giving its entry: Vanilla, id's table (BUILTIN-5); QuakeSpasm, id's table, then the `quakespasm` builtins, then the `quakespasm-rerelease` names; Ironwail, id's table and then the `ironwail` server builtins; vkQuake, the `vkquake-ext` server builtins, then id's table, then the `vkquake` server builtins; FTEQW, the `fteqw` builtins; DarkPlaces, id's table and then the `darkplaces` builtins; KEX, the `rerelease` builtins alone. id's layer gives id's names and prototypes for its numbers, and adds no key to the QuakeSpasm lineage, whose own tables have every number of id's. vkQuake's extension builtins come first because its `PR_EnableExtensions` (`pr_ext.c`) puts them in place of the array's, `if (num && extensionbuiltins[i].ssqcfunc && qcvm->builtins[num] != PF_Fixme) qcvm->builtins[num] = extensionbuiltins[i].ssqcfunc;`, and its `PF_Fixme` runs one for a `PF_Fixme` slot (`qcvm->builtins[binum] = bi;`): so vkQuake's `#51` is `vectoangles2` and its `#80` `infokey`.

The server QuakeC extension names are: FTEQW's the `fteqw` file's, DarkPlaces' the `darkplaces` file's, KEX's the `rerelease` file's, which declares none (ENGT-2.6), and vkQuake's the `vkquake-ext` list (ENGT-2.17). Vanilla, QuakeSpasm and Ironwail have none: no table of their sources lists extension names.

The tables and extension names of ENGT-3.9 and ENGT-3.10 are those for server QuakeC. FTEQW also has a client QuakeC table, the `fteqw` builtins of its `csqc` reading (ENGT-2.10), and a menu QuakeC table, those of its `menuqc` reading. DarkPlaces also has a client QuakeC table, the `darkplaces-client` builtins, and a menu QuakeC table, the `darkplaces-menu` builtins, with no layer of id's table under either, since each file declares the builtins of its kind from `#1`. Ironwail has a client QuakeC table, the `ironwail` client builtins, and vkQuake one made of the `vkquake-ext` client builtins and then the `vkquake` client builtins, with no layer of id's table under either, since each source says which builtins its client QuakeC has. Each table has its reading's extension names. No other engine has a client or menu QuakeC table, since no fact source gives one. A builtin number can mean a different builtin in each kind: in `fteqw`, `#5` is `lightstylestatic` for server and `bprint` for menu QuakeC, and in DarkPlaces `#1` is `makevectors` for client and `checkextension` for menu QuakeC.

In a module checked against a target engine, a call `f(...)` whose callee is a name that resolves (QC-12.5) to a global function declared with a builtin number `#N` (QC-13.3) that the engine's table lacks is warning `W0311` (QCD-7.17) at the callee's name, with the message `NAME is builtin #N, which ENGINE does not have`, `ENGINE` being the display name. When an engine's table has `#N` with extensions, the first such engine in the order of ENGT-3.9 adds them: ` (EXT, EXT)`.
There is no `W0311` when the engine has `#N`, for a call of a name that is not a builtin, for a use of a builtin that is not a call's callee, or for a builtin that is declared and never called.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-19: it read every builtin number as a decimal literal, but under an FTEQCC dialect FTEQCC reads `#0x10` as 16 and `#010` as 8; replaced by ENGT-4.10 and ENGT-4.11.
`W0311` is a warning: it never stops a build or changes the emitted progs (QCD-7).
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-93): it took a name's number from the withdrawn ENGT-4.10; replaced by ENGT-4.17, which takes it from ENGT-4.12.
**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20 (P2-93): it keyed `#N:NAME` by its number as the withdrawn ENGT-4.10 read it; replaced by ENGT-4.18, which reads it as ENGT-4.12 does.

Under the vanilla dialect, whose `qcc` takes a builtin number greater than 0 and nothing after it (QC-13.3), `#0:NAME` gives no key, so a call of such a declaration is no `W0311`; the parser reports the declaration instead.

A module is checked against its target engine's table for the module's kind (PRJ-3.1, ENGT-3.11), and the extensions of ENGT-4.1 and ENGT-4.17 come from the engines' tables for that kind. A module of a kind its engine has no table for is not checked and has no `W0311`.

The `0` of ENGT-4.17 is any number literal that FTEQCC reads as the value 0, in any of its number forms (FTEF-3.1): `0`, `00`, `.0`, `0.00`, the hex `0x0` and the integer `0i`. FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`) keys a builtin by the value `QCC_PR_LexNumber` gives, not by its spelling: `if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_float && pr_immediate._float == (int)pr_immediate._float) binum = (int)pr_immediate._float; else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_integer) binum = pr_immediate._int;`, then `if (!*fname && QCC_PR_CheckToken (":"))` reads the name; and `QCC_PR_LexNumber` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reads `0x` as base 16 (`if (pr_file_p[0] == '0' && (pr_file_p[1] == 'x' || pr_file_p[1] == 'X')) { ... base = 16;`), so `#0x0:NAME` is `binum` 0 with the name `NAME`, the same as `#0:NAME`. A literal whose value is not 0, such as `0.5` or `0x1`, is no `0` here.

**Withdrawn** 2026-10-20: it read a vanilla builtin number as the decimal literal, but id's `qcc` binds `f->builtin = (int)pr_immediate._float;`, the literal's float value, so `#16777217` is builtin 16777216; replaced by ENGT-4.12.

Under an FTEQCC dialect a builtin number is the value FTEQCC reads from the literal, in any of its number forms (FTEF-3.1), when that value is a whole number of at least 1: `#16`, `#16.0`, the hex `#0x10` and the integer `#16i` are all 16, and `#010`, which FTEQCC reads in base 8, is 8, where the vanilla dialect reads `#010` as 10. FTEQCC's `QCC_PR_ParseInitializerType` (`qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`) takes `binum` from that value, as ENGT-4.9 quotes, and `QCC_PR_LexNumber` (`qcc_pr_lex.c`) reads a leading `0` in base 8: `else if (pr_file_p[0] == '0') { pr_file_p++; if (*pr_file_p >= '0' && *pr_file_p <= '9') QCC_PR_ParseWarning(WARN_OCTAL_IMMEDIATE, "A leading 0 is interpreted as base-8."); base = 8;`. A value that is not whole, such as `1.5`, is FTEQCC's "Bad builtin immediate" and no number here.

A builtin's number is that of the first `#N` initialiser of its name, in compilation order (QC-11.5), `N` being the number the dialect's compiler binds for the literal when it is at least 1: under the vanilla dialect `qcc`'s `(int)` of the literal's float value (QC-13.10), so `#16777217` is 16777216 and `#123456789` is 123456792, and under an FTEQCC dialect FTEQCC's `binum` (ENGT-4.13). A literal that gives no number by these rules, a value outside -2^31 to 2^31 - 1 among them, is no number here and gives no `W0311` (the parser reports it, QCD-3.9).

Under an FTEQCC dialect the number of ENGT-4.11's value is FTEQCC's `binum` (FTE-17.6): `(int)` of a float literal's value, so `#123456789` is 123456792, not the shortest decimal of the float, 123456790; the `int` of an `i` literal, so `#16777217i` is 16777217; and no number for a `u` or `l` literal. A float value outside -2^31 to 2^31 - 1, such as that of `#2147483647`, which is 2^31, is no number (QC-13.10).

Under an FTEQCC dialect a builtin declared `= #"NAME"`, `= :"NAME"` or `= :NAME` (FTE-17.5) is keyed by `NAME` as `#0:NAME` is (ENGT-4.17), since FTEQCC reads the name in place of the number and leaves `binum` 0 (`int binum = 0;` ... `else if (pr_token_type == tt_immediate && pr_immediate_type == type_string) QC_strlcpy(fname, pr_immediate_string, sizeof(fname));`, `qcc_pr_comp.c`, fte-team/fteqw@`f937b9d88f71fc4429db5fe56c6a98d922711b2e`). A call of it whose engine lacks `NAME` is the `W0311` of ENGT-4.17, with the message `FUNC is builtin #0:NAME, which ENGINE does not have`.

Under an FTEQCC dialect a `d` literal (`#287d`, `#287.0d`, `#0437d`) gives no key and no `W0311`: it is a `double`, which FTEQCC binds no number for and reports as "Bad builtin immediate" (`dialect-fteqcc-rerelease.md` FTE-23.3). In hex `d` is a digit, so `#0x11d` is 285.

Under an FTEQCC dialect the `NAME` of ENGT-4.14 is the one FTEQCC reads (`dialect-fteqcc-rerelease.md` FTE-23.5, FTE-23.6): adjacent strings joined, so `= #"ex_" "bprint";` is keyed by `ex_bprint`, the name after `:` when the strings are empty (`= #"":ex_bprint;`), and at most its first 255 bytes.

Under an FTEQCC dialect a builtin may be declared `= #0:NAME` (FTE-17.4), which the engine looks up by `NAME` (ENGT-2.4). A global function whose name has no number by ENGT-4.12 takes as its key the `NAME` of its first such initialiser in compilation order, `0` being any literal whose value is 0 (ENGT-4.9). A call of it, as in ENGT-4.1, whose engine table has no builtin keyed `#0:NAME`, names compared exactly, is `W0311` with the message `FUNC is builtin #0:NAME, which ENGINE does not have`, `FUNC` being the function's name, and the extensions of the first engine, in the order of ENGT-3.9, whose table has `NAME` with some. ENGT-4.2 holds for these keys as for numbers.

An initialiser `#N:NAME` with `N` at least 1 is keyed by its number alone, as in ENGT-4.12, and its name is not read. FTE-17.4 says FTEQCC accepts the form and is silent on which key an engine uses for it; keying by number is this project's choice, since a number is what a progs carries for every builtin with one.
The input is the bytes before its first NUL byte; anything after it is ignored.
A backslash followed by `n` (0x6E) becomes one newline byte (0x0A).
A backslash followed by any byte other than `n` becomes one backslash, and that byte is dropped. In particular `\\` becomes `\`, `\t` becomes `\` and `\N` becomes `\`.
A backslash that is the last byte of the input stays a backslash.
Every byte that is not part of an escape is copied unchanged, including control bytes and bytes 0x80 to 0xFF.
Escapes do not chain: the input is scanned once, left to right, and the output is never re-scanned. `\\n` becomes `\n` (two bytes, backslash and `n`).
The output is never longer than the input.

Command-line options are matched against the arguments after the program name, exactly and case-sensitively (`Q_strcmp`), and the first occurrence wins. An option that takes a value (`-basedir`, `-game`, `-cachedir`) is ignored when it is the last argument.

The base directory is the argument after `-basedir` if there is one; otherwise the host's default, which is the current working directory on Windows (`sys_win.c`) and DOS (`sys_dos.c`) and `.` on Linux (`sys_linux.c`).

If the base directory ends with `/` or `\`, exactly one such character is removed; any others stay. `-basedir ..//base//` gives the game directory `..//base//id1`. An empty base directory stays empty, giving `/id1`.

Adding a game directory `D` puts `D` at the head of the search path, then for N = 0, 1, 2, ... puts the archive `D/pakN.pak` (N in decimal, no padding) at the head, stopping at the first N whose file cannot be opened. The result, from the head, is `D/pakK.pak`, ..., `D/pak1.pak`, `D/pak0.pak`, `D`: a game directory's archives are searched before its loose files, and higher-numbered archives before lower ones.

The archive scan stops at the first missing number: with `pak0.pak` and `pak2.pak` but no `pak1.pak`, `pak2.pak` is never loaded. With no `pak0.pak` the game directory has only its loose files. A missing archive is not an error, and neither is a missing game directory.
An archive that opens but fails to load (PAK-1, PAK-2) is fatal; it is not skipped.

Game directories are added in this order, each in front of the previous ones: `<base>/id1` always; `<base>/rogue` if `-rogue` is given; `<base>/hipnotic` if `-hipnotic` is given; `<base>/<value>` if `-game <value>` is given. The order does not depend on the order of the options on the command line, so with both `-rogue` and `-hipnotic`, `hipnotic` is searched before `rogue`.

The value of `-game` is appended to `<base>/` as given: it is not checked, and it may contain `/` or `..`. `-game` marks the game as modified (FS-4.3). `-game id1` adds `id1` a second time, which changes no lookup result.
The game directory the engine writes to (`com_gamedir`, used by `COM_WriteFile`) is the last directory added by FS-1.7.

`-path` discards the search path built by FS-1 and builds a new one from the arguments that follow it, up to the end or the first argument starting with `+` or `-`. Each is put at the head in turn, so the last one listed is searched first. `-path` with no such argument leaves the search path empty. It does not change the game directory of FS-1.9, and it marks the game as modified (FS-4.3).

A `-path` argument whose extension (FS-2.3) is exactly `pak` is loaded as an archive; if it cannot be opened, the engine stops with the fatal error `Couldn't load packfile: <argument>`. Any other argument is a directory, and it is not checked to exist.

A `-path` argument's extension is the text after the first `.` anywhere in it, at most 7 bytes, compared case-sensitively. So `mod/pak0.pak` is an archive, but `./id1/pak0.pak` (extension `/id1/pa`) and `id1/PAK1.PAK` (extension `PAK`) are directories.
With `-proghack`, a lookup of exactly `progs.dat` starts at the second element of the search path instead of the first. No other name is affected.

QuakeC Studio does not implement `-cachedir` (a deliberate divergence). In id's engine it copies loose files from the search path into a local cache directory and reads the copy; it is off unless asked for on every platform (`sys_win.c` sets `parms.cachedir = NULL`, and `sys_linux.c` has "caching is disabled by default, use -cachedir to enable"), and it exists to speed up installs on network drives, which is not a property of game data.
A lookup returns the file from the first element of the search path, from the head, that has it. Elements after that one are not consulted, and nothing is merged across elements.
An archive element has a name if one of its entries matches by PAK-3.1.
A directory element has a name if the file `<directory>/<name>` exists and can be opened for reading. The name is joined with a single `/` and not otherwise changed.

In the shareware game (FS-4.2), directory elements are skipped for any name that contains `/` or `\`; archive elements are not affected. A loose `progs.dat` is still found; a loose `maps/start.bsp` is not.
A name found nowhere is not an error at this level: the lookup reports no file, and the caller decides (`COM_LoadFile` returns `NULL`).

A found file's size is the entry's `filelen` for an archive, or the file's length for a directory. `COM_LoadFile` returns its bytes followed by one NUL byte that is not counted in the size, so text files can be parsed as C strings.

Names in directory elements, the archive names of FS-1.4 and the game directory names of FS-1.7 are matched ASCII case-insensitively on every OS. id's code leaves this to the host filesystem, so the answer differs by platform; this spec fixes the answer of the DOS and Windows reference builds, whose filesystems ignore case, so that an install copied from a CD (`ID1/PAK0.PAK`) or a mod made on Windows behaves the same on macOS and Linux. Archive entries stay case-sensitive (PAK-3.1).

A name that is absolute (starts with `/` or `\`, or a drive letter and `:`), or that has a `..` path component, never matches a directory element (a deliberate divergence). id's code joins it unchanged, so it can read files outside the game directory; QuakeC Studio confines reads to the install. Such a name still matches an archive entry with exactly that name (PAK-3.1).
